research.area: authentication and environments (Kalshi Trade API v2, verified 2026-10-05)

facts.fact: Every authenticated REST request carries three headers. KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY holds the API Key ID, a UUID string such as a952bcbe-ec3b-4b5b-b8f9-11dae589608c. KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP holds the current Unix time in MILLISECONDS as a decimal string, such as 1703123456789 (13 digits). KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE holds a standard base64 string.
facts.quote:
| `KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY` | Your API Key ID | `a952bcbe-ec3b-4b5b-b8f9-11dae589608c` |
| `KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP` | Current time in milliseconds | `1703123456789` |
| `KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE` | Request signature (see below) | `base64_encoded_signature` |

facts.fact: The pre-sign text is the plain concatenation timestamp_ms + HTTP_METHOD + path, with no separators and the method in uppercase (the official SDK calls method.upper()). Example: 1703123456789GET/trade-api/v2/portfolio/balance. Only those three parts are signed. The JSON request body is NOT part of the signature.
facts.quote: Create a message string: Concatenate `timestamp + HTTP_METHOD + path` ... Example: `1703123456789GET/trade-api/v2/portfolio/balance` ... The signature is the base64 encoding of the signed concatenation of the timestamp, the HTTP method and the path.

facts.fact: Sign the full URL path from the API root. This INCLUDES the /trade-api/v2 prefix and EXCLUDES the hostname and the query string. The signed path is the same on every host (external-api, api.elections, demo). Example: for DELETE https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders/abc?market_ticker=X, sign '/trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders/abc'.
facts.quote: The host does not change the signature payload. Sign the full request path from the API root, without query parameters. ... sign: /trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders ... not the hostname and not the query string.

facts.fact: Strip '?' and everything after it before signing.
facts.quote: When signing requests, use the path **without query parameters**. For example, if your request is to `/trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders?limit=5`, sign only `/trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders` (strip the `?` and everything after it).

facts.fact: RSA keys (2048-bit) sign with RSA-PSS over SHA-256, using MGF1(SHA-256) and a salt length equal to the digest length, which is 32 bytes. In Python cryptography that is padding.PSS.DIGEST_LENGTH (not MAX_LENGTH). In Node it is crypto.constants.RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_DIGEST. A local offline test with a throwaway key gave a 256-byte signature, which is 344 base64 characters. RSA-PSS signatures are randomized, so they differ on every call.
facts.quote: Ed25519 keys sign the string directly; RSA keys use RSA-PSS with SHA-256 (MGF1 with SHA-256, salt length equal to the digest length).

facts.fact: Ed25519 keys (RFC 8032) sign the raw UTF-8 pre-sign text directly, with no pre-hash. Signatures are 64 bytes, which is 88 base64 characters, and they are deterministic (verified locally with a throwaway key). Kalshi picks the verification algorithm from the registered public key. Headers, pre-sign text, permissions and errors are the same for both key types.
facts.quote: Headers, pre-sign text, permissions and errors are identical for both types. Kalshi selects the verification algorithm from the registered public key; sign with the algorithm that matches your key.

facts.fact: The signature is encoded with standard base64 (Python base64.b64encode(...).decode('utf-8')), not URL-safe base64.
facts.quote: return base64.b64encode(signature).decode('utf-8')

facts.fact: Do not infer the key type from the PEM header. Parse the key with serialization.load_pem_private_key, then branch on isinstance(key, Ed25519PrivateKey). PKCS#8 RSA keys also start with BEGIN PRIVATE KEY (confirmed locally).
facts.quote: The PEM header does not identify the key type: PKCS#8 RSA keys, including `openssl genpkey` output, also begin with `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`. Determine the type from the parsed key, as the samples below do.

facts.fact: The WebSocket connection itself needs authentication, even for public channels. Send the same three KALSHI-ACCESS-* headers on the handshake, and sign timestamp + 'GET' + '/trade-api/ws/v2'.
facts.quote: timestamp + "GET" + "/trade-api/ws/v2"

facts.fact: These are the official troubleshooting rows: 401 means a wrong key ID or key, or the wrong algorithm. A signature error usually means the timestamp was sent in seconds instead of milliseconds. 'Path not found' means a double /trade-api/v2 prefix. Another failure is signing the query string.
facts.quote:
| 401 Unauthorized | Check the API Key ID and private key path, and sign with the algorithm of the parsed key (the PEM header alone does not tell you which) |
| Signature error | Ensure timestamp is in milliseconds (not seconds) |
| Path not found | If your `BASE_URL` already ends with `/trade-api/v2`, pass only the endpoint path to the helper (e.g. `/portfolio/balance`, not `/trade-api/v2/portfolio/balance`) so the request URL is not double-prefixed |

facts.fact: The allowed clock skew for the REST/WebSocket KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP is NOT documented anywhere in docs.kalshi.com, the OpenAPI spec or the changelog. Only FIX documents a window (30 s for SendingTime). Keep the clock NTP-synced and generate a fresh timestamp and signature for every request and retry.
facts.quote: SendingTime must be within 30 seconds of the server's current time, or the message will be rejected with `SessionRejectReason<373>=10`. (FIX only)

facts.fact: Requests to collection paths with a trailing slash get a 301 redirect to the path without it. A redirect changes the signed path. Never add trailing slashes, and do not auto-follow redirects on authenticated calls.
facts.quote: Requests with trailing slashes (e.g., `/milestones/`) will now receive a 301 redirect to the version without the trailing slash

facts.fact: The official kalshi_python_sync 3.31.0 (PyPI, 2026-09-29) signs timestamp_str + method.upper() + urlparse(full_url).path, so the path includes /trade-api/v2 and drops the query. It accepts both RSA and Ed25519 keys. Its DEFAULT host is PRODUCTION (https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2) and it requires Python >=3.13. The project .venv is Python 3.12.10 and has no cryptography package installed. The old kalshi-python package is deprecated, and the docs warn the SDKs 'may lag the API'.
facts.quote: self._base_path = "https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2" if host is None else host  /  Requires-Python: >=3.13

facts.fact: github.com/Kalshi/kalshi-starter-code-python, last pushed 2025-03-07, is the only public official example repo. It is RSA-only (sign_pss_text) and uses the older shared hosts (https://demo-api.kalshi.co and https://api.elections.kalshi.com). It keeps separate DEMO_KEYID/DEMO_KEYFILE and PROD_KEYID/PROD_KEYFILE variables and defaults to Environment.DEMO. It strips the query before signing and sleeps 100 ms between calls. The SDK source repo Kalshi/exchange-infra is private (GitHub API returns 404).
facts.quote: msg_string = timestamp_str + method + path_parts[0]

facts.topic: API keys: where to create in the UI
facts.fact: Keys are created in the web app under Profile Settings at https://kalshi.com/account/profile, in the 'API Keys' section, with the 'Create New API Key' button. The quick start describes the same path as Account & security -> API Keys -> Create Key. The process is the same on demo (demo.kalshi.co) with a separate demo login. The exact demo URL path is not stated.
facts.quote: In the "Profile Settings" page [https://kalshi.com/account/profile](https://kalshi.com/account/profile), locate the "API Keys" section. Click on the "Create New API Key" button to generate a key pair. Ed25519 is selected by default; choose RSA if your client supports only RSA-PSS. ... This process is the same for the demo or production environment.

facts.topic: API keys: types and PEM formats
facts.fact: There are two key types. Ed25519 (recommended, and the web-app default since 2026-10-01) comes as a PKCS#8 PEM ('-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----'). RSA 2048-bit comes as a PKCS#1 PEM ('-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----'). The API endpoint POST /api_keys/generate still defaults key_type to 'rsa' (enum: rsa, ed25519). The official SDKs need version 3.31.0 or later for Ed25519; RSA works in every version. A self-registered public key must be PEM '-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----'.
facts.quote: | **Ed25519** (recommended) | Ed25519 (RFC 8032) over the pre-sign text | `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` (PKCS#8) | ... | **RSA** (2048-bit) | RSA-PSS with SHA-256 over the pre-sign text | `-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----` (PKCS#1) | Clients limited to RSA-PSS, including SDK versions before 3.31.0 |

facts.fact: The private key is shown once and also downloaded as a .txt file. Kalshi does not store it. The Key ID (a UUID) is displayed on screen. The sample loader passes password=None, and you may encrypt the PEM locally and pass the password instead. Sub-users (Team Members) cannot create or manage keys; only the account owner can.
facts.quote: **Important**: For security reasons, the private key will not be stored by our service, and you will not be able to retrieve it again once this page is closed. ... The key will also be downloaded as txt file with the name provided.

facts.fact: In the web app any user can paste a PEM public key generated with openssl. Through the API, POST /trade-api/v2/api_keys (own public key) is tier-gated: it returns 403 'insufficient API usage level' below Premier or Market Maker. POST /trade-api/v2/api_keys/generate (Kalshi generates the pair) has no tier gate documented.
facts.quote: This endpoint allows users with Premier or Market Maker API usage levels to create API keys by providing their own RSA or Ed25519 public key in PEM format.

facts.fact: The ApiKeyScope enum is, verbatim: read, write, read::block_trade_accept, read::portfolio_balance, write::trade, write::transfer, write::fcm_risk, write::block_trade_accept. If scopes are omitted, the key gets full access [read, write], and write includes transfers. If 'write' is requested, 'read' must also be included. Child scopes can be granted without the parent. A read-only key is ["read"]. A key that can trade but cannot move money is ["read","write::trade"]: write::trade covers order, order-group and RFQ/quote writes without transfer-write access. Read-only scopes have existed since 2025-12-18, write::transfer since 2026-06-02 and write::trade since 2026-06-30. GET /api_keys returns each key's scopes.
facts.quote: List of scopes to grant to the API key. If the broad `write` parent scope is included, `read` must also be included. Child scopes may be granted without the broad parent scope. Defaults to full access (`read`, `write`) if not provided.

facts.topic: API keys: scope selection in the web UI
facts.fact: The docs do not say whether the web 'Create New API Key' dialog lets you choose scopes or a subaccount restriction. Both are documented only as API request fields ('scopes', 'subaccount') on POST /api_keys and POST /api_keys/generate. One documented path to a narrow key is to create a key in the UI, call generate with scopes, then DELETE the broad key. That needs a write call to an API-key endpoint, so it is the user's decision.

The integer field 'subaccount' (0-63) locks a key to one subaccount. Such a key can read and trade only there. It cannot transfer funds, create subaccounts or manage API keys. Other endpoints return 403 with the message below. Numbered subaccounts need the Advanced API tier or above. The docs suggest this pattern to give a bot a fixed amount of capital.
facts.quote: Endpoints outside its allowed set return `403 this API key is restricted to a single sub-account and cannot access this endpoint`. ... | Give a bot or API trader a fixed amount of capital | A subaccount funded with that amount, plus an API key restricted to it |

facts.fact: No expiry or TTL for API keys is documented. A key stays valid until it is deleted with DELETE /trade-api/v2/api_keys/{api_key} (returns 204; permanent). The only rotation guidance is 'Rotate API keys regularly'. Rotation means creating a new key, switching to it, then deleting the old one. FIX allows one active connection per API key.
facts.quote: This endpoint permanently deletes an API key. Once deleted, the key can no longer be used for authentication. This action cannot be undone.

facts.fact: GET /api_keys returns api_key_region_expiration_ts, an integer Unix timestamp in SECONDS (for example 1791224100) for when the account's location attestation for API-key requests expires. It is absent if the account never attested. After it passes, keys cannot trade Sports, Elections and Entertainment markets. The changelog names only those three categories. How to attest is not documented. Crypto, weather and FX markets are not listed, which suggests (but does not confirm) they are unaffected.
facts.quote: Once this date has passed, API keys are not valid for trading Sports, Elections, and Entertainment markets. The field is absent when the account has never attested.

facts.fact: Production REST: https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2 is recommended; https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2 is also supported. Production WebSocket: wss://external-api-ws.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2 is recommended; wss://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2 is also supported. Both hosts serve every market. The external-api hosts were added on 2026-05-07. Public market-data GETs work without auth on external-api.kalshi.com (HTTP 200 observed 2026-10-05).
facts.quote: | Production | `https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2` | `https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2` |

facts.fact: Demo (fake money) is still offered in Oct 2026. Web app: https://demo.kalshi.co/ (sign-up at https://demo.kalshi.co/sign-up). The .com spelling is not a valid Kalshi domain. Demo REST: https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 (recommended) or https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2. Demo WebSocket: wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2 or wss://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2.
facts.quote:
| REST Trade API | `https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2` | `https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2` |
| WebSocket API | `wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2` | `wss://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2` |

facts.fact: On 2026-10-05 at 17:57 UTC, unauthenticated GET /trade-api/v2/markets?limit=1 returned HTTP 200 on both external-api.demo.kalshi.co and demo-api.kalshi.co, with markets created that same minute. GET /series/KXBTC15M on demo also returned 200.
facts.quote: "created_time":"2026-10-05T17:57:27.286984Z" (demo /markets response)

facts.topic: environments: demo needs separate account and keys
facts.fact: Demo uses a separate account (the same email may be reused) and separate API keys. Demo keys work only on demo hosts and production keys only on production hosts. Use separate env vars, for example the project's KALSHI_ENV plus a key ID and key path per environment.
facts.quote: Credentials are not shared between environments, so demo API keys only work against demo endpoints and production API keys only work against production endpoints.

facts.topic: environments: demo account setup and funding
facts.fact: Demo sign-up accepts mock personal details (fake name, address, SSN). Demo accounts start with NO funds. Mock funds come from test payment methods: test debit cards (for example Visa Debit 4000 0566 5566 5556, any future expiry, any 3-digit CVV), Plaid sandbox (user_good / pass_good) or test USDC on Solana Devnet from faucet.circle.com. Demo is sometimes down ('under construction') for up to about 24 h. Nothing in demo affects production.
facts.quote: You can just use mock information when signing up (fake name, address, Social Security Number, etc.), no real personal details needed. ... Your demo account does not come with funds preloaded ... Sometimes, the Demo environment may be under construction.

facts.fact: The docs warn that demo prices and behavior may not match real markets. Observed 2026-10-05 17:57 UTC: demo KXBTC15M-26OCT051400-00 had the same ticker, open/close times, floor_strike 85319.11, price_level_structure 'tapered_deci_cent' and exchange_index 2 as production. Its book was almost empty: yes_bid_dollars "0.0100" x yes_bid_size_fp "8.00", yes_ask_dollars "1.0000" x "0.00", volume_fp "302.88". Production had yes_bid "0.9790" x "955.77", yes_ask "0.9800" x "5484.06" and volume_fp "2395135.67". The demo status=open filter also returned a stale May-2026 market (status "closed", no strike). Conclusion: demo can test auth, placing, cancelling, amending and order state, but not realistic fills or edge.
facts.quote: The price and behavior of markets in the demo environment may not be reflective of those in real markets.

facts.fact: Matching runs on shards. Crypto and Commodities series live on shard (exchange_index) 2; KXBTC15M showed exchange_index 2 on both production and demo. Collateral must already sit on the target shard before an API order. App and web orders move funds between shards automatically; the docs describe no such auto-transfer for API orders. Funds can be moved with the UI at https://kalshi.com/account/exchange-indexes, POST /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfer, or opt-in target_balance_allocation auto-rebalancing (every 10 s). GET /portfolio/balance has a per-shard balance_breakdown.
facts.quote: Kalshi's collateralization checks run within the matching engine. Programmatic traders must preallocate collateral on a given exchange shard before order placement.

facts.fact: Cancel V2 (DELETE /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}) takes exchange_index and market_ticker as QUERY parameters. These are not signed, because the query is stripped before signing. With neither set, the cancel goes to shard 0. Cancelling a shard-2 BTC order by order_id alone therefore misses the order. Always pass market_ticker or exchange_index=2.
facts.quote: Exchange shard index. If omitted, auto-routes when market_ticker is provided; otherwise defaults to 0. Use -1 to require auto-routing. ... Auto-routing requires `market_ticker`. An `order_id` alone cannot identify the exchange shard.

facts.fact: GET /portfolio/balance returns these fields. 'balance' is an int64 in CENTS (2500 = $25.00) and truncates sub-cent amounts. 'balance_dollars' is a fixed-point dollar STRING such as "25.0000" (responses can have up to 6 decimals). 'portfolio_value' is an int64 in CENTS. 'balance_breakdown' is a list of {exchange_index int, balance dollar string}. 'updated_ts' is a Unix timestamp whose unit is not stated. Direct-member balances are kept to $0.0001 (0.01c) precision. The endpoint also accepts keys that only have the read::portfolio_balance scope.
facts.quote: `GET /portfolio/balance` returns `balance_dollars`, the member's available balance as a fixed-point dollar string, alongside the existing integer-cent `balance` field. ... The legacy `balance` field truncates any sub-cent amount, so use `balance_dollars` for exact values.

facts.fact: The two transfer endpoints use different units. POST /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfer (moving funds between shards) takes 'amount' as an int64 in CENTICENTS, so $5.00 = 50000, plus source_exchange_shard and destination_exchange_shard as ints with default 0. POST /portfolio/subaccounts/transfer takes 'amount_cents' as an int64 in CENTS, so $5.00 = 500.
facts.quote: amount: type: integer, format: int64, description: The amount to transfer in centicents  /  amount_cents: type: integer, format: int64, description: Amount to transfer in cents.

facts.fact: Public market objects return prices as 4-decimal dollar strings (for example yes_bid_dollars "0.9790" and notional_value_dollars "1.0000"). Sizes, volumes and open interest are 2-decimal fixed-point contract strings (yes_bid_size_fp "955.77", volume_fp "2395135.67"). GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook returns {"orderbook_fp":{"yes_dollars":[["0.2000","4618.28"],...],"no_dollars":[...]}}, where each level is [price in dollars, size in contracts].

Every Thursday from 3:00 to 5:00 AM ET there is a trading pause. Orders cannot be placed or amended, but they can be cancelled, and resting orders stay unless cancel_order_on_pause=true was set. Expect disconnects. The public GET /exchange/status returns exchange_active and trading_active, including per-exchange_index values.
facts.quote: Every **Thursday from 3:00 AM to 5:00 AM ET**, Kalshi runs scheduled maintenance. During this window, a **trading pause** is in effect.

facts.fact: The legacy order-mutation endpoints under /trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders are deprecated. They now cost 10x the V2 tokens (create 100 tokens) and, once deprecated, return the message below. Sign and send orders at /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders (V2).
facts.quote: Once deprecated, calls to these endpoints will return `Please switch to the V2 endpoints` with a link to the V2 order API reference.

facts.fact: Every AUTHENTICATED request spends tokens from a per-account token bucket. There are two independent buckets, Read and Write. Most endpoints cost 10 tokens by default. The Write bucket covers order placement, amends, cancels, order groups, RFQ quotes and block-trade accepts; everything else, including all GETs, uses Read. REST and FIX share the same buckets. The sustained rate for an endpoint is budget / cost.
facts.quote: Every authenticated request costs **tokens**. Your tier sets your **budget**: the rate, in tokens per second, at which your balance refills. Your sustained rate for an endpoint is `budget ÷ cost`. Most requests cost the default of **10 tokens**.

facts.topic: rate limits: tiers (tokens per second, Read / Write)
facts.fact: Budgets in tokens per second, Read / Write: Basic 200 / 100, Advanced 300 / 300, Expert 600 / 600, Premier 1,200 / 1,200, Paragon 2,400 / 2,400, Prime 4,800 / 4,800, Prestige 12,000 / 9,600. Premier and above were raised 20% on 2026-09-24. At Basic with 10-token calls that is about 20 GETs/s and 10 order creates/s.
facts.quote: Basic 200 100 | Advanced 300 300 | Expert 600 600 | Premier 1,200 1,200 | Paragon 2,400 2,400 | Prime 4,800 4,800 | Prestige 12,000 9,600 (Tier | Read budget | Write budget)

facts.fact: Basic and Advanced Read buckets, and Write buckets above Basic, hold 3 seconds of budget. Basic Write holds only 1 second (100 tokens), so a Basic account can burst at most 10 creates and banks nothing. Advanced Write holds 900 tokens. A whole batch must fit in the bucket, which implies a Basic batch create is capped at 10 orders (inferred). The OpenAPI BucketLimit text says non-Basic write buckets hold 'two seconds', which conflicts with the guide's three. GET /account/limits (authenticated) returns the account's real refill_rate and bucket_capacity.
facts.quote: Basic and Advanced Predictions Read buckets, and Write buckets above the Basic tier, hold up to **three seconds of budget**. ... Predictions Read buckets above Advanced, Perps Read buckets, and Basic-tier Write buckets hold one second of budget.

facts.fact: Create Order V2 costs the default 10 tokens. Cancel Order V2 costs 2. Batch create costs 10 per order, and batch cancel 2 per order (25 orders = 50). Cancel-all costs the same as one cancel. POST /account/api_usage_level/upgrade costs 30 Write tokens. GET /account/endpoint_costs lists non-default costs, but it was not called because it sits under /account.
facts.quote: **Rate limit:** 2 tokens per request. (Cancel Order V2)  /  **Rate limit:** 10 tokens per order in the batch — billed per item, so total cost for a batch of N orders is N × 10. (Batch Create Orders V2)

facts.fact: A single REST order write with exchange_index >= 1 is billed to that shard's Write bucket. Shard 0 bills the unscoped bucket. Auto-routed writes (exchange_index -1, or omitted with market_ticker) are billed to EVERY shard's Write bucket and add latency. Batch writes always bill the unscoped bucket. Read budgets are not split by shard.
facts.quote: Auto-routed traffic (`exchange_index: -1`, or omitted when `market_ticker` is provided) is billed to every shard's Write bucket.

facts.fact: A rate-limited request gets HTTP 429 with no Retry-After or X-RateLimit-* headers. There is no penalty or cooldown: the next request succeeds once the bucket has refilled enough to cover its cost. Use exponential backoff. A batch that does not fit is rejected in full.
facts.quote: A rate-limited request returns `429 Too Many Requests` with the body: {"error": "too many requests"} 429 responses do not currently include `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-*` headers. There is no penalty or cooldown. ... Apply exponential backoff on 429.

facts.topic: rate limits: 429 observed on public endpoint
facts.fact: On 2026-10-05 at 17:57:28 UTC, an UNAUTHENTICATED GET to https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/markets?limit=1 returned 429. The body was nested, unlike the flat body in the docs, and there was no Retry-After or X-RateLimit header. About 1 s later the same GET to external-api.kalshi.com returned 200. Limits for public endpoints are undocumented. The likely cause is this machine's background collectors using the shared host, but that is a guess. Detect 429 by status code and accept both body shapes.
facts.quote: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests ... {"error":{"code":"too_many_requests","message":"too many requests"}}

facts.fact: ErrorResponse has three fields: code (string), message (string) and details (string, optional). In practice it comes wrapped under 'error'. Branch on 'code'; the 'service' field was removed on 2026-08-06.
facts.quote: Branch on `code` instead, which is present on every error response.

facts.fact: Basic comes with signup. Advanced is self-serve through POST /trade-api/v2/account/api_usage_level/upgrade. It requires at least 1 of the last 100 Predictions orders to have been placed via the API, and it is a permanent grant; the call returns 403 if the requirement is not met. Advanced is also required for subaccounts. Expert through Prestige are earned automatically from 30-day volume share (Expert: 0.075% to earn, 0.05% to keep) and granted for 30 days. GET /account/limits returns usage_tier, read and write {refill_rate, bucket_capacity} and grants[] with expires_ts in Unix seconds.
facts.quote: Grants a permanent Advanced API usage-level grant. Currently only the Predictions exchange instance is supported. Criteria: at least 1 of the user's last 100 Predictions orders was created via API.

facts.fact: The number of WebSocket connections per user depends on usage tier, starting from a default of 200. Orderbook subscriptions are capped at 500k markets per session and 10k commands per second.
facts.quote: WebSocket connections per user are limited by usage tier. The default limit begins at 200 and increases based on API usage tier.

facts.fact: Public GET /markets on production external-api returned 'cache-control: public, max-age=15' and 'x-kalshi-cache-hits: 1'; demo returned max-age=5. GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook returned no cache-control header. Market-list prices may therefore be up to about 15 s old. Use the orderbook endpoint or WebSocket for prices checked right before an order. This caching is not in the docs.
facts.quote:
cache-control: public, max-age=15
x-kalshi-cache-hits: 1

facts.fact: Using the API binds the user to Kalshi's Developer Agreement. The page could not be read because kalshi.com returned HTTP 429 to both curl and WebFetch.
facts.quote: By continuing to use or access Kalshi's API, you are agreeing to be bound to our Developer Agreement

facts.fact: Raw doc markdown, the OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specs, public API responses with headers, the starter code, the unpacked SDK wheel and the offline signing self-test are cached in C:\Users\Jarvis\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-Jarvis-Documents-Kalshi-PM\5805aad9-f58e-4981-a45a-fa35e3d20f67\scratchpad\kdocs_auth (and ...\scratchpad\kdocs for doc pages). Only public unauthenticated GETs were sent: /markets, /series/KXBTC15M and one orderbook, on production and demo. No authenticated, account, portfolio, order or API-key endpoint was called.

code_examples.purpose: Official Python: load a PEM key, sign with Ed25519 or RSA-PSS, and send a signed GET. These are three consecutive verbatim blocks from the API Keys page.
code_examples.code:
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from cryptography.hazmat.backends import default_backend

def load_private_key_from_file(file_path):
    with open(file_path, "rb") as key_file:
        private_key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(
            key_file.read(),
            password=None,  # or provide a password if your key is encrypted
            backend=default_backend()
        )
    return private_key

import base64
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import padding
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

def sign_text(private_key, text: str) -> str:
    message = text.encode('utf-8')
    if isinstance(private_key, Ed25519PrivateKey):
        # Ed25519 signs the message itself
        signature = private_key.sign(message)
    else:
        # RSA signs with RSA-PSS over SHA-256
        signature = private_key.sign(
            message,
            padding.PSS(
                mgf=padding.MGF1(hashes.SHA256()),
                salt_length=padding.PSS.DIGEST_LENGTH
            ),
            hashes.SHA256()
        )
    return base64.b64encode(signature).decode('utf-8')

import requests
import datetime
import base64
from urllib.parse import urlparse
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization, hashes
from cryptography.hazmat.backends import default_backend
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import padding
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

# Configuration
API_KEY_ID = 'your-api-key-id-here'
PRIVATE_KEY_PATH = 'path/to/your/kalshi-key.key'
BASE_URL = 'https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2'  # or 'https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2' for production

def load_private_key(key_path):
    with open(key_path, "rb") as f:
        return serialization.load_pem_private_key(f.read(), password=None, backend=default_backend())

def create_signature(private_key, timestamp, method, path):
    """Create the request signature with the key's algorithm."""
    # Strip query parameters before signing
    path_without_query = path.split('?')[0]
    message = f"{timestamp}{method}{path_without_query}".encode('utf-8')
    if isinstance(private_key, Ed25519PrivateKey):
        signature = private_key.sign(message)
    else:
        signature = private_key.sign(
            message,
            padding.PSS(mgf=padding.MGF1(hashes.SHA256()), salt_length=padding.PSS.DIGEST_LENGTH),
            hashes.SHA256()
        )
    return base64.b64encode(signature).decode('utf-8')

def get(private_key, api_key_id, path, base_url=BASE_URL):
    """Make an authenticated GET request to the Kalshi API."""
    timestamp = str(int(datetime.datetime.now().timestamp() * 1000))
    # Signing requires the full URL path from root (e.g. /trade-api/v2/portfolio/balance)
    sign_path = urlparse(base_url + path).path
    signature = create_signature(private_key, timestamp, "GET", sign_path)

    headers = {
        'KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY': api_key_id,
        'KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE': signature,
        'KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP': timestamp
    }

    return requests.get(base_url + path, headers=headers)

# Load private key
private_key = load_private_key(PRIVATE_KEY_PATH)

# Get balance
response = get(private_key, API_KEY_ID, "/portfolio/balance")
print(f"Your balance: ${response.json()['balance'] / 100:.2f}")

def post(private_key, api_key_id, path, data, base_url=BASE_URL):
    """Make an authenticated POST request to the Kalshi API."""
    timestamp = str(int(datetime.datetime.now().timestamp() * 1000))
    # Signing requires the full URL path from root (e.g. /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders)

    signature = create_signature(private_key, timestamp, "POST", sign_path)

        'KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE': signature,
        'KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP': timestamp,

checks.claim: The private key is shown once, downloaded as a .txt file, and not stored by Kalshi. The Key ID UUID is shown on screen. password=None in the sample; you can encrypt locally. Only the account owner can create or manage keys; sub-users cannot.
checks.evidence: api_keys: '**Important**: For security reasons, the private key will not be stored by our service, and you will not be able to retrieve it again once this page is closed... The key will also be downloaded as txt file with the name provided.' Quick start: 'Private Key: Downloaded as a PEM text file' and 'API Key ID: Displayed on screen'. The sample has 'password=None,  # or provide a password if your key is encrypted'. sub_users_vs_subaccounts: 'Whatever their permissions, sub-users can't create or manage API keys' and 'Only the account owner can create API keys.' (The SDK cannot load an encrypted PEM; see the SDK check.)

checks.claim: In the web app any user can paste a PEM public key. POST /api_keys (own public key) is limited to Premier/Market Maker (403 'insufficient API usage level'). POST /api_keys/generate has no documented tier gate.
checks.evidence: create-api-key: 'This endpoint allows users with Premier or Market Maker API usage levels to create API keys by providing their own RSA or Ed25519 public key in PEM format.' Its 403 is 'Forbidden - insufficient API usage level, or fcm_subtrader_id from a non-FCM caller'. generate-api-key's only 403 is 'Forbidden - fcm_subtrader_id requires an FCM member caller'. api_keys (web UI): 'Paste the contents of `kalshi.pub` into the public key field. The private key never leaves your system.'

checks.claim: The ApiKeyScope enum is read, write, read::block_trade_accept, read::portfolio_balance, write::trade, write::transfer, write::fcm_risk, write::block_trade_accept. The default is [read, write], and write includes transfers. write requires read. Child scopes can be granted alone. ["read","write::trade"] can trade but cannot transfer. Dates: read 2025-12-18, write::transfer 2026-06-02, write::trade 2026-06-30. GET /api_keys returns scopes.
checks.evidence: openapi ApiKeyScope enum, verbatim: ['read','write','read::block_trade_accept','read::portfolio_balance','write::trade','write::transfer','write::fcm_risk','write::block_trade_accept']. scopes description: 'If the broad `write` parent scope is included, `read` must also be included. Child scopes may be granted without the broad parent scope. Defaults to full access (`read`, `write`) if not provided.' Changelog Dec 18, 2025 (read-only scopes); Jun 2, 2026: '`write` continues to grant all write endpoint groups, including transfer-scoped writes'; Jun 30, 2026: '`write::trade` to grant access to order, order-group, and RFQ/quote write endpoints without granting transfer-write access'. The sub-users table maps Trade to `write::trade` ('Place and cancel orders, including RFQs and quotes') and Transfers to `write::transfer` ('Deposit and withdraw funds and manage payment methods'). The GET /api_keys ApiKey schema requires 'scopes'.

checks.topic: API keys: scope selection in the web UI
checks.claim: The docs do not say whether the web dialog lets you pick scopes or a subaccount lock. Both are documented only as API fields.
checks.evidence: The absence is confirmed: the api_keys page, both quick starts, the changelog and help.kalshi.com/en/articles/13823854-kalshi-api never mention choosing scopes or a subaccount in the dialog. Related: subaccounts page: 'Subaccounts are currently an **API-only** feature — they are not yet supported in the Kalshi web or mobile app', so a subaccount lock almost certainly needs POST /api_keys/generate.

checks.claim: The integer 'subaccount' (0-63) locks a key to one subaccount: it can read and trade only there and cannot transfer, create subaccounts or manage keys. Other endpoints return the 403 below. Numbered subaccounts need Advanced tier or above. The docs suggest this for giving a bot fixed capital.
checks.evidence: GenerateApiKeyRequest.subaccount: 'minimum: 0, maximum: 63 ... A restricted key may only read and trade on that sub-account; it cannot act on other sub-accounts, transfer funds between sub-accounts, or create sub-accounts.' Subaccounts page: 'A restricted key cannot transfer funds, manage subaccounts or API keys' and 'Endpoints outside its allowed set return `403 this API key is restricted to a single sub-account and cannot access this endpoint`'. sub_users table: 'Direct accounts on the Advanced API tier or above'. Goal table: 'Give a bot or API trader a fixed amount of capital | A subaccount funded with that amount, plus an API key restricted to it'.
checks.corrected_fact: Missing nuance: with a restricted key, GET /portfolio/balance omits balance_breakdown ('omitted only when using a subaccount-restricted API key'), so the per-shard check needs ?exchange_index=2. Exchange-sharding FAQ: 'Subaccount balances are local to a specific exchange instance', so a shard-2 bot subaccount must be provisioned and funded with exchange_index=2.

checks.claim: No key TTL is documented; a key is valid until DELETE /trade-api/v2/api_keys/{api_key} (204, permanent). The only guidance is 'Rotate API keys regularly'. FIX allows one connection per key.
checks.evidence: delete-api-key: response '204: API key successfully deleted', and 'This action cannot be undone.' The ApiKey schema has only api_key_id, name, scopes, subaccount and fcm_subtrader_id, with no expiry field. The only rotation text in llms-full.txt is 'Rotate API keys regularly' (WebSocket quick start, Security card). fix/authentication: 'Use one active FIX connection per API key.'

checks.claim: GET /api_keys returns api_key_region_expiration_ts (int, Unix seconds). After it passes, keys cannot trade Sports, Elections and Entertainment. The field is absent if the account never attested. How to attest is undocumented, and crypto is not listed.
checks.evidence: Changelog Aug 16, 2026, verbatim: '`GET /trade-api/v2/api_keys` now returns `api_key_region_expiration_ts`, the unix timestamp (seconds) when your location attestation for API key requests expires. Once this date has passed, API keys are not valid for trading Sports, Elections, and Entertainment markets. The field is absent when the account has never attested.' Schema: 'type: integer, format: int64, nullable: true ... a past value means the attestation has lapsed'. A grep for 'attest' across llms-full.txt and openapi finds no instructions. The example value 1791224100 is illustrative and does not come from the docs.

checks.claim: REST https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2 (recommended) or https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2. WS wss://external-api-ws.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2 (recommended) or wss://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2. All markets on both. external-api added 2026-05-07. Public GETs work without auth.
checks.evidence: api_environments tables, verbatim. Note: 'Despite the `elections` subdomain, the production Trade API provides access to all Kalshi markets'. Changelog May 7, 2026 'Dedicated external Trade API endpoints documented'. The openapi servers list has the same four URLs. Live, unauthenticated, 18:16:34 UTC: GET https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/markets?series_ticker=KXBTC15M&status=open&limit=2 returned 200.

checks.claim: Web https://demo.kalshi.co/ (sign-up /sign-up); .com is not a Kalshi domain. REST https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 or https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2. WS wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2 or wss://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2.
checks.evidence: demo_env table, verbatim. The help article links https://demo.kalshi.co/ and https://demo.kalshi.co/sign-up and says: 'demo.kalshi.co is Kalshi's official Demo trading environment. We understand the .co domain may be confusing, but the .com version is not a valid Kalshi domain.'

checks.claim: Unauthenticated GET /markets?limit=1 returns 200 on both demo hosts with freshly created markets. /series/KXBTC15M on demo returns 200.
checks.evidence: Re-observed independently at 18:16:37 UTC. Both https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2/markets?limit=1 and https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2/markets?limit=1 returned 200 with created_time '2026-10-05T18:16:01.094952Z'. GET /series/KXBTC15M on external-api.demo returned 200 (exchange_index 2). Demo GET /exchange/status returned 200 and lists 'Demo shard 1' and 'Demo shard 2'.

checks.topic: environments: demo needs separate account and keys
checks.claim: Demo is a separate account (the same email may be reused) with separate keys. Demo keys only work on demo hosts and prod keys only on prod hosts.
checks.evidence: api_environments: 'Credentials are not shared between environments, so demo API keys only work against demo endpoints and production API keys only work against production endpoints.' Help article: 'Your demo account credentials are completely separate from your production account credentials' and 'there are no conflicts with using the same email or information between the two environments.' Note: the project's .env.example has one KALSHI_API_KEY_ID / KALSHI_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH pair and 'KALSHI_ENV=prod'.

checks.topic: environments: demo account setup and funding
checks.claim: Mock personal details are accepted. Demo has no preloaded funds. Funding is by test debit card (Visa Debit 4000 0566 5566 5556, any future expiry, any 3-digit CVV), Plaid sandbox user_good/pass_good, or Solana Devnet test USDC from faucet.circle.com. Demo is sometimes down for up to ~24 h and is isolated from production.
checks.evidence: Fresh fetch of the help article (dateModified 2026-09-24T03:28:05Z): 'You can just use mock information when signing up (fake name, address, Social Security Number, etc.)'; 'Your demo account does not come with funds preloaded'; 'Visa Debit 4000 0566 5566 5556'; 'Mastercard Debit 5200 8282 8282 8210'; 'Use any future expiration date and any 3-digit Card Verification Value (CVV)'; Plaid 'user_good' / 'pass_good', phone 415-555-0010, OTP 123456; 'Go to faucet.circle.com, select USDC and the Solana Devnet network'; 'checking back later anytime over the next 24 hours'; 'Nothing you do in the demo environment affects your production account.'

checks.claim: Demo KXBTC15M mirrors production's ticker, times, strike, structure and shard, but its book is nearly empty. status=open also returned a stale May-2026 closed market. Demo can test auth and order mechanics, but not fills or edge.
checks.evidence: The pattern re-observed at 18:16-18:17 UTC (exact numbers are point-in-time). Demo and prod KXBTC15M-26OCT051430-30 both had floor_strike 85432.83, 'tapered_deci_cent' and exchange_index 2. Demo: yes_bid_dollars '0.5200' x yes_bid_size_fp '231.00', yes_ask_dollars '1.0000' x '0.00', volume_fp '1.00'; the demo orderbook was {"orderbook_fp":{"no_dollars":[],"yes_dollars":[["0.0100","1.00"]]}}. Prod: '0.5800' x '3663.93', '0.5900' x '7748.20', volume_fp '209371.47'. Demo status=open also returned KXBTC15M-26MAY050000-00 with status 'closed', no floor_strike and exchange_index 0. demo_env: 'The price and behavior of markets in the demo environment may not be reflective of those in real markets.'

checks.claim: Crypto and Commodities are on shard 2; KXBTC15M has exchange_index 2. Collateral must be on the target shard before an API order. App/web auto-transfer does not apply to API orders. Funds move via the UI, POST /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfer, or opt-in auto-rebalancing (every 10 s). Balance has a per-shard breakdown.
checks.evidence: exchange_sharding: 'Programmatic traders must preallocate collateral on a given exchange shard before order placement.' 'orders placed through the Kalshi App and Web automatically transfer capital between exchange shards as needed'. Shard table: '| 2 | Crypto |' and '| 2 | Commodities |'. 'Every 10 seconds, Kalshi computes...'. UI: https://kalshi.com/account/exchange-indexes. Live: prod and demo /series/KXBTC15M show exchange_index 2, and prod /exchange/status has index 2 'Crypto & Commodities'.
checks.corrected_fact: The shard table only 'determine[s] the shard where new events are created', and 'The `exchange_index` field is the authoritative source of truth'. The stale demo KXBTC15M-26MAY050000-00 reports exchange_index 0. Read exchange_index from each market or order object instead of hardcoding 2 for the series.

checks.claim: Cancel V2 DELETE /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id} takes exchange_index and market_ticker as unsigned QUERY params. With neither, it targets shard 0, so cancelling a shard-2 order by order_id alone misses it. Always pass market_ticker or exchange_index=2.
checks.evidence: cancel-order-v2: exchange_index (in: query) 'If omitted, auto-routes when market_ticker is provided; otherwise defaults to 0. Use -1 to require auto-routing.' Warning: 'Auto-routing requires `market_ticker`. An `order_id` alone cannot identify the exchange shard.' Responses: 200 CancelOrderV2Response {order_id, client_order_id, reduced_by (FixedPointCount, e.g. '10.00'), ts_ms (epoch ms)}, plus 401, 404, 500. Query strings are excluded from the signature (see path rules).
checks.corrected_fact: Pass market_ticker (auto-route; billed to every shard's Write bucket, with extra latency) or the exchange_index read from that order or market object; the Order schema has exchange_index. Do not hardcode 2. A wrong-shard cancel most likely returns 404, which is inferred rather than documented.

checks.claim: GET /portfolio/balance: balance int64 CENTS (sub-cent truncated); balance_dollars fixed-point dollar string (up to 6 dp); portfolio_value int64 cents; balance_breakdown [{exchange_index int, balance dollar string}]; updated_ts unit unstated; $0.0001 direct-member precision; accepts read::portfolio_balance.
checks.evidence: GetBalanceResponse: balance 'integer, int64 ... available balance in cents'; balance_dollars $ref FixedPointDollars ('responses emit up to 6'); portfolio_value 'int64 ... in cents'; updated_ts 'Unix timestamp of the last update to the balance.' (no unit); balance_breakdown items IndexedBalance {exchange_index, balance: FixedPointDollars}. The description says 'also accepts API keys with the 'read::portfolio_balance' scope'. fee_rounding: 'Direct member balances are aligned to `$0.0001` (`0.01c`)'.
checks.corrected_fact: Source slip: the quote 'returns `balance_dollars`... The legacy `balance` field truncates any sub-cent amount' comes from the changelog entry of May 28, 2026, not the get-balance page. Safety nuance: since Aug 20, 2026, 'balance' and 'portfolio_value' include ALL exchange indexes unless ?exchange_index=N is passed. Before a KXBTC15M API order, check balance_breakdown[exchange_index==2].balance or call with ?exchange_index=2.

checks.claim: POST /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfer 'amount' is int64 CENTICENTS ($5.00 = 50000) with source_exchange_shard / destination_exchange_shard defaulting to 0. POST /portfolio/subaccounts/transfer 'amount_cents' is int64 CENTS ($5.00 = 500).
checks.evidence: IntraExchangeInstanceTransferRequest: amount 'int64 ... The amount to transfer in centicents'; source_exchange_shard / destination_exchange_shard 'minimum: 0, maximum: 100, default: 0'. ApplySubaccountTransferRequest: amount_cents 'int64 ... Amount to transfer in cents.' Arithmetic: $1 = 100 cents = 10,000 centicents.
checks.corrected_fact: The research left out required fields. The intra-exchange transfer ALSO requires 'source' and 'destination' (ExchangeInstance enum: 'event_contract' | 'margined'; use event_contract for both). The 200 response means 'Transfer request accepted. The transfer is processed asynchronously.' and returns {transfer_id}; poll GET /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfers/{transfer_id}. 'Cross-exchange-index subaccount transfers run in up to three non-atomic steps.' The subaccount transfer requires client_transfer_id (uuid), from_subaccount, to_subaccount and amount_cents, and a retry with the same client_transfer_id returns 409.

checks.claim: Prices are 4-dp dollar strings and sizes/volume/OI are 2-dp _fp strings. The orderbook is {orderbook_fp:{yes_dollars:[[price,size]...], no_dollars:[...]}}.
checks.corrected_fact: Arrays are sorted ASCENDING and the best bid is the LAST element (guide: 'The **highest** bid (best bid) is the **last** element in each array'). The API reference's 'organized from best to worst prices' is wrong for the live payload. Best YES ask = 1 - last no_dollars price. FixedPointDollars responses may carry up to 6 decimals, so parse with Decimal and never assume exactly 4.

checks.claim: Trading pause every Thursday 3:00-5:00 AM ET: no place or amend, cancel allowed, resting orders stay unless cancel_order_on_pause=true; expect disconnects. Public GET /exchange/status gives exchange_active and trading_active, including per-index values.
checks.evidence: maintenance_and_pauses: 'Every **Thursday from 3:00 AM to 5:00 AM ET**, Kalshi runs scheduled maintenance. During this window, a **trading pause** is in effect.' Table: 'Cancel orders | Yes | No' (Trading Pause | Exchange Pause). 'Clients should be prepared for session disconnections'. Live GET https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/exchange/status returned 200 without auth, with exchange_index_statuses for indexes 0-3 and 'cache-control: public, max-age=1'.
checks.corrected_fact: In the rare EXCHANGE pause, which also covers unscheduled outages, cancels are NOT possible, so a cancel-on-exit safety plan can fail. Set cancel_order_on_pause=true and/or expiration_time on test orders. The top-level exchange_active / trading_active 'reflect the default exchange index (0)', so for KXBTC15M check the exchange_index_statuses entry with exchange_index 2, including intra_exchange_transfers_active.

checks.claim: The legacy /portfolio/orders mutation endpoints are deprecated (10x V2 cost, create = 100 tokens) and return 'Please switch to the V2 endpoints'. Send orders to /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders.
checks.evidence: Changelog Jun 18, 2026: 'Legacy `/portfolio/orders` mutation endpoints will be deprecated sometime between June 18 and June 25. Once deprecated, calls to these endpoints will return `Please switch to the V2 endpoints`'. Jun 4, 2026: '`POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders` - cost `50` to `100`', '`DELETE /trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders/{order_id}` - cost `10` to `20`'. openapi.yaml 3.32.0 no longer lists any legacy mutation path. Remaining: POST/DELETE /portfolio/events/orders, POST/DELETE /portfolio/events/orders/batched, DELETE /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}, POST .../{order_id}/amend, POST .../{order_id}/decrease.
checks.corrected_fact: READS still use the legacy prefix: GET /portfolio/orders and GET /portfolio/orders/{order_id}. The spec has no GET under /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}.

checks.claim: Authenticated requests spend tokens from Read and Write buckets. The default cost is 10. Write covers place, amend, cancel, order groups, RFQ quotes and block accepts; everything else is Read. REST and FIX share buckets. Sustained rate = budget / cost.
checks.evidence: rate_limits: 'Every authenticated request costs **tokens**. Your tier sets your **budget**... Your sustained rate for an endpoint is `budget ÷ cost`. Most requests cost the default of **10 tokens**.' Bucket table, and 'The split is by operation type, not by protocol. REST and FIX requests drain the same buckets.'
checks.corrected_fact: The docs do not literally say 'per-account'; the budget is set by 'your tier'. Write is further split into per-shard Write buckets, so 'two buckets' is a simplification.

checks.topic: rate limits: tiers (tokens per second, Read / Write)
checks.claim: Basic 200/100, Advanced 300/300, Expert 600/600, Premier 1,200/1,200, Paragon 2,400/2,400, Prime 4,800/4,800, Prestige 12,000/9,600. Premier and above were raised 20% on 2026-09-24. Basic gives about 20 GET/s and 10 creates/s.
checks.evidence: The rate_limits tier table matches exactly. Changelog Sep 24, 2026: 'Predictions read and write rate limits are increasing 20% for Premier, Paragon, Prime, and Prestige.' 200/10 = 20 and 100/10 = 10.

checks.claim: Basic and Advanced Read, and Write above Basic, hold 3 s of budget. Basic Write holds 1 s (100 tokens = 10 creates). Advanced Write holds 900. A batch must fit whole. OpenAPI says 'two seconds', which conflicts. GET /account/limits shows real values.
checks.evidence: rate_limits: 'Basic and Advanced Predictions Read buckets, and Write buckets above the Basic tier, hold up to **three seconds of budget**' and '...Basic-tier Write buckets hold one second of budget.' 'Write bucket capacity is three times the per-second budget above the Basic tier.' The Premier example shows bucket_capacity 3600. 'A 25-order create batch needs 250 tokens available when it arrives, or the entire batch is rejected.' openapi BucketLimit.bucket_capacity says '(e.g. write buckets at non-Basic tiers hold two seconds of budget)'; the conflict is real.

checks.claim: Create V2 = 10; Cancel V2 = 2; batch create 10 per order; batch cancel 2 per order; cancel-all = 2; upgrade = 30 Write tokens. GET /account/endpoint_costs lists non-default costs.
checks.evidence: cancel-order-v2: '**Rate limit:** 2 tokens per request.' batch-create-orders-v2: '10 tokens per order in the batch — billed per item'. batch-cancel-orders-v2: '2 tokens per order in the batch'. cancel-all-orders: '2 tokens per request, the same cost as cancelling one event-market order'. upgrade 429 text: 'This endpoint costs 30 tokens and uses the Predictions Write bucket.' create-order-v2 has no override, and RateLimitError says 'The default cost is 10 tokens per request'. GetAccountEndpointCostsResponse.default_cost: 'This is currently 10.'
checks.corrected_fact: In openapi.yaml, GET /account/endpoint_costs has NO security block, so it appears to be public. It was not called here because it sits under /account.

checks.claim: A single REST write with exchange_index >= 1 bills that shard; shard 0 bills unscoped; auto-routed writes bill every shard and add latency; batches bill unscoped; Read is not sharded.
checks.evidence: rate_limits, verbatim: '`exchange_index >= 1` is billed to that shard's Write bucket. Shard 0 traffic (`exchange_index: 0`) bills your unscoped Write bucket. Auto-routed traffic (`exchange_index: -1`, or omitted when `market_ticker` is provided) is billed to every shard's Write bucket.' '**Batch REST** creates and cancels always bill their total per-order cost to your unscoped Write bucket'. 'Read budgets are not shard-scoped.' exchange_sharding FAQ: 'Automatic routing will incur an additional latency cost.'

checks.claim: 429 body {"error": "too many requests"}, no Retry-After or X-RateLimit-* headers, no penalty or cooldown, exponential backoff, and a batch that does not fit is rejected in full.
checks.evidence: rate_limits, verbatim: 'A rate-limited request returns `429 Too Many Requests` with the body: {"error": "too many requests"}'; '429 responses do not currently include `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-*` headers. There is no penalty or cooldown.'; 'Apply exponential backoff on 429.'; '...or the entire batch is rejected.'

checks.topic: rate limits: 429 observed on public endpoint
checks.claim: At 17:57:28 UTC an unauthenticated GET to api.elections.kalshi.com/.../markets?limit=1 returned 429 with a nested body and no Retry-After; external-api returned 200 a second later. Public limits are undocumented.
checks.evidence: This was a point-in-time event, and I did not try to provoke a 429. Corroboration: the saved raw response kdocs_auth\prod_shared_markets.headers.txt shows 'Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 17:57:28 GMT', 'X-Cache: Error from cloudfront' and body {"error":{"code":"too_many_requests","message":"too many requests"}}. My own public 404 (GET /markets/NOT-A-REAL-TICKER-XYZ) has the same nested shape. The rate-limit docs cover only 'authenticated' requests, so public limits are indeed undocumented. 'Error from cloudfront' suggests the 429 came from the CDN layer, not the token bucket. Detect 429 by status code and accept both body shapes.

checks.claim: ErrorResponse = {code, message, details?} as strings, wrapped under 'error' in practice. Branch on 'code'; 'service' was removed 2026-08-06.
checks.evidence: openapi ErrorResponse: code 'Error code', message 'Human-readable error message', details 'Additional details about the error, if available' (all strings; the schema is unwrapped). Live public 404 GET https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2/markets/NOT-A-REAL-TICKER-XYZ returned {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"not found"}}, which is wrapped. Changelog Aug 6, 2026: 'The `service` field announced as deprecated on July 28 has been removed from error response bodies... Branch on `code` instead, which is present on every error response.' WebSocket errors differ: {"id":123,"type":"error","msg":{"code":2,"msg":"Params required"}}, with a numeric code.

checks.claim: Basic comes with signup. Advanced is self-serve via POST /account/api_usage_level/upgrade (needs 1 of the last 100 Predictions orders placed via API; permanent; 403 if not met) and is required for subaccounts. Expert+ is earned by 30-day volume share (Expert 0.075% earn / 0.05% keep) and granted for 30 days. GET /account/limits returns usage_tier, read/write {refill_rate, bucket_capacity} and grants[].expires_ts in seconds.
checks.evidence: upgrade page: 'Grants a permanent Advanced API usage-level grant... Criteria: at least 1 of the user's last 100 Predictions orders was created via API.' Responses: 201; 403 'No API-created order was found in the user's latest 100 Predictions orders'. rate_limits: 'Expert | 0.075% | 0.05%' and 'A qualifying review grants the tier for **30 days**'. create-subaccount: 'available to all users on the Advanced API tier and above'. GetAccountApiLimits grants.expires_ts: 'Unix timestamp (seconds) when the grant expires. Absent for permanent grants.'

checks.claim: WS connections per user depend on tier, from a default of 200. Orderbook subscriptions are capped at 500k markets per session and 10k commands/s.
checks.evidence: Changelog Sep 18, 2025: 'WebSocket connections per user are limited by usage tier. The default limit begins at 200 and increases based on API usage tier.' Jun 18, 2026: 'Max 500k market subscriptions per session.' and 'Max 10k/s commands per second enforced.'

checks.claim: Prod /markets sends cache-control max-age=15 and x-kalshi-cache-hits; demo sends max-age=5; the orderbook has no cache-control. Market-list prices can be about 15 s old. This is undocumented.
checks.evidence: Re-observed. Prod /markets: 'cache-control: public, max-age=15' and 'x-kalshi-cache-hits: 1' at 18:16:34, and again at 18:28:01-02 UTC even with request headers 'Cache-Control: no-cache' and 'Pragma: no-cache', so the server-side cache is not bypassed. Demo /markets: 'cache-control: public, max-age=5'. /exchange/status: 'public, max-age=1'. /markets/{ticker}/orderbook: no cache-control header. Error 404: 'cache-control: no-store'. No caching statement exists in llms-full.txt or openapi.yaml.

checks.claim: Using the API binds the user to the Developer Agreement. kalshi.com/developer-agreement returned 429 and was not read.
checks.evidence: welcome/index: 'By continuing to use or access Kalshi's API, you are agreeing to be bound to our Developer Agreement' linking https://kalshi.com/developer-agreement. I reproduced the block: curl returned 429 with a 'Vercel Security Checkpoint' page.
checks.corrected_fact: An official copy is readable: https://kalshi-public-docs.s3.amazonaws.com/Kalshi-Developer-Agreement.pdf ('v1.1', S3 Last-Modified 2023-11-09; it may not be the current kalshi.com version). Key clauses: Sec 3 'Use of Kalshi APIs is expressly limited to facilitating a members own trading on the Exchange'; 3.3 prohibits 'spoofing or wash sales'; 3.5 prohibits 'monitoring the availability, performance, or functionality' and benchmarking; 4.3 requires retries 'with exponential backoff, not immediately' and 'a bounded number of times'; Sec 5 allows throttling or termination at Kalshi's sole discretion; 9.2 caps Kalshi's aggregate liability at '$50.00 USD'.

checks.claim: Raw docs, specs, responses, starter code, SDK wheel and self-test are cached in scratchpad\kdocs_auth and \kdocs, and only public unauthenticated GETs were sent.
checks.evidence: The files exist: kdocs_auth has the SDK zip, starter files, sign_selftest.py, prod_/demo_ responses and help pages. Small slip: the OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specs are in scratchpad\kdocs and \verify, not kdocs_auth. I cannot audit another agent's network history. My own session sent only public GETs to /markets, /series/KXBTC15M, /markets/{ticker}/orderbook, /exchange/status and a bad-ticker 404, plus docs, PyPI, GitHub, help-center and S3 fetches.

checks.topic: open question: batch endpoints and Advanced tier
checks.claim: The research left open whether production batch order endpoints still require Advanced, as the Aug-2025 changelog said.
checks.evidence: Changelog Nov 14, 2025: '`POST /portfolio/orders/batched` will now be generally available. Advanced API access is no longer a prerequisite. Release date: `November 20, 2025`'. Dec 1, 2025: '`DELETE /portfolio/orders/batched` is now generally available. Advanced API access is no longer required... Release date: `December 4, 2025`'. The V2 batch pages only say 'The maximum batch size scales with your tier's write budget'.
checks.corrected_fact: Batch create and cancel need no Advanced tier in production. At Basic, a batch is effectively capped at 10 creates or 50 cancels because the whole batch must fit in the 100-token Write bucket.

checks.claim: The quoted code blocks are verbatim from official sources, and the offline self-test output is correct.
checks.evidence: Compared against fresh fetches: the api_keys Python blocks, the quick-start Complete Working Example, the create-order Step 2 POST (side 'bid', count '1', price '0.0100', 'good_till_canceled', 'taker_at_cross', success 201), the WS create_headers excerpt, SDK auth.py sign/create_auth_headers (identical to the 3.31.0 wheel), the openssl commands, the /account/limits JSON and the saved 429 response all match. My independent offline_sign_check.py reproduced every self-test assertion (64/88 Ed25519 deterministic; 256/344 RSA randomized; salt=32 verifies; the PKCS#8 RSA header).

missing_critical: KEY TYPE vs PROJECT CODE: the web 'Create New API Key' dialog has generated Ed25519 keys by default since 2026-10-01 (changelog), but the project's .env.example says 'Phase 2+ (Kalshi authenticated endpoints, RSA-PSS request signing)'. The project .venv (Python 3.12.10) has neither 'cryptography' nor 'websockets'. The signer must branch on isinstance(key, Ed25519PrivateKey), or the user must pick RSA in the dialog. Otherwise every call returns 401.

SHARD-2 COLLATERAL BEFORE ANY KXBTC15M ORDER: GET /portfolio/balance 'balance' (int CENTS) is the ALL-shard total by default (changelog Aug 20, 2026). Read balance_breakdown[exchange_index==2].balance (a dollar STRING such as '25.0000') or call ?exchange_index=2. To fund shard 2, use the UI at https://kalshi.com/account/exchange-indexes, or POST /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfer with REQUIRED source='event_contract', destination='event_contract', amount in CENTICENTS ($1.00 = 10000), source_exchange_shard=0, destination_exchange_shard=2. The transfer is async (200 = accepted, returns transfer_id; poll GET /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfers/{transfer_id}). It also needs a transfer-capable key ('write' or 'write::transfer'); a ['read','write::trade'] key most likely cannot do it. Check /exchange/status exchange_index_statuses[2].intra_exchange_transfers_active first.

READ-AFTER-WRITE LAG: GET /exchange/user_data_timestamp docs say 'There is typically a short delay before exchange events are reflected in the API endpoints. Whenever possible, combine API responses to PUT/POST/DELETE requests with WebSocket data' (affects GetBalance, GetOrder(s), GetFills, GetPositions). Reconcile from the mutation responses first (create 201: order_id, client_order_id, fill_count, remaining_count as FixedPointCount strings WITHOUT _fp, average_fill_price/average_fee_paid only when fill_count > 0, ts_ms epoch ms; cancel 200: reduced_by, ts_ms). Then use the authenticated WS 'user_orders' (has last_update_reason since 2026-10-01) and 'fill' channels, then REST.

ORDER READ PATHS AND FIELDS: reads stay at GET /portfolio/orders and GET /portfolio/orders/{order_id}; there is no GET under /portfolio/events/orders/{id}. Order fields: status enum resting|canceled|executed; fill_count_fp/remaining_count_fp/initial_count_fp (2-dp strings); yes_price_dollars/no_price_dollars; taker_fees_dollars/maker_fees_dollars; book_side bid|ask; outcome_side yes|no; exchange_index; client_order_id. GET /portfolio/orders has NO client_order_id filter for direct members, so filter by ticker and match client_order_id locally. Canceled or executed orders older than the historical cutoff (orders_updated_ts, about 2 weeks back) appear only in GET /historical/orders.

IDEMPOTENCY: always send a fresh uuid4 client_order_id and reuse it on retries. The create-order quick start says '409 Conflict: Order with this client_order_id already exists'. Treat a 409 on retry as 'possibly already placed' and look the order up; do not resubmit with a new id.

CREATE ORDER V2 FIELDS AND UNITS (POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders): required are ticker, side, count, price, time_in_force and self_trade_prevention_type. side is the YES-leg book side: 'bid' = buy YES, 'ask' = sell YES, which equals buy NO at 1-price. So 'buy NO at 1c' is side 'ask', price '0.9900'. count is a FixedPointCount STRING, and fractional contracts are allowed down to 0.01: '25' means 25 contracts, '0.25' means a quarter contract, so pin down the meaning of the user's '25*0.01'. price is a FixedPointDollars string with 2-4 dp ('0.0100') and must sit on the market's price_ranges grid. KXBTC15M uses tapered_deci_cent: $0.001 steps in [0, 0.10] and [0.90, 1.00], $0.01 steps between. The quick start's 400 hint 'price must be 1-99 cents' is stale. time_in_force is fill_or_kill | good_till_canceled | immediate_or_cancel. expiration_time is in Unix SECONDS (GTC only). reduce_only is accepted only with immediate_or_cancel. self_trade_prevention_type is taker_at_cross | maker.

KILL-SWITCH CAVEATS: DELETE /portfolio/events/orders (cancel-all, 2 tokens, all shards) warns 'Newly placed orders may also be cancelled during the minute after the request', so do not place new orders right after a cancel-all. Order groups (rolling 15-second contract limit) 'do not function across exchange instances'. In an exchange pause or outage, cancels are rejected, so give unattended test orders cancel_order_on_pause=true and an expiration_time.

ORDERBOOK ORDERING CONFLICT: the GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook API reference says levels are 'organized from best to worst prices'. The live response and the Orderbook Responses guide are ASCENDING with the best bid LAST (live depth=3 yes_dollars [['0.6600',..],['0.6700',..],['0.6800',..]]). Taking element [0] as best would price orders off the worst shown level. YES ask = 1 - last no_dollars price. GET /markets prices are server-cached up to about 15 s (max-age=15; a client no-cache header does not bypass it), so price orders from the orderbook endpoint or WS. WS orderbook channels report no-side levels in no-leg pricing unless the subscription sets use_yes_price: true.

STATUS VOCABULARY: GET /markets filter values are unopened|open|closed|settled, but market objects report status 'active' (enum initialized, inactive, active, closed, determined, disputed, amended, finalized). Code that checks market['status']=='open' will never match. Demo's status=open returned a stale 'closed' KXBTC15M market with exchange_index 0, so re-check status, close_time and exchange_index on each market before ordering.

EXCHANGE STATUS PER SHARD: GET /exchange/status is public (max-age=1). Its top-level trading_active and exchange_active 'reflect the default exchange index (0)'. Gate KXBTC15M orders on the exchange_index_statuses entry with exchange_index 2 ('Crypto & Commodities').

REDIRECTS: python-requests rewrites a 301 POST into a GET (body dropped) and keeps same-host custom headers, so the request reaches the wrong method and path with a stale signature. Use allow_redirects=False on every authenticated call and treat any 3xx as a hard error. The 301 was observed on /series/ and /markets/.

DEVELOPER AGREEMENT (official copy at https://kalshi-public-docs.s3.amazonaws.com/Kalshi-Developer-Agreement.pdf, v1.1): API use is limited to the member's own trading. Spoofing and wash sales are prohibited, so test orders that are placed only to be cancelled should be few and genuinely executable. 'Monitoring the availability, performance, or functionality' of Kalshi is prohibited. Retries must use bounded exponential backoff. Kalshi's liability is capped at $50.

HOSTS AND ENV SELECTION IN THIS PROJECT: config\settings.yaml base_url is the shared https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2, where background collectors already drew a CloudFront 429. Send order traffic to the recommended https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2 (prod) or https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 (demo). .env.example defaults KALSHI_ENV=prod with ONE key id/path pair. Make the environment and key pairing explicit and fail closed: demo keys return 401 on prod hosts and vice versa.

TOKEN COSTS SOURCE: GET /trade-api/v2/account/endpoint_costs has no security requirement in openapi.yaml (appears public) and would give the authoritative non-default costs. It was not called because it is under /account; the user can decide to call it.

facts.fact: Event-market orders are created with POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders (operationId CreateOrderV2). In the current OpenAPI spec (info.version 3.32.0), /portfolio/orders has only a GET. The legacy POST /portfolio/orders and its cancel/amend/decrease/batch siblings are no longer in the spec's paths. The surviving /portfolio/orders paths are GET /portfolio/orders, GET /portfolio/orders/{order_id}, GET /portfolio/orders/queue_positions and GET /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/queue_position.
facts.quote: Endpoint for submitting event-market orders using the V2 request/response shape (single-book `bid`/`ask` side and fixed-point dollar prices). The legacy `/portfolio/orders` endpoint will be deprecated no earlier than May 6, 2026 — clients should migrate to this path.

facts.fact: The changelog entry of June 18, 2026 deprecates all six legacy mutation endpoints: POST /portfolio/orders, DELETE /portfolio/orders/{order_id}, POST /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/decrease, POST and DELETE /portfolio/orders/batched, and POST /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/amend. Before that, their token cost was raised to 10x the V2 cost (POST /portfolio/orders went to 100 tokens; V2 create is 10). I did not call these endpoints (not allowed), so their current behaviour comes from the changelog only.
facts.quote: Legacy `/portfolio/orders` mutation endpoints will be deprecated sometime between June 18 and June 25. Once deprecated, calls to these endpoints will return `Please switch to the V2 endpoints` with a link to the V2 order API reference.

facts.fact: Required body fields: ticker (string), side (BookSide 'bid'|'ask'), count (FixedPointCount string), price (FixedPointDollars string), time_in_force, self_trade_prevention_type. Optional: client_order_id (string), expiration_time (int64, Unix SECONDS), post_only (bool), cancel_order_on_pause (bool), reduce_only (bool), subaccount (int >= 0), order_group_id (string), exchange_index (int). V2 has none of these legacy fields: type, action, yes_price, no_price, yes_price_dollars, no_price_dollars, count_fp, buy_max_cost, sell_position_floor, expiration_ts.
facts.quote:
required:
        - ticker
        - side
        - count
        - price
        - time_in_force
        - self_trade_prevention_type

facts.fact: V2 quotes everything on the YES leg. side='bid' buys YES at `price`. side='ask' sells YES at `price`, which is economically the same as buying NO at 1 - price. To buy NO at $0.12, send side='ask' with price='0.8800'. To exit a YES long, send side='ask'; add reduce_only=true with time_in_force='immediate_or_cancel' so the order can only reduce. Prices are never expressed as a NO price in V2.
facts.quote: Side of the book for an order or trade. For event markets, this refers to the YES leg only: `bid` means buy YES, `ask` means sell YES. (Selling YES is economically equivalent to buying NO at `1 - price`, but this endpoint quotes everything from the YES side.)

facts.fact: `price` and every *_dollars field are US DOLLAR strings, not cents. Requests accept 2-4 decimal places; responses emit up to 6. Examples: '0.5600' is 56 cents; '0.9580' is a sub-cent level seen live on KXBTC15M. Always format with 4 decimals. A 1-decimal string such as '0.5' falls outside the documented input format.
facts.quote: Fixed-point US dollar string. Most request fields accept 2-4 decimal places (e.g., "0.56", "0.5600"); responses emit up to 6. Valid quote intervals for a given market are constrained by that market's price level structure.

facts.fact: The V2 `count` field is a fixed-point CONTRACT string, the same format as '_fp' fields. V2 has no separate count_fp field. Requests accept 0-2 decimals ('10', '10.0', '10.00'); responses always emit 2 ('10.00'). Fractional contracts are allowed in 0.01 steps. Naming pitfall: the V2 create/amend/decrease responses call these fields fill_count and remaining_count (no _fp suffix), but they are still FixedPointCount strings. The Order object uses fill_count_fp, remaining_count_fp and initial_count_fp.
facts.quote: Fixed-point contract count string (2 decimals, e.g., "10.00"; referred to as "fp" in field names). Requests accept 0-2 decimal places (e.g., "10", "10.0", "10.00"); responses always emit 2 decimals. Fractional contract values (e.g., "2.50") are supported; the minimum granularity is 0.01 contracts.

facts.fact: Since Apr 17, 2026 every active market supports fractional contracts. The fractional_trading_enabled flag was deprecated then and removed from the REST schema on July 9, 2026. Live data shows fractional book sizes, e.g. KXBTC15M yes_bid_size_fp '6012.99'.
facts.quote: `Market` and `EventChildMarket` responses now support fractional trading unconditionally — the field is always `true`.

facts.fact: V2 documents no minimum order size and no minimum notional. The only stated constraint is 0.01-contract granularity, so the smallest count is presumably '0.01' (unverified). The 'minimum: 1, whole contracts only' rule belongs only to the legacy integer `count` field.
facts.quote:
count:
          type: integer
          minimum: 1
          description: Order quantity in contracts (whole contracts only). Provide count or count_fp; if both provided they must match.

facts.fact: Market.price_ranges is the authoritative tick grid: an array of {start, end, step} dollar strings. Snap every order price to the step of the band that contains it; off-grid prices are rejected. price_level_structure is only a label, so do not branch on it. Whole-cent prices are valid in every structure.
facts.quote: `price_ranges` — an array of `{ start, end, step }` bands in fixed-point dollars. This is the source of truth for valid prices: any price on the grid is valid, and any off-grid price is rejected. Consume it dynamically per market and snap order and quote prices to the relevant band's `step`.

facts.fact: tapered_deci_cent ticks are $0.001 from $0.00 to $0.10, $0.01 from $0.10 to $0.90, and $0.001 from $0.90 to $1.00. Other structures: linear_cent ($0.01 everywhere), deci_cent ($0.001 everywhere), the center_{x}_edge_{y}_cent family, and center_deci_edge_centi_cent ($0.0001 below $0.01 and above $0.99; used by all combo markets).

Public GETs on 2026-10-05 confirmed the field names and units. KXBTC15M-26OCT051400-00: exchange_index 2, price_level_structure 'tapered_deci_cent', 3-band price_ranges, yes_bid_dollars '0.8800', yes_ask_dollars '0.8900', yes_bid_size_fp '6012.99', notional_value_dollars '1.0000', status 'active'. Its orderbook had sub-cent levels (yes '0.9580', '0.9590'). KXGOLD15M: exchange_index 2, tapered_deci_cent. KXUSDJPY15M-26OCT051415-30 and KXTEMPMIAH-26OCT0515-T91.99: exchange_index 0, linear_cent, a single band with step '0.0100'. An empty side reports yes_bid_dollars '0.0000' with size '0.00'.
facts.quote: "exchange_index":2,..."price_level_structure":"tapered_deci_cent","price_ranges":[{"end":"0.1000","start":"0.0000","step":"0.0010"},{"end":"0.9000","start":"0.1000","step":"0.0100"},{"end":"1.0000","start":"0.9000","step":"0.0010"}]

facts.fact: $0 and $1 are invalid prices; Kalshi documents the reject for FIX, and REST presumably shares the same matching engine. Valid prices are strictly between 0 and 1 and on the grid. On tapered_deci_cent that means '0.0010' to '0.9990'; on linear_cent, '0.0100' to '0.9900'.
facts.quote: Invalid price (off-tick, out-of-band, `$0`, or `$1`): `Text<58>=INVALID_PRICE`, `CxlRejReason<102>=99` (Other)

facts.fact: time_in_force is REQUIRED in V2. Allowed values: 'fill_or_kill', 'good_till_canceled', 'immediate_or_cancel'. REST has no 'Day' or 'GTD' values (FIX does). For an expiring order, send good_till_canceled plus expiration_time. immediate_or_cancel cannot be combined with expiration_time.
facts.quote: Use `good_till_canceled` with `expiration_time` for an order that should rest until a specific expiration time; without `expiration_time`, `good_till_canceled` is a true good-till-canceled order. `GTT` is not a valid API value.

facts.fact: The V2 request field is expiration_time, an int64 Unix timestamp in SECONDS. The legacy request field was called expiration_ts. Type pitfall: on the REST Order object, expiration_time is an RFC3339 date-time string. The WebSocket user_orders channel uses expiration_ts_ms, in milliseconds.
facts.quote: Optional Unix timestamp in seconds for when the order expires. To place an expiring order, set `time_in_force` to `good_till_canceled` and provide this `expiration_time`.

facts.fact: post_only is a plain boolean with no schema description. A post-only order that would cross the book is cancelled, never filled. It is reported with last_update_reason 'PostOnlyCrossCancel' on REST and WebSocket, and Text 'POST_ONLY_CROSS' on FIX. An Oct 24, 2025 changelog entry for the legacy batch endpoint says crossing post-only orders return error code 'invalid order' with details 'post only cross'. The exact V2 single-create response for a crossing post-only order is not documented.
facts.quote: When a post-only order would cross the book, the `last_update_reason` field is now reported as `PostOnlyCrossCancel` instead of `Decrease`.

facts.fact: reduce_only (bool) caps the order size at your current position. It is accepted only with time_in_force 'immediate_or_cancel'; any other combination is rejected. If there is no position to reduce, the update reports last_update_reason 'ReduceOnlyCancel'.
facts.quote: Specifies whether the order place count should be capped by the member's current position. Orders with reduce_only set to true will be rejected unless time_in_force is immediate_or_cancel.
