facts.fact: self_trade_prevention_type is REQUIRED in V2. Allowed values: 'taker_at_cross' and 'maker'.
facts.quote: `taker_at_cross` cancels the taker order when it would trade against another order from the same user; execution stops and any partial fills already matched are executed. `maker` cancels the resting maker order and continues matching.

facts.fact: client_order_id is an optional string. Confirmed: resubmitting a client_order_id that is already in use is rejected with 409 Conflict, so retries with the same ID are idempotent. Not specified for REST: maximum length and allowed characters. The FIX spec says 'UUID preferred, max 64 chars. Must not match any open order', and the FCM changelog says IDs are unique only 'among live and recent orders', so uniqueness is not permanent. GET /portfolio/orders cannot filter by client_order_id (only the FCM endpoint can). To find an order after a timed-out create, list by ticker and match Order.client_order_id.
facts.quote: The API will reject duplicate submissions with the same `client_order_id`, preventing accidental double orders

facts.fact: exchange_index on create is optional. If it is omitted, the order auto-routes by ticker; -1 forces auto-routing. Auto-routing adds latency and is billed to every shard's Write bucket, while an explicit index >= 1 is billed only to that shard. Pass the market's own exchange_index from GET /markets. Live values: 2 for KXBTC15M and KXGOLD15M; 0 for KXUSDJPY15M and KXTEMPMIAH.
facts.quote: Exchange shard index. If omitted, auto-routes when ticker is provided; otherwise defaults to 0. Use -1 to require auto-routing by ticker.

facts.fact: Collateral is checked per shard inside the matching engine. API orders do NOT move cash between shards automatically; only App/Web orders do. Shards: 0 = default, 1 = Exotics (combos), 2 = Crypto and Commodities, 3 = Tennis, Baseball and Basketball. BTC and gold 15-minute orders need cash already on shard 2; FX and weather orders need it on shard 0. GET /portfolio/balance returns balance_breakdown[{exchange_index, balance (dollar string)}]. Funding can be done in the UI (kalshi.com/account/exchange-indexes) or with POST /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfer, whose `amount` is an integer in CENTICENTS ($5.00 = 50000).
facts.quote: Kalshi's collateralization checks run within the matching engine. Programmatic traders must preallocate collateral on a given exchange shard before order placement.

facts.fact: Success is HTTP 201 with a lightweight body, not a full Order. Required fields: order_id, fill_count, remaining_count, ts_ms. Optional fields: client_order_id, average_fill_price, average_fee_paid. average_fill_price and average_fee_paid are dollar strings, present only when fill_count > 0, and average_fee_paid is PER CONTRACT. ts_ms is the matching-engine time in Unix milliseconds. For IOC orders, remaining_count is the final value after the unfilled part is cancelled. The response has no status field: remaining_count '0.00' means nothing is resting. Get the full state from GET or the WebSocket.
facts.quote:
example:
        order_id: 3b23c1c7-f4ef-4f0d-8b9a-9e53c61f1a0d
        client_order_id: 8c35ecb3-328f-4f52-8c7c-0f4b9862f8d1
        fill_count: "0.00"
        remaining_count: "10.00"
        ts_ms: 1715793600123

facts.fact: Create V2 can return 400, 401, 403, 409, 429, 500 and 503. The error body (ErrorResponse) has three strings: code, message, details. Branch on `code`; the `service` field was removed in Aug 2026. A 429 uses a different body: {"error": "too many requests"}. The docs do not list REST `code` values for order rejects. FIX Text(58) values hint at them: ORDER_ALREADY_EXISTS, MARKET_INACTIVE, MARKET_ALREADY_CLOSED, EXCEEDED_PER_MARKET_RISK_LIMIT, FOK_INSUFFICIENT_VOLUME, POST_ONLY_CROSS, REDUCE_ONLY, INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE, EXCHANGE_UNAVAILABLE (outcome unknown: reconcile).
facts.quote:
ErrorResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        code:
          type: string
          description: Error code
        message:
          type: string
          description: Human-readable error message
        details:
          type: string

facts.fact: Market orders are gone from the API. `type` was removed from create on Feb 11, 2026, and V2 has no type field, so every order is a limit order with a required price. To take liquidity, send an aggressive limit price with immediate_or_cancel or fill_or_kill. Order objects still carry type ['limit','market'] for historical orders. The help center still describes 'market orders' for the app.
facts.quote: `POST /portfolio/orders` removed `type`; `type=market` is no longer offered.

facts.fact: The legacy CreateOrderRequest schema is still in the spec's components but no path uses it. Its fields: side 'yes'|'no' plus action 'buy'|'sell'; count (integer >= 1, whole contracts) and/or count_fp (string); yes_price/no_price (integer CENTS, 1-99); yes_price_dollars/no_price_dollars (dollar strings); expiration_ts (Unix seconds); buy_max_cost (integer CENTS, forces fill-or-kill); sell_position_floor (deprecated, accepts only 0; use reduce_only); exchange_index (default 0, no auto-routing). None of these exist in V2. The FIX equivalent of buy_max_cost is MaxExecutionCost (tag 21009), in dollars.
facts.quote:
buy_max_cost:
          type: integer
          description: Maximum cost in cents. When specified, the order will automatically have Fill-or-Kill (FoK) behavior.

facts.fact: DELETE /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}, no body. Query params: subaccount (default 0), exchange_index, market_ticker. Response 200: {order_id, client_order_id, reduced_by, ts_ms}, where reduced_by is a FixedPointCount string equal to the remaining count at cancel time. Cost: 2 tokens. Pitfall: if both exchange_index and market_ticker are omitted, the cancel goes to shard 0, so a shard-2 (BTC) order must be cancelled with exchange_index=2 or market_ticker.
facts.quote: Exchange shard index. If omitted, auto-routes when market_ticker is provided; otherwise defaults to 0. Use -1 to require auto-routing. The market_ticker parameter is required for auto-routing.

facts.fact: POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}/amend, with subaccount as a query param. Required body fields: ticker, side ('bid'|'ask'), price (dollar string), count (FixedPointCount). Optional: client_order_id (the original), updated_client_order_id, expiration_time (Unix seconds; omit to keep, 0 to clear; added Oct 1, 2026), exchange_index. `count` is the new TOTAL (already filled plus desired resting), not the remaining amount. Response 200: {order_id, client_order_id, remaining_count, fill_count, average_fill_price, average_fee_paid, ts_ms}; an amend that crosses the book fills immediately.
facts.quote: The request `count` is the updated total/max fillable count, equal to already filled count plus desired resting remaining count. This behavior matches the v1 amend endpoints; only the request/response shape differs.

facts.fact: Queue priority survives an expiry-only amend or a size decrease. A price change or a size increase sends the order to the back of the queue.
facts.quote: Amending only expiry or decreasing size preserves queue position. Increasing size or changing price forfeits queue position and places the order at the back of the queue.

facts.fact: POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}/decrease, with subaccount as a query param. Body: exactly one of reduce_by or reduce_to (FixedPointCount strings, e.g. '2.00'), plus optional exchange_index and market_ticker for routing. Response 200: {order_id, client_order_id, remaining_count, ts_ms}.
facts.quote: Endpoint for decreasing the remaining count of an existing event-market order using the V2 request/response shape. Exactly one of `reduce_by` or `reduce_to` must be provided.

facts.fact: POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders/batched with body {"orders": [CreateOrderV2Request, ...]}. Response 201: {"orders": [{order_id, client_order_id, fill_count, remaining_count, average_fill_price, average_fee_paid, ts_ms, error}]}. Each order can fail on its own, so check every item's `error` (ErrorResponse); ts_ms is absent on items that errored. Cost: 10 tokens PER ORDER. Batches are always billed to the unscoped Write bucket, whatever exchange_index says.
facts.quote: **Rate limit:** 10 tokens per order in the batch — billed per item, so total cost for a batch of N orders is N × 10.

facts.fact: Kalshi publishes no fixed maximum batch size; it 'scales with your tier's write budget'. The whole batch must fit in the token bucket at once, or the entire batch is rejected. My inference from the published budgets: Basic tier (100 tokens/s, 1-second Write bucket) allows at most 10 creates (10 x 10) or 50 cancels (50 x 2) per batch. Advanced (300/s, 3-second bucket = 900 tokens) allows about 90 creates.
facts.quote: The whole batch must fit in the bucket at once. A 25-order create batch needs 250 tokens available when it arrives, or the entire batch is rejected.

facts.fact: DELETE /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders/batched; this DELETE carries a JSON body: {"orders": [{order_id (required), subaccount, exchange_index, market_ticker}]}. Response 200: {"orders": [{order_id, client_order_id, reduced_by, ts_ms, error}]}, where reduced_by is a FixedPointCount string and is zero if that cancel errored. Cost: 2 tokens per order. Give every item a market_ticker or exchange_index.
facts.quote: For auto-routing, each order must include `market_ticker`. An `order_id` alone cannot identify the exchange shard.

facts.fact: DELETE /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders, with optional query param subaccount. It cancels all resting event-market orders on every shard and returns 204 with no body. Cost: 2 tokens. Caveat: orders placed in the following minute may also be cancelled.
facts.quote: Cancels all resting event-market orders for the authenticated Direct member across every exchange shard. If `subaccount` is omitted, matching orders may come from any subaccount. If it is provided, only orders for that subaccount are eligible. Newly placed orders may also be cancelled during the minute after the request.

facts.fact: GET /trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders. Query params: ticker; event_ticker (comma-separated, max 10); min_ts and max_ts (Unix timestamps); status; limit (1-1000, default 100); cursor; subaccount (omit for all); exchange_index (omit for all shards). Response: {orders: [Order], cursor}. Canceled or executed orders older than orders_updated_ts (currently about two weeks back) appear only in GET /historical/orders, which takes ticker, min_ts, max_ts, limit, cursor and subaccount.
facts.quote: Restricts the response to orders that have a certain status: resting, canceled, or executed. Orders that have been canceled or fully executed before the historical cutoff are only available via `GET /historical/orders`. Resting orders will always be available through this endpoint.

facts.fact: GET /trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders/{order_id} returns {"order": Order}. Cost: 2 tokens. The only documented parameter is order_id; there is no exchange_index.
facts.quote: **Rate limit:** 2 tokens per request. See `GET /trade-api/v2/account/endpoint_costs` for current non-default endpoint costs.

facts.fact: REST Order fields and units. IDs: order_id, user_id, client_order_id, ticker. Direction: outcome_side ('yes'|'no') and book_side ('bid'|'ask'); `side` and `action` are deprecated. Also type ('limit'|'market') and status. Prices: yes_price_dollars and no_price_dollars (dollar strings). Counts: fill_count_fp, remaining_count_fp, initial_count_fp (2-decimal contract strings). Money: taker_fill_cost_dollars, maker_fill_cost_dollars, taker_fees_dollars, maker_fees_dollars (dollar strings, up to 6 decimals). Times: expiration_time, created_time, last_update_time (RFC3339 strings). Other: self_trade_prevention_type, order_group_id, cancel_order_on_pause, subaccount_number, exchange_index. Integer-cent and integer-count fields were removed from all REST and WS responses on March 12, 2026.
facts.quote:
required:
        - order_id
        - user_id
        - client_order_id
        - ticker
        - outcome_side
        - book_side
        - type
        - status
        - yes_price_dollars
        - no_price_dollars
        - fill_count_fp
        - remaining_count_fp
        - initial_count_fp
        - taker_fees_dollars
        - maker_fees_dollars
        - taker_fill_cost_dollars
        - maker_fill_cost_dollars

facts.fact: REST order status values are exactly 'resting', 'canceled' and 'executed' (one L in 'canceled'). 'pending' was removed in Nov 2025. The WebSocket user_orders channel adds 'unknown'. A partially filled IOC presumably ends as 'canceled' with fill_count_fp > 0 (inferred from the field semantics, not documented).
facts.quote:
OrderStatus:
      type: string
      enum: ['resting', 'canceled', 'executed']

facts.fact: Mapping from legacy action/side to the new fields, with columns action | side | outcome_side | book_side: buy yes = yes/bid; sell no = yes/bid; buy no = no/ask; sell yes = no/ask. Use outcome_side/book_side; the deprecated fields will not be removed before May 28, 2026.
facts.quote:
| buy | yes | yes | bid |
| sell | no | yes | bid |
| buy | no | no | ask |
| sell | yes | no | ask |

facts.fact: GET /trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders/{order_id}/queue_position returns {"queue_position_fp": "<contracts ahead>"}. GET /trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders/queue_positions takes market_tickers (comma-separated), event_ticker and subaccount (default 0), and returns {"queue_positions": [{order_id, market_ticker, queue_position_fp}]}. Both values are FixedPointCount strings counting contracts ahead under price-time priority.
facts.quote: Endpoint for getting queue positions for all resting orders. Queue position represents the number of contracts that need to be matched before an order receives a partial or full match, determined using price-time priority.

facts.fact: Rate limits use two token buckets, Read and Write. Write covers order placement, amends, cancels, order groups, RFQ quotes and block-trade accepts. Per-second budgets (Read/Write): Basic 200/100, Advanced 300/300, Expert 600/600, Premier 1,200/1,200, Paragon 2,400/2,400, Prime 4,800/4,800, Prestige 12,000/9,600. A Basic Write bucket holds 1 second of budget; Write buckets above Basic hold 3 seconds. Sustained rate = budget / cost, e.g. Basic allows 10 creates per second.
facts.quote: Most requests cost the default of **10 tokens**. For endpoints that cost more or less, [`GET /account/endpoint_costs`](/api-reference/account/list-non-default-endpoint-costs) is the authoritative list of non-default costs currently in effect.

facts.fact: Order endpoint token costs. Documented: V2 create 10 (the default; no override is noted), V2 cancel 2, batch create 10 per order, batch cancel 2 per order, cancel-all 2, GET single order 2. Inferred: V2 amend 10 and V2 decrease 10, because the legacy 5x price step moved amend/decrease to 50 (= 5 x 10). The authoritative live list is GET /trade-api/v2/account/endpoint_costs (non-default costs only); I did not call it, since it is an account endpoint.
facts.quote: Legacy `/portfolio/orders` mutation and batch endpoint rate-limit token costs will be 5x the corresponding V2 `/portfolio/events/orders` endpoint costs. ... `POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders/{order_id}/amend` - cost `15` to `50`

facts.fact: A rate-limited request gets HTTP 429 with body {"error": "too many requests"}. There is no Retry-After header, no X-RateLimit-* headers, and no penalty or cooldown. Kalshi says to back off exponentially.
facts.quote: 429 responses do not currently include `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-*` headers. There is no penalty or cooldown. The bucket keeps refilling, and your next request succeeds once the balance covers its cost.

facts.fact: Single REST create, cancel, decrease and amend calls with exchange_index >= 1 are billed to that shard's Write bucket; exchange_index 0 goes to the unscoped bucket. Auto-routed single calls are billed to every shard's bucket. Batch calls always go to the unscoped bucket.
facts.quote: Auto-routed traffic (`exchange_index: -1`, or omitted when `market_ticker` is provided) is billed to every shard's Write bucket.

facts.fact: New accounts start at Basic. Advanced is self-serve via POST /trade-api/v2/account/api_usage_level/upgrade (30 tokens), but only after at least one of your last 100 orders was placed through the API. GET /trade-api/v2/account/limits returns {usage_tier, read: {refill_rate, bucket_capacity}, write: {refill_rate, bucket_capacity}, grants}.
facts.quote: Grants a permanent Advanced API usage-level grant. Currently only the Predictions exchange instance is supported. Criteria: at least 1 of the user's last 100 Predictions orders was created via API.

facts.fact: I found no published limit on the number of open or resting orders in the docs, the help center or the changelog. Published count limits: at most 100,000 order groups per user, and an order-group contracts_limit of 1 to 1,000,000 per rolling 15 seconds. Per-market risk limits exist (FIX reject EXCEEDED_PER_MARKET_RISK_LIMIT), but their values are not in the API docs.
facts.quote: Creates a new order group with a contracts limit measured over a rolling 15-second window. Users can have up to 100,000 order groups at a time. When the limit is hit, all orders in the group are cancelled and no new orders can be placed until reset.

facts.fact: An order group works as a fill circuit breaker. Create it with POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/order_groups/create, body {contracts_limit (int >= 1) or contracts_limit_fp (string), subaccount, exchange_index (default 0)}; the response is {order_group_id, subaccount, exchange_index}. Put order_group_id on every create. If fills within a rolling 15 seconds exceed the limit, the group cancels all its orders and rejects new ones until PUT /portfolio/order_groups/{id}/reset. A group lives on ONE shard: create it with exchange_index 2 for BTC or gold.
facts.quote: Order groups do not function across exchange instances.

facts.fact: Every Thursday from 3:00 to 5:00 AM ET there is a trading pause. During it you cannot place or amend orders, but cancels work. During a rarer exchange pause, cancels fail too. Resting orders stay on the book unless cancel_order_on_pause is true.
facts.quote: Every **Thursday from 3:00 AM to 5:00 AM ET**, Kalshi runs scheduled maintenance. During this window, a **trading pause** is in effect.

facts.fact: Orders work only while market status == 'active'; the GET /markets filter value 'open' maps to 'active'. After close_time (every 15 minutes on 15-minute series), all order operations, including cancels, are rejected with MARKET_INACTIVE, and resting orders are cancelled shortly after. When an inactive market is reactivated, all its resting orders are cancelled.
facts.quote: Once `close_time` passes, all order operations, including cancellations, are rejected with `MARKET_INACTIVE`. Resting orders are cancelled shortly after close, and cancellation updates are published on the usual user channels.

facts.fact: GET orders, fills, positions and balance lag the exchange. Reconcile using the mutation responses plus the WebSocket user_orders and fill channels. GET /exchange/user_data_timestamp returns as_of_time.
facts.quote: There is typically a short delay before exchange events are reflected in the API endpoints. Whenever possible, combine API responses to PUT/POST/DELETE requests with WebSocket data to obtain the most accurate view of the exchange state.

facts.fact: Channel user_orders (authenticated; message type 'user_order') sends an update on every create, fill, cancel and amend. Message fields: order_id, ticker, exchange_index, status (resting|canceled|executed|unknown), outcome_side, book_side, yes_price_dollars (4 decimals; there is no no_price field), fill_count_fp, remaining_count_fp and initial_count_fp (2 decimals), taker/maker fill-cost and fee fields in dollars (6 decimals), client_order_id, created_ts_ms, last_updated_ts_ms, expiration_ts_ms, last_update_reason. last_update_reason values: Decrease, Amend, MarginCancel, SelfTradeCancel, ExpiryCancel, CloseCancel, HaltCancel, Trade, PostOnlyCrossCancel, ReduceOnlyCancel, SettlementBoundsCancel.
facts.quote: Order update reason. ReduceOnlyCancel means reduce_only capped the order at placement.

facts.fact: Fills no longer include client_order_id (removed Mar 30, 2026), so map fills to orders by order_id. Fill fields and units: count_fp (contract string), yes_price_dollars and no_price_dollars (dollar strings), fee_cost (dollar string), is_taker (bool), exchange_index.
facts.quote: Removed `client_order_id` from `GET /portfolio/fills` and `GET /portfolio/fills/historical` responses.

facts.fact: GET /portfolio/balance: `balance` is an integer in CENTS and truncates sub-cent amounts; `balance_dollars` is an exact dollar string; `portfolio_value` is an integer in CENTS; balance_breakdown is [{exchange_index, balance (dollar string)}]. Direct-member balances are aligned to $0.0001.
facts.quote: The legacy `balance` field truncates any sub-cent amount, so use `balance_dollars` for exact values.

facts.fact: Fees are computed at $0.000001 granularity. Balances are then aligned to $0.0001 for direct members and $0.01 for FCM-cleared (non-direct) members, with a per-order accumulator that rebates rounding overpayment. In the Order object, taker_fees_dollars and maker_fees_dollars are totals. In create and amend responses, average_fee_paid is per contract.
facts.quote: Fees are six-decimal dollar amounts (`$0.000001` granularity) — the finest precision a fill's revenue (price × quantity) can occupy.

facts.fact: Required headers: KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY (the key ID), KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP (milliseconds), and KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE. The signature is base64 RSA-PSS-SHA256 or Ed25519 over timestamp + method + path. Sign the full path from the API root without the query string, e.g. '/trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders'. Production base URL: https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2 (recommended; https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2 also works). Demo: https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2.
facts.quote: Base64 signature of the pre-sign text (timestamp + method + path) made with the API key's algorithm - RSA-PSS with SHA-256 for RSA keys, Ed25519 for Ed25519 keys

facts.fact: For least privilege, give the bot's key only the scopes ['read', 'write::trade']. write::trade allows order, order-group and RFQ writes but not transfers, so a leaked key cannot move money between shards or subaccounts. Do shard funding by hand in the UI.
facts.quote: API keys can use `write::trade` to grant access to order, order-group, and RFQ/quote write endpoints without granting transfer-write access.

facts.fact: Where `subaccount` goes: in the BODY on create and on each batch-cancel item; in the QUERY string on single cancel, amend and decrease (default 0). Omit it unless you use subaccounts.
facts.quote: Subaccount number (0 for primary, 1-63 for subaccounts). Defaults to 0.

facts.fact: Official Python SDKs: kalshi_python_sync 3.31.0 (uploaded 2026-09-29, requires Python >= 3.13) and kalshi_python_async. OrdersApi methods: create_order_v2, cancel_order_v2, amend_order_v2, decrease_order_v2, batch_create_orders_v2, batch_cancel_orders_v2, cancel_all_orders, get_order, get_orders, get_order_queue_position, get_order_queue_positions. There is no legacy create_order. The CreateOrderV2Request model types count and price as StrictStr. The public starter repo github.com/Kalshi/kalshi-starter-code-python was last pushed 2025-03-07, before V2 orders and fixed-point pricing, so do not copy its order payloads.
facts.quote: SDKs are updated periodically and may lag the API. Active traders should treat the REST [OpenAPI specification](https://docs.kalshi.com/openapi.yaml) and WebSocket [AsyncAPI specification](https://docs.kalshi.com/asyncapi.yaml) as the source of truth.

facts.fact: On May 21, 2026, Kalshi disclosed that V2 cancel and amend responses can occasionally describe a different order than the one requested. The cancel or amend itself still executes correctly. No later changelog entry says this was fixed (the Sept 3 entry only fixed amend remaining_count). To be safe, check that the response's order_id equals the requested one and reconcile through WS or GET.
facts.quote: In certain uncommon cases, responses from `DELETE /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}` and `POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}/amend` do not describe the order that was cancelled or amended

facts.fact: GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook needs no auth and returns {"orderbook_fp": {"yes_dollars": [[price, count], ...], "no_dollars": [...]}}. It lists bids only, as strings, sorted ascending, so the best bid is the LAST element. Best YES ask = 1 - best NO bid. Live example on KXBTC15M: yes_dollars ending ['0.9590','1740.54'], no_dollars ending ['0.0400','1098.60'], so the YES ask was 0.9600.
facts.quote: Arrays are sorted by price in **ascending order**

facts.fact: Kalshi runs a demo environment with mock funds and separate credentials (https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2). It can validate V2 payload shapes before any real-money test, though demo prices and behaviour may differ from production.
facts.quote: For testing purposes, Kalshi offers a *demo* environment with mock funds.

facts.fact: The help center says an open resting order blocks closing the same position until that order is cancelled. It is unclear whether this applies only in the app or also to API orders.
facts.quote: If you have an open resting limit order on a position, you cannot partially or fully close that position until the resting order is cancelled.

facts.fact: Once an account's location attestation lapses, its API keys can no longer trade Sports, Elections and Entertainment markets; GET /api_keys returns api_key_region_expiration_ts. The changelog does not mention crypto, FX or weather markets, but this is a possible reject cause.
facts.quote: Once this date has passed, API keys are not valid for trading Sports, Elections, and Entertainment markets.

facts.fact: Two places in the docs are stale or contradict each other. (1) The Quick Start still says '400 Bad Request: Verify your order parameters (price must be 1-99 cents)', which predates dollar-string and sub-cent pricing. (2) The OpenAPI BucketLimit schema says non-Basic write buckets hold two seconds of budget, but the rate-limit guide says three. Read GET /account/limits at startup instead of hard-coding capacity.
facts.quote: pulse (e.g. write buckets at non-Basic tiers hold two seconds of budget).

code_examples.purpose: Official Quick Start: authenticated POST helper (signs the full path without the query string) plus a V2 create-order body: buy 1 YES at $0.01, GTC, with client_order_id for dedup. Shows 201 handling and the lightweight response fields.
code_examples.code:
def post(private_key, api_key_id, path, data, base_url=BASE_URL):
    """Make an authenticated POST request to the Kalshi API."""
    timestamp = str(int(datetime.datetime.now().timestamp() * 1000))
    # Signing requires the full URL path from root (e.g. /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders)
    sign_path = urlparse(base_url + path).path
    signature = create_signature(private_key, timestamp, "POST", sign_path)

    headers = {
        'KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY': api_key_id,
        'KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE': signature,
        'KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP': timestamp,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    }

    return requests.post(base_url + path, headers=headers, json=data)

# Place a buy order for 1 YES contract at 1 cent
order_data = {
    "ticker": market['ticker'],
    "side": "bid",
    "count": "1",
    "price": "0.0100",
    "time_in_force": "good_till_canceled",
    "self_trade_prevention_type": "taker_at_cross",
    "client_order_id": str(uuid.uuid4())  # Unique ID for deduplication
}

response = post(private_key, API_KEY_ID, '/portfolio/events/orders', order_data)

if response.status_code == 201:
    order = response.json()
    print(f"Order ID: {order['order_id']}")
    print(f"Remaining Count: {order['remaining_count']}")
else:
    print(f"Error: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")

code_examples.purpose: Batch create V2: request and response examples from the OpenAPI spec, converted from YAML to JSON. Note the per-item results and that average_fee_paid is per contract.
Cancel, decrease, amend and batch-cancel V2 examples from the OpenAPI spec, converted to JSON. Amend `count` is the TOTAL (filled + resting).

ILLUSTRATIVE (I wrote this from the docs' guidance; it is not Kalshi code). Snaps a YES price onto the market's price_ranges grid in the safe direction, then builds a tiny post-only V2 maker order on the market's own shard. The short expiration acts as a dead-man switch. To buy NO at p_no, use side='ask' with yes price 1 - p_no.
code_examples.code:
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_FLOOR, ROUND_CEILING
import time, uuid

def snap_to_grid(price: Decimal, price_ranges: list, side: str) -> Decimal:
    # bid rounds down (never pay more), ask rounds up (never sell YES cheaper)
    for band in price_ranges:
        start, end, step = (Decimal(band[k]) for k in ("start", "end", "step"))
        if start <= price <= end:
            n = ((price - start) / step).to_integral_value(
                rounding=ROUND_FLOOR if side == "bid" else ROUND_CEILING)
            snapped = start + n * step
            if not (Decimal("0") < snapped < Decimal("1")):
                raise ValueError("price must be strictly between $0 and $1")
            return snapped
    raise ValueError("price outside price_ranges")

def tiny_maker_order(market: dict, side: str, yes_price: str, count: str = "1") -> dict:
    assert market["status"] == "active"
    price = snap_to_grid(Decimal(yes_price), market["price_ranges"], side)
    return {
        "ticker": market["ticker"],
        "side": side,                                # 'bid' = buy YES; 'ask' = sell YES / buy NO at 1-price
        "count": f"{Decimal(count):.2f}",            # contracts, string, 0.01 granularity
        "price": f"{price:.4f}",                     # YES price in DOLLARS, e.g. '0.0100'
        "time_in_force": "good_till_canceled",
        "expiration_time": int(time.time()) + 120,   # Unix SECONDS
        "post_only": True,
        "self_trade_prevention_type": "taker_at_cross",
        "cancel_order_on_pause": True,
        "client_order_id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
        "exchange_index": market["exchange_index"],  # 2 for KXBTC15M/KXGOLD15M, 0 for KXUSDJPY15M/KXTEMPMIAH
    }

code_examples.purpose: Official example: best YES ask from the bid-only orderbook (YES ask = 1 - best NO bid; the best bid is the last array element). Use Decimal, not float.
code_examples.code:
from decimal import Decimal

# Using the example orderbook above
best_yes_bid = Decimal("0.4200")  # Highest YES bid (last in array)
best_yes_ask = Decimal("1.00") - Decimal("0.5600")  # $1.00 - highest NO bid = $0.44

spread = best_yes_ask - best_yes_bid  # $0.44 - $0.42 = $0.02

open_questions: What does V2 single-create return when a post_only order would cross? The 2025 legacy batch entry says error code 'invalid order' with details 'post only cross', but the V2 create response (an HTTP 4xx, or a 201 with remaining_count '0.00') is not documented.

The REST error `code` strings for common order rejects are not listed anywhere. Cases: insufficient collateral on the target shard, off-grid price, MARKET_INACTIVE after close, duplicate client_order_id (409), reduce_only without IOC. Only FIX Text(58) values are documented.

REST client_order_id constraints are unspecified: maximum length, allowed characters, and how long a used ID stays blocked after the order is canceled or executed. FIX says max 64 characters and 'must not match any open order'; the FCM note says unique only among live and recent orders.
What is the exact maximum batch size per tier? The docs only say it scales with the write budget; 10 creates per batch on Basic is my inference.
Is legacy POST /portfolio/orders now hard-failing with 'Please switch to the V2 endpoints', or does it still work at 100 tokens? Calling it to check was out of bounds.
How large is the Write-bucket burst above Basic? The rate-limit guide says 3 seconds and the OpenAPI BucketLimit says 2. Read GET /account/limits at runtime.

Is count '0.01' actually accepted? Is there a minimum notional or minimum fee on sub-1-contract orders? And is a retail kalshi.com account a 'direct member' ($0.0001 balance and fee precision) or not?
Do REST Order objects include last_update_reason? The June 4, 2026 changelog says GET /portfolio/orders reports it, but the OpenAPI 3.32.0 Order schema does not list it.
Has the May 21, 2026 issue (V2 cancel/amend responses sometimes describing the wrong order) been fixed? No changelog entry confirms a fix.
Does GET /portfolio/orders/{order_id} find orders on shard 2 without an exchange_index? That endpoint documents no shard parameter.
What exact error does a shard-2 order get when shard 2 has no collateral but shard 0 does? The docs say only that programmatic traders must preallocate per shard.
Does the help-center rule that a resting order blocks closing the same position also apply to API orders, or only to the app?

checks.topic: endpoint-status (V2 path, spec version, surviving paths)
checks.claim: Orders are created with POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders (CreateOrderV2). The spec is info.version 3.32.0. /portfolio/orders has only a GET, and the legacy mutation paths are gone. The surviving GETs are /portfolio/orders, /portfolio/orders/{order_id}, /portfolio/orders/queue_positions and /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/queue_position.
checks.evidence: I downloaded openapi.yaml (info.version: 3.32.0) and listed every path and method. Only GET exists under /portfolio/orders*. 'POST /portfolio/events/orders' has operationId CreateOrderV2. Independent check: the official SDK kalshi_python_sync 3.31.0 (orders_api.py) has create_order_v2, cancel_order_v2, amend_order_v2, decrease_order_v2, batch_create_orders_v2, batch_cancel_orders_v2, cancel_all_orders, get_order, get_orders, get_order_queue_position and get_order_queue_positions. It has no legacy create_order, cancel_order, amend_order, decrease_order or batch_* method.

checks.claim: A June 18, 2026 changelog entry deprecates the six legacy mutation endpoints, and calls return 'Please switch to the V2 endpoints'. Earlier the legacy cost was raised to 10x V2 (POST /portfolio/orders went to 100, V2 create is 10).
checks.evidence: The June 18, 2026 entry 'Legacy order mutation endpoints deprecated' lists exactly POST /portfolio/orders, DELETE /portfolio/orders/{order_id}, POST .../decrease, POST and DELETE /portfolio/orders/batched, and POST .../amend, with the quoted message text. The June 4, 2026 entry reads: 'POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders - cost `50` to `100`' and 'The V2 endpoint costs are unchanged.' I did not call the legacy endpoint, so its current live behaviour is unverified.

checks.claim: Required: ticker, side (bid|ask), count (FixedPointCount string), price (FixedPointDollars string), time_in_force, self_trade_prevention_type. Optional: client_order_id, expiration_time (int64 Unix seconds), post_only, cancel_order_on_pause, reduce_only, subaccount (>=0), order_group_id, exchange_index. None of the legacy fields exist.
checks.evidence: The CreateOrderV2Request 'required' list matches exactly. Its properties match: expiration_time 'Optional Unix timestamp in seconds' and subaccount minimum 0. The SDK model create_order_v2_request.py __properties = [ticker, client_order_id, side, count, price, expiration_time, time_in_force, post_only, self_trade_prevention_type, cancel_order_on_pause, reduce_only, subaccount, order_group_id, exchange_index]. There is no type, action, yes_price, count_fp, buy_max_cost or expiration_ts.

checks.claim: V2 quotes on the YES leg. bid = buy YES at price; ask = sell YES at price, which is the same as buying NO at 1-price. To buy NO at $0.12, send side ask, price '0.8800'. To exit a YES long, send ask with reduce_only plus IOC.
checks.evidence: The BookSide schema description is quoted verbatim correctly. Independent: Order.book_side says ''bid' is equivalent to outcome_side 'yes'; 'ask' is equivalent to outcome_side 'no'', and order_direction.md says 'bid ≡ yes, ask ≡ no, always'. The worked examples are derivations, not quoted docs, but they are consistent.
checks.corrected_fact: Safety detail the research left out: when you are flat, an ask order ties up (1 - price) x count of collateral, because it is a NO buy. Budget and max-loss checks must use this, not price x count. reduce_only is only accepted with immediate_or_cancel, so a RESTING exit ask cannot be reduce-only. If the YES position is already gone when it fills, it opens a NO position.

checks.claim: price and every *_dollars field are dollar strings, not cents. Requests accept 2-4 decimals and responses emit up to 6. Format with 4 decimals; '0.5' is outside the documented format.
checks.evidence: FixedPointDollars: 'Fixed-point US dollar string. Most request fields accept 2-4 decimal places (e.g., "0.56", "0.5600"); responses emit up to 6.' The SDK types price as StrictStr. Live public GETs show sub-cent prices: KXBTC15M-26OCT051430-30 yes_bid_dollars '0.9290', and resting levels at '0.0010'.
checks.corrected_fact: The source says 'Most' request fields accept 2-4 decimals, not all of them. Always sending 4 decimals stays within the documented range.

checks.claim: V2 count is a fixed-point contract string. Requests accept 0-2 decimals; responses always have 2. The step is 0.01. V2 responses name the fields fill_count and remaining_count (no _fp suffix) but they are still FixedPointCount strings. The Order object uses *_fp names.
checks.evidence: The FixedPointCount description is verbatim as quoted. CreateOrderV2Response.fill_count and remaining_count are $ref FixedPointCount. Order has fill_count_fp, remaining_count_fp and initial_count_fp. The SDK types count as StrictStr. The Quick Start example sends count '1' with no decimals.

checks.claim: Fractional contracts have been supported on every active market since Apr 17, 2026. fractional_trading_enabled was deprecated then and removed on July 9, 2026. Live book sizes are fractional.
checks.evidence: The Apr 17, 2026 changelog says 'the field is always `true`'. The July 9, 2026 entry removed Market.fractional_trading_enabled. The Market schema in 3.32.0 has no such field, and live GET /markets responses do not contain it. Live sizes are fractional: KXBTC15M yes_bid_size_fp '4332.26' and yes_ask_size_fp '1181.73'.

checks.claim: V2 documents no minimum order size or notional. The step is 0.01, so '0.01' is presumably the smallest count. 'minimum: 1, whole contracts only' applies only to the legacy integer count.
checks.evidence: I searched openapi.yaml, the getting_started guides and the changelog. The only count constraints are 'minimum granularity is 0.01 contracts' (FixedPointCount and fixed_point_migration.md) and the legacy CreateOrderRequest.count 'minimum: 1 ... (whole contracts only)'. Whether '0.01' is actually accepted is still unverified; testing it needs an order.

checks.claim: Market.price_ranges ({start,end,step} dollar strings) is the authoritative tick grid. Off-grid prices are rejected. price_level_structure is only a label. Whole-cent prices are valid in every structure.
checks.evidence: fixed_point_migration.md (last updated Aug 20, 2026) is quoted verbatim, including 'Whole-cent prices are valid in every structure.' The Market schema requires price_ranges and price_level_structure. The PriceRange fields start, end and step are strings in dollars.

checks.claim: tapered_deci_cent: $0.001 on $0-0.10, $0.01 on $0.10-0.90, $0.001 on $0.90-1.00. Also linear_cent, deci_cent, the center_{x}_edge_{y}_cent family, and center_deci_edge_centi_cent ($0.0001 below $0.01 and above $0.99; used by all combo markets).
checks.evidence: The table in fixed_point_migration.md matches. A live KXBTC15M/KXGOLD15M price_ranges response is exactly [{0.0000-0.1000 step 0.0010},{0.1000-0.9000 step 0.0100},{0.9000-1.0000 step 0.0010}].
checks.corrected_fact: center_deci_edge_centi_cent uses a $0.001 tick between $0.01 and $0.99 and $0.0001 at the edges. The doc names combo markets as an example ('for example, multivariate (combo) markets use center_deci_edge_centi_cent'), not as a rule for all combos. The family also has center_whole_edge_half_cent, center_whole_edge_quint_cent, center_half_edge_half_cent, center_half_edge_quint_cent, center_half_edge_deci_cent, center_quint_edge_quint_cent, center_quint_edge_deci_cent and center_centi_edge_centi_cent. As the doc says, read price_ranges and do not branch on the label.

checks.claim: KXBTC15M and KXGOLD15M: exchange_index 2, tapered_deci_cent, 3 bands. KXUSDJPY15M and KXTEMPMIAH: exchange_index 0, linear_cent, one band with step '0.0100'. An empty bid side shows '0.0000' with size '0.00'.
checks.evidence: I re-ran public GETs on 2026-10-05 around 18:15-18:25Z. KXBTC15M-26OCT051415-15 and -051430-30: exchange_index 2, tapered_deci_cent, notional_value_dollars '1.0000', status 'active'. KXGOLD15M-26OCT051430-30: exchange_index 2, tapered. KXUSDJPY15M-26OCT051430-30: exchange_index 0, linear_cent, [{0.0000-1.0000 step 0.0100}]. KXTEMPMIAH-26OCT0515-T91.99: exchange_index 0, linear_cent, yes_bid_dollars '0.0000', yes_bid_size_fp '0.00'. The cited tickers KXBTC15M-26OCT051400-00 and KXUSDJPY15M-26OCT051415-30 exist (now finalized). The research's exact price snapshots cannot be re-checked.
checks.corrected_fact: An empty ASK side is reported as yes_ask_dollars '1.0000'. I saw this on KXGOLD15M-26OCT051415-15 right after close. Treat '0.0000' bids and '1.0000' asks as 'no quote', never as tradable prices.

checks.claim: $0 and $1 are invalid prices (documented for FIX; REST presumably the same). On tapered_deci_cent the valid range is 0.0010-0.9990; on linear_cent it is 0.0100-0.9900.
checks.evidence: The July 2, 2026 changelog has the quoted text 'Invalid price (off-tick, out-of-band, `$0`, or `$1`): `Text<58>=INVALID_PRICE`'. It concerns FIX cancel/replace rejects. Live data matches the ranges: KXBTC15M has resting bids at '0.0010' and closed with yes_bid '0.9990', and linear_cent KXTEMPMIAH has yes_ask '0.0100'. I found no explicit REST statement that $0 or $1 is rejected, so medium confidence is right.

checks.claim: time_in_force is required. Values are fill_or_kill, good_till_canceled and immediate_or_cancel. REST has no Day or GTD (FIX does). For an expiring order, send GTC plus expiration_time. IOC cannot be combined with expiration_time.
checks.evidence: The CreateOrderV2Request.time_in_force enum is [fill_or_kill, good_till_canceled, immediate_or_cancel], and the expiration_time description says 'The `immediate_or_cancel` time-in-force value cannot be combined with `expiration_time`.' The FIX order-entry TimeInForce(59) values are '0=Day ... 1=GTC, 3=IOC, 4=FOK, 6=GTD'. The Nov 21, 2025 changelog lists the reject messages 'Expiration timestamp must be in the future' and 'Cannot specify both immediate_or_cancel and expiration_ts'.

checks.claim: The V2 request field expiration_time is int64 Unix SECONDS (legacy name expiration_ts). Order.expiration_time is an RFC3339 string. WebSocket user_orders uses expiration_ts_ms in milliseconds.
checks.evidence: CreateOrderV2Request.expiration_time is type integer, format int64, 'Unix timestamp in seconds'. Order.expiration_time is type string, format date-time. The AsyncAPI user_orders expiration_ts_ms is 'Unix timestamp in milliseconds'. The SDK types it as Optional[StrictInt].
checks.corrected_fact: Past expiration timestamps are rejected, not converted to IOC (Nov 21, 2025 changelog). On amend, 'A nonzero expiry must be in the future.'

checks.claim: post_only is a plain boolean. A crossing post-only order is cancelled, never filled, and reported as PostOnlyCrossCancel (REST and WebSocket) or POST_ONLY_CROSS (FIX). The legacy batch endpoint returns 'invalid order' / 'post only cross'. The V2 single-create response is undocumented.
checks.evidence: CreateOrderV2Request.post_only is 'type: boolean' with no description. The June 4, 2026 changelog quote is verbatim. The AsyncAPI user_orders last_update_reason enum includes PostOnlyCrossCancel. The FIX order-entry Text values say 'POST_ONLY_CROSS - maps to ExecutionType "Canceled"'. The Oct 24, 2025 entry is verbatim and adds: 'This makes the batch endpoint consistent with single order creation.' That means single create also returned that error, at least on the legacy endpoint.
checks.corrected_fact: The June 4, 2026 entry lists the affected surfaces as GET /portfolio/orders, GET /portfolio/order/{orderId} and the orderbook_delta WebSocket channel. The 3.32.0 Order schema has no last_update_reason, so REST visibility is unconfirmed. Handle both outcomes on V2 create: a 4xx error with code 'invalid order' and details 'post only cross', or a 201 with fill_count '0.00' and remaining_count '0.00'.

checks.claim: reduce_only caps the order at the current position. It is accepted only with IOC. If there is no position, the update reports ReduceOnlyCancel.
checks.evidence: The spec description is quoted verbatim. The Oct 1, 2026 changelog says: 'Reduce-only orders with no position to reduce report `ReduceOnlyCancel` (previously `Decrease` on Margin).' FIX REDUCE_ONLY reads 'reduce-only order canceled because there was no position to reduce'.

checks.claim: Required in V2. Values: taker_at_cross, maker.
checks.evidence: The SelfTradePreventionType enum is [taker_at_cross, maker], with the description quoted verbatim. It is in the CreateOrderV2Request required list, and the SDK validates the same.
checks.corrected_fact: FOK caveat (Sep 25, 2025 changelog): 'partial fills generated by self-crossing FoK orders are not rolled back.' A FOK that hits your own resting order can partially fill, so FOK is not strictly all-or-none.

checks.claim: client_order_id is optional. A duplicate is rejected with 409, so retries are idempotent. REST gives no max length or charset. FIX says max 64 and 'must not match any open order'. FCM says unique among live and recent orders. GET /portfolio/orders cannot filter by client_order_id.
checks.evidence: The Quick Start says '409 Conflict: Order with this `client_order_id` already exists', and CreateOrderV2 lists 409 ConflictError. No REST schema gives a length or charset. FIX order-entry reads: 'UUID preferred, max 64 chars. Must not match any open order.' The Sep 3, 2026 changelog says IDs are 'only unique within a subtrader among live and recent orders'. The GetOrders parameters have no client_order_id.
checks.corrected_fact: The dedup window is undocumented for REST, and FIX only promises uniqueness against OPEN orders. A retried IOC/FOK whose first attempt already executed or cancelled may NOT be rejected, which would double-fill. After a timeout or 5xx, reconcile first (GET /portfolio/orders?ticker=..., match client_order_id) before resending.

checks.claim: exchange_index is optional on create; when omitted the order auto-routes by ticker, and -1 forces auto-routing. Auto-routing adds latency and bills every shard's Write bucket. Pass the market's own exchange_index (2 for BTC/gold, 0 for FX/weather).
checks.evidence: The spec description is quoted verbatim. exchange_sharding.md says 'Automatic routing will incur an additional latency cost.' The Aug 27, 2026 changelog says auto-routing is on by default. The live values (2 and 0) were re-checked through public GET /markets and /series/KXBTC15M (exchange_index 2).

checks.claim: Collateral is checked per shard. API orders do not move cash between shards, and only App/Web orders do. Shards: 0 default, 1 combos, 2 crypto and commodities, 3 tennis/baseball/basketball. balance_breakdown gives per-shard dollar strings. Fund in the UI or with intra_exchange_instance_transfer, whose amount is in centicents.
checks.evidence: exchange_sharding.md: 'Programmatic traders must preallocate collateral on a given exchange shard before order placement.' Only App/Web orders are described as auto-transferring. The public GET /exchange/status returned exchange_index_statuses with descriptions 'Default', 'Combos', 'Crypto & Commodities' and 'Tennis, Baseball, Basketball'. IntraExchangeInstanceTransferRequest.amount is 'The amount to transfer in centicents' (int64). IndexedBalance.balance is FixedPointDollars.
checks.corrected_fact: The research missed an opt-in auto-rebalance. POST /portfolio/target_balance_allocation takes {allocations:[{exchange_index, percent}], resting_margin_reservation}, and every 10 seconds Kalshi transfers funds back toward those targets. The transfer request also needs source/destination ExchangeInstance plus source_exchange_shard and destination_exchange_shard. GET /portfolio/balance 'balance' and 'portfolio_value' include ALL shards unless you pass exchange_index. Check shard-2 funds through balance_breakdown or ?exchange_index=2 before placing BTC or gold orders.

checks.claim: The 201 body is lightweight. Required: order_id, fill_count, remaining_count, ts_ms. Optional: client_order_id, average_fill_price, and average_fee_paid (per contract, present only when filled). There is no status field. For IOC, remaining_count is the final value.
checks.evidence: In the CreateOrderV2Response schema, required = [order_id, fill_count, remaining_count, ts_ms]. average_fee_paid: 'Volume-weighted average fee paid per contract ... Only present when fill_count > 0'. remaining_count: 'For IOC orders, this reflects the final state'. ts_ms is 'Matching engine timestamp ... Unix epoch milliseconds'.

checks.claim: The error body is ErrorResponse {code, message, details} (branch on code; 'service' was removed in Aug 2026). A 429 body is {"error":"too many requests"}. The docs list no REST code values for order rejects; only FIX Text values hint at them.
checks.evidence: Live public GETs show the ErrorResponse is WRAPPED. A 404 returned {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"not found"}}, and a bad status filter returned a 400 of {"error":{"code":"bad_request","message":"bad request","details":"invalid status filter"}}. A parameter-validation 400 (limit=5000) returned {"msg":"Parameter validation failed for GetMarkets: ..."} with no code. The changelog does list REST order-reject codes: Jan 26, 2026 gives invalid_order (generic), invalid_order_size, available_balance_too_low, order_id_and_client_order_id_mismatch, order_side_mismatch and order_ticker_mismatch; Oct 24, 2025 gives code 'invalid order' with details 'post only cross'. The 'service' field removal is confirmed (Aug 6, 2026).
checks.corrected_fact: Parse error bodies defensively. body['error'] can be an object {code, message, details} (normal errors), a string ('too many requests' on 429), or missing with a top-level 'msg' (request validation). The OpenAPI RateLimitError response points at ErrorResponse, which contradicts the rate-limit guide. The envelope shape was seen on public endpoints; for order endpoints it is inferred. Known REST codes: invalid_order, invalid_order_size, available_balance_too_low, order_id_and_client_order_id_mismatch, order_side_mismatch, order_ticker_mismatch, and 'invalid order'/'post only cross'. These codes come from legacy-era changelog entries, so their V2 strings may differ.

checks.claim: Market orders are gone. type was removed on Feb 11, 2026, and every V2 order is a limit order. Order objects still carry type limit|market. The help center still describes market orders.
checks.evidence: The Feb 11, 2026 changelog is quoted verbatim. The Order.type enum is [limit, market], and CreateOrderV2Request has no type. The help-center Order Types page (fetched, last updated June 3, 2026) says 'A market order executes immediately at the best available price in the order book.'

checks.claim: The legacy CreateOrderRequest stays in components with side/action, count/count_fp, yes_price/no_price in integer cents 1-99, *_dollars, expiration_ts, buy_max_cost in cents with FoK, sell_position_floor accepting only 0, and exchange_index (default 0, no auto-routing). FIX MaxExecutionCost is tag 21009, in dollars.
checks.evidence: The CreateOrderRequest schema matches field by field: yes_price minimum 1, maximum 99; buy_max_cost 'Maximum cost in cents ... Fill-or-Kill'; sell_position_floor 'Only accepts value of 0'. FIX order-entry: '21009 | MaxExecutionCost | Decimal | ... Max execution cost in dollars'. No path references the schema.
checks.corrected_fact: Minor: the legacy exchange_index was 'Defaults to 0. Use -1 to auto-route by market ticker', so auto-routing was available through -1.

checks.claim: DELETE /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}, no body. Query parameters: subaccount, exchange_index, market_ticker. The 200 body is {order_id, client_order_id, reduced_by (FixedPointCount), ts_ms}. Cost 2. With no exchange_index and no market_ticker, the cancel goes to shard 0.
checks.evidence: The CancelOrderV2 parameters are OrderIdPath, SubaccountQueryDefaultPrimary (in: query) and exchange_index/market_ticker in the query. The exchange_index description is quoted verbatim. The x-mint note reads 'Rate limit: 2 tokens per request'. In CancelOrderV2Response, required = [order_id, reduced_by, ts_ms].
checks.corrected_fact: The only documented cancel responses are 200, 401, 404 and 500. A misrouted cancel probably returns 404 (inference). Never treat a cancel 404 as proof that the order is gone; reconcile with GET /portfolio/orders?ticker=... After close_time, cancels are rejected with MARKET_INACTIVE (market_lifecycle.md).

checks.claim: POST /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}/amend with subaccount in the query. Required: ticker, side, price, count (new TOTAL). Optional: client_order_id, updated_client_order_id, expiration_time (omit to keep, 0 to clear; added Oct 1, 2026), exchange_index. The 200 body is {order_id, client_order_id, remaining_count, fill_count, average_fill_price, average_fee_paid, ts_ms}.
checks.evidence: AmendOrderV2Request required = [ticker, side, price, count]. count is 'Set this to the order's already filled count plus the desired resting remaining count'. expiration_time has minimum 0: 'Omit to preserve ... 0 to remove it'. The Oct 1, 2026 'Amend order expiry' entry confirms the date.
checks.corrected_fact: AmendOrderV2Response requires only order_id and ts_ms. remaining_count and fill_count are nullable and 'Only present when the amend caused a fill or changed the resting size', so code must not assume they are there. A nonzero expiration_time must be in the future. side and ticker must match the original order: the legacy amend rejected mismatches with order_side_mismatch and order_ticker_mismatch (Jan 26, 2026).

checks.claim: An expiry-only amend or a size decrease keeps queue priority. A price change or size increase goes to the back of the queue.
checks.evidence: The AmendOrderV2 x-mint note is verbatim. The Oct 1, 2026 changelog adds: 'Send the current price and total quantity for an expiry-only amendment; queue priority is preserved.'

checks.claim: POST /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}/decrease with subaccount in the query. The body takes exactly one of reduce_by or reduce_to (FixedPointCount), plus optional exchange_index and market_ticker. The 200 body is {order_id, client_order_id, remaining_count, ts_ms}.
checks.evidence: The DecreaseOrderV2Request properties are reduce_by, reduce_to, exchange_index and market_ticker, all in the BODY. In DecreaseOrderV2Response, required = [order_id, remaining_count, ts_ms]. The May 12, 2026 changelog says 'reduce_by supported on V2 decrease endpoint'.

checks.claim: POST /portfolio/events/orders/batched with {orders:[CreateOrderV2Request]}. The 201 body has a per-item result with an error field, and ts_ms is absent on errored items. Cost is 10 per order, billed to the unscoped Write bucket.
checks.evidence: The BatchCreateOrdersV2 schemas and x-mint note are verbatim. In the item schema, ts_ms reads 'Absent when the request errored' and error is ErrorResponse. rate_limits.md: 'Batch REST creates and cancels always bill their total per-order cost to your unscoped Write bucket, regardless of exchange_index.'

checks.claim: No fixed maximum batch size is published. The whole batch must fit in the bucket. By inference: Basic allows about 10 creates or 50 cancels per batch; Advanced about 90 creates.
checks.evidence: The op description reads 'maximum batch size scales with your tier's write budget'. rate_limits.md says 'Basic-tier Write buckets hold one second of budget' (100 tokens) and 'Write buckets above the Basic tier, hold up to three seconds' (Advanced 900 tokens). With create costing 10 and cancel 2, the inference holds. Still medium confidence, since no hard number is published.

checks.claim: DELETE /portfolio/events/orders/batched with a JSON body {orders:[{order_id, subaccount, exchange_index, market_ticker}]}. The 200 body has per-item reduced_by (zero on error), ts_ms and error. Cost is 2 per order.
checks.evidence: The BatchCancelOrdersV2Request and Response schemas are verbatim: reduced_by is 'Zero if the cancel errored' and ts_ms is 'Absent when the cancel errored'. The x-mint note gives '2 tokens per order' and includes the warning 'each order must include `market_ticker`' for auto-routing.

checks.claim: DELETE /portfolio/events/orders with optional subaccount. It cancels resting orders on all shards and returns 204. Cost 2. Orders placed in the following minute may also be cancelled.
checks.evidence: The CancelAllOrders description, 204 response and x-mint '2 tokens per request' are verbatim. The changelog entries of Aug 27, 2026 (new endpoint, 'Newly placed orders may also be cancelled during the minute after the request') and Sep 3, 2026 (cost lowered to the single-cancel cost) agree.
checks.corrected_fact: The description scopes it to 'the authenticated Direct member'. Whether a retail kalshi.com account counts as a Direct member is not stated anywhere I found.

checks.claim: GET /portfolio/orders parameters: ticker, event_ticker (comma list, max 10), min_ts/max_ts, status, limit 1-1000 (default 100), cursor, subaccount (omit for all), exchange_index (omit for all). Orders older than orders_updated_ts (about 2 weeks) are only in /historical/orders.
checks.evidence: The parameter definitions match: MultipleEventTickerQuery 'maximum 10', LimitQuery min 1, max 1000, default 100, and ExchangeIndexFilterQuery 'Omit to return results from all exchange shards'. A live public GET /historical/cutoff returned orders_updated_ts '2026-09-21T00:00:00Z', 14 days before today. GetHistoricalOrders parameters are ticker, min_ts, max_ts, limit, cursor and subaccount.
checks.corrected_fact: The Sep 24, 2026 changelog says 'Orders historical cutoff advances independently'. Read GET /historical/cutoff at runtime instead of assuming two weeks.

checks.claim: GET /portfolio/orders/{order_id} returns {order: Order}. Cost 2. Only order_id is documented; there is no exchange_index.
checks.evidence: The GetOrder parameters are only OrderIdPath. The x-mint note says 'Rate limit: 2 tokens per request'. GetOrderResponse is required [order]. Whether it finds shard-2 orders without routing is still unverifiable.

checks.claim: Order fields and units as listed (outcome_side/book_side; side/action deprecated; *_dollars strings; *_fp counts; RFC3339 times). Integer fields were removed from all REST and WS responses on Mar 12, 2026.
checks.evidence: The Order schema's required list and properties match exactly, including subaccount_number and exchange_index. The *_fees_dollars and *_fill_cost_dollars fields are FixedPointDollars.
checks.corrected_fact: The last sentence is overbroad. The bulk removal was Mar 12, 2026, but some legacy fields were temporarily restored on Mar 11 and finally removed effective Apr 2, 2026. GET /portfolio/balance still returns integer-cent 'balance' and 'portfolio_value'.

checks.claim: REST status values are resting, canceled and executed. 'pending' was removed Nov 2025. WS adds 'unknown'. A partial IOC presumably ends as 'canceled' with fill_count_fp > 0.
checks.evidence: The OrderStatus enum is [resting, canceled, executed]. The Nov 20, 2025 entry is 'Removing pending from status enum'. The AsyncAPI user_orders status enum is [resting, canceled, executed, unknown]. The partial-IOC ending is still inference; FIX 'Canceled<4>: Canceled (may have partial fills)' supports it.

checks.claim: Legacy (action, side) maps to (outcome_side, book_side) as in the table. The deprecated fields will not be removed before May 28, 2026.
checks.evidence: The order_direction.md table is verbatim, along with 'will not be removed before May 28, 2026'.
checks.corrected_fact: Docs inconsistency: OpenAPI Order/Fill and AsyncAPI user_orders say these fields 'will not be removed before May 14, 2026'. Both dates have passed, so side, action and is_yes can disappear at any time. Read only outcome_side and book_side.

checks.claim: GET /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/queue_position returns {queue_position_fp}. GET /portfolio/orders/queue_positions takes market_tickers, event_ticker and subaccount and returns {queue_positions:[{order_id, market_ticker, queue_position_fp}]}.
checks.evidence: The GetOrderQueuePositionResponse, OrderQueuePosition and GetOrderQueuePositionsResponse schemas match. queue_position_fp is FixedPointCount, 'The number of preceding shares before the order in the queue'.

checks.claim: There are separate Read and Write buckets. Budgets (Read/Write): Basic 200/100, Advanced 300/300, Expert 600/600, Premier 1200/1200, Paragon 2400/2400, Prime 4800/4800, Prestige 12000/9600. The Basic Write bucket holds 1 second; higher tiers hold 3 seconds.
checks.evidence: The rate_limits.md tier table and bucket text match. These are the post-Sep 24, 2026 values: that changelog raised only Premier and above by 20%.

checks.claim: Token costs: V2 create 10, cancel 2, batch create 10 per order, batch cancel 2 per order, cancel-all 2, GET order 2. Inferred: amend 10 and decrease 10.
checks.evidence: The x-mint notes give cancel 2, batch 10 and 2 per item, cancel-all 2 and GetOrder 2. The amend and decrease values are now directly backed by the June 4, 2026 entry ('10x the corresponding V2 ... costs'): legacy amend and decrease went '50 to 100', so V2 amend and decrease = 10. The June 1 entry (5x: 50) agrees. The default cost is 10 per rate_limits.md.

checks.claim: A 429 returns {"error": "too many requests"}, with no Retry-After or X-RateLimit headers and no cooldown. Use exponential backoff.
checks.evidence: rate_limits.md, 'When you hit the limit', is verbatim. During this check, a public unauthenticated GET also returned 429 after about 5 requests in 2 seconds. I did not capture that body.
checks.corrected_fact: The OpenAPI components.responses.RateLimitError schema is ErrorResponse {code, message, details}, which contradicts the guide. Accept both shapes.

checks.claim: Single REST create, cancel, decrease and amend with exchange_index >= 1 bill that shard. Index 0 bills unscoped. Auto-routed calls bill every shard. Batches bill unscoped.
checks.evidence: The rate_limits.md 'Predictions per-shard Write budgets' text is verbatim. The exchange_sharding.md FAQ: 'Auto-routed single REST order writes are billed to the unscoped Write bucket and every nonzero shard's Write bucket.'

checks.claim: New accounts start at Basic. Advanced is self-serve through POST /account/api_usage_level/upgrade (30 tokens) once 1 of the last 100 orders came through the API. GET /account/limits returns {usage_tier, read, write, grants}.
checks.evidence: The UpgradeAccountApiUsageLevel description and x-mint '30 tokens' match, and its 403 reads 'No API-created order was found in the user's latest 100 Predictions orders'. GetAccountApiLimitsResponse required = [usage_tier, read, write, grants]. rate_limits.md: 'Basic: complete account signup.'

checks.claim: No published limit on open orders. Up to 100,000 order groups. contracts_limit is 1 to 1,000,000 per rolling 15 seconds. Per-market risk limits exist but have no published values.
checks.evidence: I searched the spec, guides and changelog and found no open-order cap. The CreateOrderGroup description says 'up to 100,000 order groups' (Aug 13, 2026 entry). order_groups.md says 'contracts limit (1–1,000,000)'. FIX Text includes EXCEEDED_PER_MARKET_RISK_LIMIT.

checks.claim: POST /portfolio/order_groups/create takes {contracts_limit or contracts_limit_fp, subaccount, exchange_index (default 0)} and returns {order_group_id, subaccount, exchange_index}. Fills over the limit within 15 seconds cancel the group's orders until a reset. A group lives on one shard.
checks.evidence: The CreateOrderGroupRequest and Response schemas match. exchange_sharding.md: 'Order groups do not function across exchange instances.' order_groups.md describes the triggered state and the reset.
checks.corrected_fact: Reset, trigger and limit take exchange_index as a QUERY parameter (ExchangeIndexQuery, 'Defaults to 0'), so a shard-2 group must be reset with ?exchange_index=2. contracts_limit (integer) is 'Whole contracts only'; use contracts_limit_fp for fractional limits.

checks.claim: Thursday 3-5 AM ET trading pause: no placing or amending, but cancels work. In an exchange pause, cancels fail too. Resting orders stay unless cancel_order_on_pause is set.
checks.evidence: The maintenance_and_pauses.md table matches. The public GET /exchange/status returns per-shard trading_active and exchange_active, which works as a pre-trade check.

checks.claim: Orders need status 'active'; the filter value 'open' maps to 'active'. After close_time, all order operations including cancels are rejected with MARKET_INACTIVE, and resting orders are cancelled. Reactivation cancels resting orders.
