missing_critical: Error-body envelope. Live REST errors are wrapped: {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"not found"}} and {"error":{"code":"bad_request","message":"bad request","details":"invalid status filter"}}. Request-validation 400s return {"msg":"Parameter validation failed ..."} with no code, and a 429 is {"error":"too many requests"}. Code that reads resp.json()['code'] will crash. Parse all three shapes. These were seen on public endpoints; order endpoints are presumed to behave the same.

REST reject codes are documented, in the changelog. Jan 26, 2026 lists invalid_order (generic), invalid_order_size, available_balance_too_low, order_id_and_client_order_id_mismatch, order_side_mismatch and order_ticker_mismatch. Oct 24, 2025 gives 'invalid order' with details 'post only cross'. Nov 21, 2025 gives the messages 'Expiration timestamp must be in the future' and 'Cannot specify both immediate_or_cancel and expiration_ts'. Map these, and treat any unknown code, 5xx or timeout as 'outcome unknown, reconcile first'.

Never blind-retry POST or DELETE. The project's existing client (C:\Users\Jarvis\Documents\Kalshi-PM\src\kpm\clients\http.py) retries 429/5xx and caches responses permanently on disk. That is fine for public GETs but would double-place orders and serve stale order or portfolio data. The execution layer needs its own no-cache client. After a timeout or 503, look up the order with GET /portfolio/orders?ticker=X and match client_order_id before resending. FIX says a client order ID only has to be unique among OPEN orders, so a retried IOC/FOK that already executed may not get a 409.

Shard cash. GET /portfolio/balance 'balance' and 'portfolio_value' include ALL shards unless ?exchange_index=N is passed. BTC and gold (shard 2) need cash on shard 2, and FX and weather need it on shard 0. Check balance_breakdown before every order. There is also an opt-in auto-rebalance, POST /portfolio/target_balance_allocation, which moves funds every 10 s. Transfers need the write::transfer scope, which a trade-only key does not have.

Ask-side risk. With side='ask' you lock (1 - price) x count (a NO buy when flat), not price x count. Size limits and max-loss checks must use the correct leg. reduce_only only works with IOC, so a RESTING exit ask can open a NO position if the YES position is already gone (fills, settlement).
FOK is not all-or-none against your own orders. Sep 25, 2025 changelog: 'partial fills generated by self-crossing FoK orders are not rolled back'.

15-minute market timing. KXBTC15M has can_close_early: true, so close_time can move earlier. After close, even cancels are rejected (MARKET_INACTIVE). Set expiration_time well before close_time and never rely on a last-second cancel. Live, the status=open listing briefly returned a just-closed market (status 'closed') at the 18:15Z boundary. Always check status == 'active' and close_time on your side, and re-fetch GET /markets/{ticker} before sending.

Quote sanity. An empty side shows yes_bid_dollars '0.0000' or yes_ask_dollars '1.0000'. The orderbook of a nonexistent ticker returns HTTP 200 with empty arrays. depth=N returns the N best levels, still ascending. GET /markets top of book can lag the orderbook, so price from the orderbook or WebSocket. WebSocket orderbook NO levels use NO-leg prices unless you subscribe with use_yes_price: true.
Pre-trade pause check. Public GET /exchange/status returns exchange_index_statuses[] with trading_active and exchange_active per shard. Pause checks should use it.

Reconciliation over WebSocket. URL wss://external-api-ws.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2 (demo wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2). Sign timestamp + 'GET' + '/trade-api/ws/v2'. Subscribe to user_orders and fill. The fill channel still carries an optional client_order_id, but REST fills do not. Expect disconnects during the Thursday 3-5 AM ET window.

Signing details. RSA-PSS needs MGF1(SHA-256) with salt_length = digest length (cryptography PSS.DIGEST_LENGTH) and an uppercase method. Ed25519 is recommended. The official SDK requires Python >= 3.13, but this project's venv is Python 3.12.10, so either sign directly or upgrade Python. No clock-skew tolerance is documented; keep the system clock NTP-synced.

Routing pitfalls. A cancel with no exchange_index and no market_ticker goes to shard 0, and the only documented cancel responses are 200/401/404/500. A 404 does not prove the order is gone. Order-group reset, trigger and limit take exchange_index as a query parameter that defaults to 0, so shard-2 groups need ?exchange_index=2.

Amend response. Only order_id and ts_ms are required; remaining_count and fill_count can be absent. side and ticker must match the original order. The May 21, 2026 'response may describe a different order' issue has no recorded fix, so compare the response order_id with the request and reconcile.
API key scopes default to full read+write, including transfers, when not specified. Create the key with ['read','write::trade'] explicitly. Whether the web UI offers scope selection is unverified.

Unauthenticated public reads have an undocumented rate limit. I got a 429 after about 5 requests in 2 s while the user's background downloads were running. Don't let market-data 429s block the cancel path, and prefer WebSocket or authenticated reads for live pricing.

Fees for tiny orders are not covered. KXBTC15M series fee_type is 'quadratic' with fee_multiplier 1 (public GET /series/KXBTC15M). Fees are rounded up to $0.000001, and direct-member balances align to $0.0001 with a rounding fee. On 0.01-contract orders, fees and rounding can be a large share of notional. Compute them before claiming a 25 x 0.01 live test proves anything about strategy P&L. Whether count '0.01' is accepted is still unverified.

research.area: portfolio and accounting (Kalshi Trade API v2, OpenAPI spec v3.32.0 as published on docs.kalshi.com on 2026-10-05)

facts.fact: Every *_dollars field, plus fee_cost and balance_dollars, is a FixedPointDollars STRING. In requests it takes 2-4 decimals. Responses can emit up to 6 decimals (example "0.5600"; a WS fill fee_cost example is "0.010000"). Every *_fp field is a FixedPointCount STRING that responses always emit with 2 decimals (example "10.00"). The minimum contract granularity is 0.01, and fractional fills happen even if you never send fractional orders. Parse both with Decimal, never float.
facts.quote: Fixed-point US dollar string. Most request fields accept 2-4 decimal places (e.g., "0.56", "0.5600"); responses emit up to 6. ... Fixed-point contract count string (2 decimals, e.g., "10.00" ...) ... the minimum granularity is 0.01 contracts.

facts.fact: Since Mar 7, 2026, the portfolio _dollars fields on GET /portfolio/orders, /portfolio/orders/{id}, /portfolio/fills and /portfolio/positions can carry up to 6 decimals (micro-cent source values). Do not assume 2 or 4 decimal places.
facts.quote: Selected portfolio response `_dollars` fields now emit up to `6` decimal places, using micro_cent source values

facts.fact: Response fields: balance (int64, CENTS, e.g. 1234 = $12.34); balance_dollars (FixedPointDollars string, e.g. "12.3456"); portfolio_value (int64, CENTS); updated_ts (int64 Unix timestamp; seconds vs milliseconds is not stated); balance_breakdown (array of IndexedBalance {exchange_index:int, balance: FixedPointDollars string}, omitted only for subaccount-restricted keys). Required fields: balance, balance_dollars, portfolio_value, updated_ts. Query parameters: subaccount (0 primary, 1-63; default 0) and exchange_index. Both values cover all exchange indexes unless exchange_index is passed.
facts.quote: balance: Member's available balance in cents for the requested account and exchange index. It includes all exchange indexes when `exchange_index` is omitted. ... balance_dollars: Member's available balance as a fixed-point dollar string ... portfolio_value: Member's portfolio value in cents ... updated_ts: Unix timestamp of the last update to the balance.

facts.fact: Since May 28, 2026, direct-member balances sit on a $0.0001 grid. The integer-cent balance field truncates the sub-cent part, so the accounting layer should treat balance_dollars as the source of truth. The official quick start converts the legacy field as balance['balance'] / 100, which confirms that field is in cents.
facts.quote: direct member balances are aligned to centi-cent (`$0.0001`, or `0.01c`) precision. The legacy `balance` field truncates any sub-cent amount, so use `balance_dollars` for exact values.

facts.fact: Per the Oct 7, 2025 changelog, portfolio_value is the available balance plus the current market value of all positions, in cents. Default scoping changed twice: the Aug 13, 2026 entry scoped it to exchange_index 0, and the Aug 20, 2026 entry made all-index totals the default again. The current OpenAPI spec says all indexes unless exchange_index is given.
facts.quote: `GET /trade-api/v2/portfolio/balance` returns `balance` and `portfolio_value` across all exchange indexes by default. Pass `exchange_index` to scope both values to one exchange index.

facts.fact: GET /portfolio/balance also accepts an API key that only has the 'read::portfolio_balance' child scope, which suits a read-only accounting process. The API key scopes include read, write, read::portfolio_balance, write::trade and write::transfer.
facts.quote: This endpoint also accepts API keys with the 'read::portfolio_balance' scope.

facts.fact: The docs do not confirm whether 'available balance' is net of collateral reserved for resting orders. The exchange-sharding page says auto-rebalancing computes 'account balance minus the value of its resting orders', which suggests some views of balance include resting value. Test it with the first tiny order: read balance_dollars before and after placing a resting order.
facts.quote: Every 10 seconds, Kalshi computes the customer's balance on each exchange shard as its account balance minus the value of its resting orders.

facts.fact: In the web and app UI, Cash already includes a 'Credit' amount, which is a nonwithdrawable credit balance. Cash can also differ from the amount you can withdraw. The docs do not say whether API balance or balance_dollars includes non-withdrawable credits.
facts.quote: Credit shows your nonwithdrawable credit balance. This amount is already included in Cash, so do not add it again when calculating your portfolio total.

facts.fact: In GET /portfolio/subaccounts/balances, SubaccountBalance.balance is a FixedPointDollars STRING; until Jan 27, 2026 it was a centi-cent integer. GetBalance uses the same field name, balance, for INTEGER CENTS. The other fields are subaccount_number (0-63), exchange_index and updated_ts (int64 Unix).
facts.quote: The subaccount balance field will be represented as a fixed-point dollars string instead of a centicent integer.

facts.fact: The matching engines are sharded, and an order is only collateralized by funds on its market's shard. The web and app move cash between shards automatically; the API does not. An API trader must pre-fund the market's shard. Live GET /exchange/status shows index 0 'Default', 1 'Combos', 2 'Crypto & Commodities' and 3 'Tennis, Baseball, Basketball'. Status fields: exchange_index_statuses[].exchange_index, description, exchange_active, trading_active, intra_exchange_transfers_active.
facts.quote: Kalshi's collateralization checks run within the matching engine. Programmatic traders must preallocate collateral on a given exchange shard before order placement.

facts.fact: Live public GET /series results on 2026-10-05: KXUSDJPY15M exchange_index=0 (category Financials); KXTEMPMIAH exchange_index=0 (Climate and Weather); KXBTC15M exchange_index=2 (Crypto). FX and Miami temperature orders draw on shard-0 cash. BTC 15-minute orders need cash moved to shard 2 first.
facts.quote: "ticker":"KXBTC15M" ... "exchange_index":2 ... "fee_type":"quadratic","fee_multiplier":1

facts.fact: POST /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfer takes amount as an INTEGER in CENTICENTS ($1.00 = 10000). Other request fields: source and destination, each 'event_contract' or 'margined'; source_exchange_shard and destination_exchange_shard, 0-100, default 0; and optional source_subaccount and destination_subaccount. Processing is asynchronous and the response is {transfer_id}. GET /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfers returns amount as a FixedPointDollars STRING, plus status 'pending'|'complete' and created_ts (int64 Unix). Its limit maxes at 500, and cursor is omitted on the last page.
facts.quote: amount: type: integer format: int64 description: The amount to transfer in centicents

facts.fact: POST /portfolio/target_balance_allocation sets allocations [{exchange_index:int, percent:int}], which must total 100; an empty array disables rebalancing. It also takes resting_margin_reservation 'none'|'max'|'sum' (default 'sum'). Kalshi then rebalances between shards every 10 seconds. This is an alternative to manual transfers.
facts.quote: Percentages must total 100. Passing an empty allocations array disables automatic rebalancing.

facts.fact: Required MarketPosition fields: ticker; exchange_index; total_traded_dollars (string; 'Total spent on this market'); position_fp (SIGNED string: + = YES contracts, - = NO contracts, e.g. "-25.00"); market_exposure_dollars ('Cost of the aggregate market position'); realized_pnl_dollars ('Locked in profit and loss'); fees_paid_dollars ('Fees paid on fill orders'); last_updated_ts (an RFC3339 date-time STRING despite the _ts suffix).
facts.quote: position_fp: String representation of the number of contracts bought in this market. Negative means NO contracts and positive means YES contracts

facts.fact: Required EventPosition fields: event_ticker, total_cost_dollars, total_cost_shares_fp (YES plus NO shares traded on the event), event_exposure_dollars, realized_pnl_dollars and fees_paid_dollars.
facts.quote: total_cost_shares_fp: String representation of the total number of shares traded on this event (including both YES and NO contracts)

facts.fact: The legacy integer fields position, market_exposure, realized_pnl, fees_paid and total_traded are gone; integer count and integer-cent fields were removed from all REST and WS payloads on March 12, 2026. resting_orders_count stopped being returned on Nov 13, 2025 and was removed from the schema on July 9, 2026. The live public /markets/trades payload also has no integer count or price fields, which supports this.
facts.quote: Legacy integer count fields (with `_fp` equivalents) and integer cents price fields (with `_dollars` equivalents) will be **removed** from all REST and WebSocket response payloads on **March 12, 2026**

facts.fact: Query parameters: cursor; limit (1-1000, default 100); count_filter (comma list of 'position' and/or 'total_traded'); settlement_status ('unsettled' default | 'settled' | 'all', added Oct 1, 2026); ticker; event_ticker (single); subaccount (default 0, primary only); exchange_index (omit for all shards). Settled and all queries page by event ticker, and cursors are specific to each status. An empty cursor means no next page.
facts.quote: Settled and all-state positions are paginated by event ticker to keep large histories bounded. Cursors are specific to the selected settlement status.

facts.fact: Required Fill fields: fill_id, exchange_index, trade_id, order_id, ticker, market_ticker, outcome_side ('yes'|'no'), book_side ('bid'|'ask'), count_fp (string), yes_price_dollars, no_price_dollars (strings), is_taker (bool) and fee_cost (FixedPointDollars string). Optional: created_time (RFC3339), ts (int Unix seconds, legacy), subaccount_number (nullable int), and the deprecated side ('yes'|'no') and action ('buy'|'sell').
facts.quote: required: - fill_id - exchange_index - trade_id - order_id - ticker - market_ticker - outcome_side - book_side - count_fp - yes_price_dollars - no_price_dollars - is_taker - fee_cost

facts.fact: On a REST fill, trade_id is a legacy alias of fill_id and market_ticker is a legacy alias of ticker. Deduplicate on fill_id. The docs do not say whether the fill id equals the public trade id.
facts.quote: trade_id: Unique identifier for this fill (legacy field name, same as fill_id)

facts.fact: REST fills have no price, count, yes_price or no_price integer fields; they were removed Mar 12, 2026. yes_price_fixed and no_price_fixed were removed Apr 2, 2026. client_order_id was removed from REST fills on Mar 30, 2026, so join fills to orders by order_id and keep your own client_order_id-to-order_id map. The WS fill channel still carries an optional client_order_id.
facts.quote: Removed `client_order_id` from `GET /portfolio/fills` and `GET /portfolio/fills/historical` responses.

facts.fact: Direction comes from outcome_side, or the equivalent book_side (bid = yes, ask = no). The mapping is buy yes or sell no gives yes/bid, and buy no or sell yes gives no/ask. The price is the same for both parties. To update position_fp, add +count_fp when outcome_side=='yes' and -count_fp when it is 'no'. The legacy side and action are deprecated; the Fill schema says they stay until at least May 14, 2026 and the guide says May 28, 2026. Do not depend on them.
facts.quote: | buy | yes | yes | bid | / | sell | no | yes | bid | / | buy | no | no | ask | / | sell | yes | no | ask |

facts.fact: Required Settlement fields: ticker, exchange_index, event_ticker, market_result ('yes'|'no'|'scalar'), yes_count_fp, yes_total_cost_dollars, no_count_fp, no_total_cost_dollars, revenue (INTEGER CENTS, e.g. 25 winning contracts -> 2500), settled_time (RFC3339) and fee_cost (FixedPointDollars string, example '0.3400'). value is an optional, nullable INTEGER in CENTS giving the payout of one YES contract (e.g. 100 or 0). Integer-cent revenue and value cannot show sub-cent scalar payouts; use the market's settlement_value_dollars for those.

facts.fact: Settlement.fee_cost is the SUM OF TRADE FEES the user paid over that market position, not a separate settlement fee. Do not add it on top of per-fill fee_cost when computing P&L. The legacy integer-cent yes_total_cost and no_total_cost were removed Apr 2, 2026.

facts.fact: Query parameters: limit (1-1000, default 100), cursor, ticker, event_ticker (single), min_ts, max_ts (seconds) and subaccount (omitted = all). The endpoint only covers settled positions still in the live data set. After archival, GET /historical/positions has position, P&L and fee data, but no endpoint has the settlement-record fields (revenue, value). Persist settlement records locally as they arrive.
facts.quote: `GET /portfolio/settlements` reads only settled positions still in the live data set. After archival, `GET /historical/positions` provides position, realized P&L, and fee data, but there is currently no historical endpoint with the same settlement-record fields.

facts.fact: Settlement fees are zero for plain yes/no results and can only apply to sub-cent scalar settlements. In the FIX example for a direct user, the payout is floored to the $0.0001 balance grid and the residual is the settlement fee (e.g. $30.60306 payout -> $30.6030 credited, $0.00006 fee). The overview page instead says payouts round to whole cents; this research treats the $0.0001 FIX example as current for direct members.
facts.quote: Settlement fees are zero for simple yes/no determinations but may apply for sub-cent scalar settlement.

facts.fact: Direct-member balances align to $0.0001 and non-direct (FCM-cleared) balances to $0.01. Fees are 6-decimal dollar amounts. Every fill has three components: a trade fee (model fee rounded UP to $0.000001), a rounding fee (brings the balance back onto the grid) and a rebate (paid back from accumulated rounding overpayment, in grid increments). Net fee = trade fee + rounding fee - rebate, and it is never below $0.
facts.quote: Direct member balances are aligned to `$0.0001` (`0.01c`) ... Fees are six-decimal dollar amounts (`$0.000001` granularity) ... **Net fee** = trade fee + rounding fee - rebate (always >= $0.00)

facts.fact: The documented steps are: 1) trade_fee = ceil_6dp(model_fee); 2) aligned_change = floor_precision(revenue - trade_fee), where revenue is signed and negative for buyers; 3) rounding_fee = (revenue - trade_fee) - aligned_change; 4) add rounding_fee to the ORDER's accumulator; 5) rebate accumulated rounding in increments of the grid precision, capped so the fill's net fee is not negative. Worked example (non-direct): revenue -0.055000 with model fee 0.00363825 gives trade fee 0.003639, rounding fee 0.001361 and a balance change of -0.06. A local Decimal replica reproduces this exactly. For a direct member the same fill gives a rounding fee of 0.000061 and a balance change of -0.0587.
facts.quote: The fee accumulator is maintained per order across all fills regardless of whether the fills are taker or maker. If an order initially takes (matching resting orders) and then becomes a resting maker order, the accumulated rounding carries over to subsequent maker fills.

facts.fact: Under these mechanics, a direct member pays ceil_6dp(model fee) plus only enough rounding to land on the $0.0001 grid. That is not the older 'round up to the next cent per trade' rule that third-party fee guides still quote. A per-fill fee_cost can be a sub-cent value such as "0.010000" or smaller. Whether REST fee_cost is the net fee (including rounding fee and rebate) is not documented.
facts.quote: Before any rebate, the user's balance changes by `aligned_change`, which is always on the user's precision grid.

facts.fact: Series.fee_type takes 'quadratic' | 'quadratic_with_maker_fees' | 'quadratic_with_combo_maker_fees' | 'flat', and Series.fee_multiplier is a double. Maker fees apply only to the *_with_maker_fees types. The combo variant uses a 0.5 maker multiplier instead of 0.25. Events can override with fee_type_override and fee_multiplier_override (scheduled changes: GET /events/fee_changes); series changes are listed at GET /series/fee_changes (array series_fee_change_arr). Markets may carry fee_waiver_expiration_time.
facts.quote: 'quadratic' is described by the General Trading Fees Table, 'quadratic_with_maker_fees' is described by the General Trading Fees Table with maker fees described in the Maker Fees section, 'quadratic_with_combo_maker_fees' is the same maker-fee structure with a 0.5 maker multiplier instead of 0.25, 'flat' is described by the Specific Trading Fees Table.

facts.fact: Live on 2026-10-05: KXUSDJPY15M, KXTEMPMIAH and KXBTC15M all have fee_type 'quadratic' and fee_multiplier 1, and GET /series/fee_changes?show_historical=true returns an empty series_fee_change_arr for each. Because plain 'quadratic' has no maker-fee section, resting (maker) fills in these series should have a zero model fee. Under the rounding rules, only taker fills, or sub-cent revenue, would then produce a fee_cost.
facts.quote: {"series_fee_change_arr":[]}

facts.fact: The fee coefficients are not confirmed from an official source. Third-party guides give taker fee = 0.07 x C x P x (1-P) and maker fee = 0.0175 x C x P x (1-P), times fee_multiplier. The 0.0175 maker rate is consistent with the 0.25 maker multiplier in the official fee_type text. The official PDF, https://kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf, returned HTTP 429 and could not be read.
facts.quote: Fee structures can be found at https://kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf.

facts.fact: Pagination is cursor-based: pass cursor=<value from the previous response>. The end marker varies by endpoint. Positions and fills return an empty cursor, intra-transfer history omits it, and the guide says to continue 'until the cursor is null'. Stop when the cursor is falsy. limit maxes at 1000 (default 100) for fills, settlements, positions, historical endpoints and event fee changes; at 500 for deposits, withdrawals and intra-transfers; and at 10000 for /incentive_programs, which returns its cursor as next_cursor, not cursor. The guide's 'typically 1-100' and its /portfolio/history link are out of date; that endpoint does not exist in the spec.

facts.fact: NO Trade API endpoint reports per-account earned or paid incentive rewards. All 150+ paths in openapi.yaml v3.32.0 were checked. The only incentive path is the public program list, whose paid_out flag is per program. There is no rewards, credits, ledger or activity endpoint, and deposit types exclude rewards. In the API, a paid reward is visible only as an increase in balance_dollars that fills, settlements, deposits, withdrawals and transfers do not explain. The help center says developers get only program definitions.

facts.fact: Rewards are credited after a program ends, in a later batch run with variable timing, not in real time. The per-market earnings estimate in the market's Rewards popover is UI-only and not final. A reward below $1 for one program is not paid, and payouts are rounded down to the cent. A verified SSN must be on file to receive credits above the annual IRS reporting threshold, which counts referral and incentive credits together.

facts.fact: Current scoring per the help center, modified 2026-09-25: one book snapshot per second at a random moment. The Reference Price is found by walking down from the best bid to the first level where cumulative size reaches 1/5 of the Target Size. Only orders that help reach the Target Size on their side qualify. An order's score is size x DiscountFactor^(ticks below the Reference Price). Scores are normalized per side, so one snapshot is worth at most 2.0. A snapshot is excluded unless BOTH sides reach the Target Size. Reward = your period share x period reward x (non-excluded snapshots / total snapshots), rounded down to the cent. Target Size is >100 and <20,000; periods are up to 31 days; the program ends Jan 1, 2027. Eligibility excludes non-US users and IB/FCM customers.
facts.quote: Your reward = Your Time Period Score × Time Period Reward × (non-excluded snapshots ÷ total snapshots), rounded down to the nearest cent

facts.fact: The CFTC-filed terms of Feb 11, 2026 (effective Feb 28, 2026) differ from the current help summary. They set the Reference Yes Price to the highest yes bid, run the program until Sep 1, 2026, set the Time Period Reward floor at $10/day, and explicitly exclude members who signed a Market Maker Agreement. The help page says the program ends Jan 1, 2027 and uses the 1/5-of-Target reference price, so a later amendment exists. That amendment is posted only at kalshi.com/regulatory/notices, which returned HTTP 429.

code_examples.purpose: Unit normalisation helpers for every portfolio and accounting field type: cents ints, centi-cent ints, fixed-point dollar strings and _fp count strings. Always use Decimal.

Local copy of Kalshi's documented fill fee-rounding steps 1-3; the per-order rebate accumulator is not modelled. Run in the project .venv, it reproduced the doc's worked example exactly: (0.003639, 0.001361, -0.06). The same fill for a direct member gives (0.003639, 0.000061, -0.0587).
code_examples.code:
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_FLOOR
MICRO = Decimal("0.000001")

def fill_fee_components(revenue: Decimal, model_fee: Decimal, precision: Decimal):
    """revenue: signed price*qty in dollars (negative for buyers).
    precision: Decimal('0.0001') direct member, Decimal('0.01') non-direct (FCM-cleared)."""
    trade_fee = model_fee.quantize(MICRO, rounding=ROUND_CEILING)        # 1) ceil_6dp
    raw = revenue - trade_fee
    aligned_change = raw.quantize(precision, rounding=ROUND_FLOOR)        # 2) floor to balance grid
    rounding_fee = raw - aligned_change                                   # 3) goes to ORDER accumulator
    return trade_fee, rounding_fee, aligned_change                        # 5) rebates (grid increments,
                                                                          #    net fee >= 0) not modelled

print(fill_fee_components(Decimal("-0.055000"), Decimal("0.00363825"), Decimal("0.01")))
# -> (Decimal('0.003639'), Decimal('0.001361'), Decimal('-0.06'))

code_examples.purpose: One pagination generator for every list endpoint. /incentive_programs names its cursor next_cursor; the other endpoints use cursor. The end of the list can be an empty string, null or a missing key.
code_examples.code:
def pages(get_json, path, params, items_key, cursor_field="cursor"):
    cursor = None
    while True:
        q = dict(params)
        if cursor:
            q["cursor"] = cursor
        body = get_json(path, q)                 # your signed (or public) GET helper
        yield from body.get(items_key) or []
        cursor = body.get(cursor_field)
        if not cursor:                           # "", None, or absent all mean done
            return

# fills since t0 (min_ts is Unix SECONDS; subaccount omitted = all subaccounts):
#   pages(get, "/portfolio/fills", {"min_ts": t0, "limit": 1000}, "fills")
# settlements (live data set only - persist locally):
#   pages(get, "/portfolio/settlements", {"limit": 1000}, "settlements")
# positions (response also has 'event_positions'; subaccount defaults to 0):
#   pages(get, "/portfolio/positions", {"settlement_status": "all", "limit": 1000}, "market_positions")
# public LIP programs (market_ticker filter is ignored server-side -> filter here):
#   [p for p in pages(get, "/incentive_programs", {"status": "active", "type": "liquidity", "limit": 1000},
#                     "incentive_programs", cursor_field="next_cursor") if p["market_ticker"] == tkr]

code_examples.purpose: Turn a REST or WS fill into a ledger row using the canonical direction fields. outcome_side 'yes' adds to position_fp and 'no' subtracts from it. The fee comes straight from the fill's fee_cost.
code_examples.code:
from decimal import Decimal

def fill_row(f: dict) -> dict:
    q = Decimal(f["count_fp"])
    long_yes = f["outcome_side"] == "yes"            # same bit as book_side == "bid"
    px_side = Decimal(f["yes_price_dollars"] if long_yes else f["no_price_dollars"])  # REST only;
    # WS fills carry only yes_price_dollars -> no price = 1 - yes price
    return {
        "fill_id": f.get("fill_id") or f["trade_id"],  # REST trade_id == fill_id (legacy alias)
        "order_id": f["order_id"],                       # REST fills no longer carry client_order_id
        "ticker": f.get("ticker") or f["market_ticker"],
        "exchange_index": f["exchange_index"],
        "position_delta": q if long_yes else -q,         # matches MarketPosition.position_fp sign
        "side_cost": px_side * q,                        # cost of side gained, before netting/collateral return
        "fee": Decimal(f["fee_cost"]),                  # do NOT add Settlement.fee_cost again
        "maker": not f["is_taker"],
    }

code_examples.purpose: Detect LIP reward credits by reconciling the balance. No endpoint reports them, so a reward credit can only appear as an unexplained increase in balance_dollars.
code_examples.code:
from decimal import Decimal

def unexplained_cash(prev_balance: str, now_balance: str, fill_cash: Decimal, fees: Decimal,
                     settlement_payouts: Decimal, deposits: Decimal, withdrawals: Decimal,
                     transfers_in: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """All inputs in dollars. prev/now from GET /portfolio/balance 'balance_dollars' (use the same
    exchange_index scope both times). settlement_payouts from Settlement.revenue (cents/100).
    A positive residual shortly after a program flips to paid_out=true is a candidate reward credit;
    collateral-return (DIRECNET) and resting-order reservations can also move cash - log both."""
    expected = fill_cash - fees + settlement_payouts + deposits - withdrawals + transfers_in
    return (Decimal(now_balance) - Decimal(prev_balance)) - expected

open_questions: Is GET /portfolio/balance 'balance'/'balance_dollars' net of collateral reserved by resting orders? The docs only say 'available balance'. Check with the first tiny resting order: read the balance before placing it, after placing it, and after cancelling it.
Does API balance include the UI's non-withdrawable 'Credit' balance? Are LIP reward credits withdrawable cash or non-withdrawable credit?
GetBalance.updated_ts is described as an int64 'Unix timestamp' with no unit. Seconds or milliseconds is unconfirmed.
Is REST Fill.fee_cost the net fee (trade fee + rounding fee - rebate) or only the trade fee? No per-component breakdown is exposed anywhere.

The official fee coefficients (taker 0.07, maker 0.0175 x C x P x (1-P)) come from third-party sources. kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf returned HTTP 429. Confirm whether maker fills in plain 'quadratic' series (KXUSDJPY15M, KXTEMPMIAH, KXBTC15M) really have fee_cost 0 by checking the first real maker fill.
Is the multi-ticker filter on GET /portfolio/fills (ticker=A,B,...) live before its changelog date of October 8, 2026?

Do REST fills still emit the deprecated side and action fields? The Fill schema says they stay until at least May 14, 2026; the order-direction guide says May 28, 2026. Public trades still emit the legacy taker_side.
Fill sort order (newest first?) and the exact end-of-list cursor value (empty string vs null) are undocumented for /portfolio/fills.
Does a fill's fill_id/trade_id equal the public trade_id of the matched trade on /markets/trades? That would allow a join to public trade history for adverse-selection analysis.

What are the current LIP terms after the Feb 11, 2026 filing? The help page (Sep 25, 2026) shows a 1/5-Target reference price and a Jan 1, 2027 end date, but the filed amendment at kalshi.com/regulatory/notices returned HTTP 429. Also unconfirmed: whether DLP/Market-Maker-Agreement members are still excluded, and how 'new_event' programs differ from 'series_lip'.
Is a standard kalshi.com account with API keys a 'direct member', with a $0.0001 balance grid and finer fees? Assumed yes, not confirmed.

Unit sanity: live KXUSDJPY15M period_reward 200000 is $20.00 per 15-minute program, and each of the 10 KXTEMPMIAH strikes shows 1000000 ($100.00) per ~49-minute window. Earlier session estimates ($5 per USD/JPY market, $2,400/day total for Miami) do not match these values. Re-check the centi-cent conversion and whether every hour or strike carries a program.

No API endpoint reports per-account LIP earnings, and payouts under $1 per program are not paid. Can a tiny test (for example 25 contracts) prove the reward leg at all, or only the order, fill and fee path?

checks.claim: *_dollars, fee_cost and balance_dollars are FixedPointDollars strings (requests take 2-4 dp, responses up to 6 dp). *_fp fields are FixedPointCount strings, always 2 dp in responses. Minimum granularity is 0.01 contracts. Fractional fills can happen without fractional orders. Parse with Decimal.
checks.evidence: openapi.yaml v3.32.0 (downloaded 2026-10-05, info.version 3.32.0): FixedPointDollars: 'Most request fields accept 2-4 decimal places (e.g., "0.56", "0.5600"); responses emit up to 6.' FixedPointCount: 'Requests accept 0-2 decimal places ... responses always emit 2 decimals ... the minimum granularity is 0.01 contracts.' fixed_point_migration: 'Even if you are not placing fractional orders, you will encounter fractional values elsewhere in the API (for example, fills).' Live public /markets/trades returned count_fp '13.78', and a KXUSDJPY15M market showed open_interest_fp '1067.93'. A scan of the spec found that every scalar *_dollars/*_fp field references these two types. The only exceptions are orderbook containers (yes_dollars/no_dollars arrays, orderbook_fp object). Caveat: the Fixed-Point Representation guide (Last Updated Aug 20, 2026) still says *_dollars fields have 'up to 4 decimal places'. That is stale relative to the spec and changelog, so parsers must accept 6 dp.

checks.claim: Since Mar 7, 2026, portfolio _dollars fields on orders, order-by-id, fills and positions can carry up to 6 decimals.
checks.evidence: Changelog entry labeled 'Mar 7, 2026': 'Selected portfolio response `_dollars` fields now emit up to `6` decimal places, using micro_cent source values from upstream portfolio protos.' Affected endpoints listed: GET /portfolio/orders, /portfolio/orders/{order_id}, /portfolio/fills, /portfolio/positions. asyncapi.yaml user_orders documents taker/maker fee and cost fields as 'fixed-point dollars (6 decimals)'.

checks.claim: Fields: balance (int64 cents), balance_dollars (FixedPointDollars), portfolio_value (int64 cents), updated_ts (int64, unit unstated), and balance_breakdown (IndexedBalance[], omitted only for subaccount-restricted keys). Params are subaccount (default 0) and exchange_index. Values cover all indexes unless exchange_index is given.
checks.evidence: Spec GetBalanceResponse required [balance, balance_dollars, portfolio_value, updated_ts]. balance is int64 'available balance in cents'. portfolio_value is int64 'in cents'. updated_ts is int64 'Unix timestamp of the last update to the balance.' with no unit given. IndexedBalance is {exchange_index, balance: FixedPointDollars}. Params: SubaccountQueryDefaultPrimary ('Defaults to 0') and exchange_index ('If omitted, both include all exchange indexes'). In the official SDK 3.31.0, GetBalanceResponse.balance is StrictInt, balance_dollars is StrictStr and updated_ts is StrictInt. Nuance from the Aug 13, 2026 changelog: 'Passing subaccount explicitly (including 0, previously treated as omitted) returns that subaccount's balance on the requested exchange index. Omitting subaccount keeps the primary account's aggregate balance'. So omitted and subaccount=0 may differ. Use one form consistently for before/after reconciliation.

checks.claim: Since May 28, 2026, direct-member balances sit on a $0.0001 grid, and the integer 'balance' truncates sub-cent amounts, so balance_dollars is the source of truth. The quick start divides balance by 100.
checks.evidence: Changelog 'May 28, 2026' entry, verbatim: 'direct member balances are aligned to centi-cent (`$0.0001`, or `0.01c`) precision. The legacy `balance` field truncates any sub-cent amount, so use `balance_dollars` for exact values.' quick_start_authenticated_requests prints f"Your balance: ${balance['balance'] / 100:.2f}".

checks.claim: portfolio_value is available balance plus the market value of positions, in cents. Aug 13, 2026 scoped it to index 0; Aug 20, 2026 restored all-index default.
checks.evidence: Changelog Oct 7, 2025: 'portfolio_value ... (available balance plus current market value of all positions), both in cents.' Aug 13, 2026: 'now scopes portfolio_value to the requested exchange_index (defaulting to 0)'. Aug 20, 2026: 'returns balance and portfolio_value across all exchange indexes by default. Pass exchange_index to scope both values to one exchange index.' The spec description matches.

checks.claim: GetBalance accepts keys holding only the 'read::portfolio_balance' scope. Scopes include read, write, read::portfolio_balance, write::trade and write::transfer.
checks.evidence: GetBalance description: 'This endpoint also accepts API keys with the 'read::portfolio_balance' scope.' The full ApiKeyScope enum is ['read','write','read::block_trade_accept','read::portfolio_balance','write::trade','write::transfer','write::fcm_risk','write::block_trade_accept']. The spec says child scopes 'grant only their specific endpoint group and can be granted without the parent scope', and that keys default to full access (read, write) if scopes are not provided.

checks.claim: The docs do not say whether 'available balance' is net of resting-order collateral. The sharding page computes 'account balance minus the value of its resting orders'. Test this empirically.
checks.evidence: Sharding page quote is verbatim: 'Every 10 seconds, Kalshi computes the customer's balance on each exchange shard as its account balance minus the value of its resting orders.' No spec or doc text defines whether GetBalance 'available balance' nets resting collateral. Indirect hint: RestingMarginReservation ('Collateral an automatic rebalance leaves behind for resting orders ... `sum` reserves the summed margin of every resting order') implies the rebalancer's account balance still contains resting-order collateral. This remains an empirical question.

checks.claim: UI Cash already includes non-withdrawable Credit and can differ from the withdrawable amount. The docs do not say whether API balance includes credits.
checks.evidence: Help article, verbatim: 'Credit shows your nonwithdrawable credit balance. This amount is already included in Cash, so do not add it again...' and 'Your cash balance may differ from the amount available to withdraw.' No API doc maps API balance to Cash or Credit.

checks.claim: SubaccountBalance.balance is a FixedPointDollars string (a centi-cent integer before Jan 27, 2026), while GetBalance.balance is integer cents. Other fields are subaccount_number, exchange_index and updated_ts.
checks.evidence: Spec SubaccountBalance required [subaccount_number, exchange_index, balance (FixedPointDollars, 'Balance in dollars.'), updated_ts int64]. SDK 3.31.0 has balance as StrictStr. The quoted sentence is from the changelog entry 'Jan 27, 2026', not from the API reference page that the research cited.

checks.claim: Collateral is per shard. The app and web move cash automatically; the API does not, so API traders must pre-fund the shard. /exchange/status lists shards 0-3 with the status fields given.
checks.evidence: Sharding page: 'Programmatic traders must preallocate collateral on a given exchange shard before order placement.' Also: 'orders placed through the Kalshi App and Web automatically transfer capital between exchange shards as needed to fund the order.' Live public GET /exchange/status (2026-10-05 ~18:10Z) returned exchange_index_statuses for 0 'Default', 1 'Combos', 2 'Crypto & Commodities' and 3 'Tennis, Baseball, Basketball'. Each entry had exchange_active, trading_active and intra_exchange_transfers_active.

checks.claim: KXUSDJPY15M and KXTEMPMIAH are on exchange_index 0 and KXBTC15M is on exchange_index 2.
checks.evidence: Live public GET /series: KXBTC15M has exchange_index 2, category Crypto, fee_type 'quadratic', fee_multiplier 1. KXUSDJPY15M has exchange_index 0 (Financials). KXTEMPMIAH has exchange_index 0 (Climate and Weather). The live open event KXBTC15M-26OCT051415 has exchange_index 2. The sharding table assigns Crypto and Commodities to shard 2.

checks.claim: POST /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfer takes amount as integer CENTICENTS. source and destination are 'event_contract'|'margined'. Shards are 0-100 (default 0), subaccounts are optional, processing is async and returns {transfer_id}. The history endpoint returns amount as a FixedPointDollars string, status pending|complete and created_ts int64, with limit up to 500 and cursor omitted on the last page.
checks.evidence: Spec IntraExchangeInstanceTransferRequest: amount is int64 'The amount to transfer in centicents'. source and destination are ExchangeInstance enum ['event_contract','margined']. source_exchange_shard and destination_exchange_shard are 0-100, default 0. source_subaccount and destination_subaccount are 'Only supported for event contract to event contract transfers'. The 200 response reads 'Transfer request accepted. The transfer is processed asynchronously.' with body {transfer_id}. IntraExchangeInstanceTransfer.amount is FixedPointDollars, status is enum ['pending','complete'], created_ts is int64. TransfersLimitQuery max is 500. History cursor: 'Omitted when there are no further pages.' Missing caveats: 'When source_exchange_shard and destination_exchange_shard are the same, Kalshi treats the request as a subaccount transfer' and 'Cross-exchange-index subaccount transfers run in up to three non-atomic steps. If a later step fails, completed steps are not undone'.

checks.claim: POST /portfolio/target_balance_allocation takes allocations [{exchange_index, percent}] that must total 100 (an empty array disables it), plus resting_margin_reservation none|max|sum (default sum). Kalshi rebalances every 10 seconds.
checks.evidence: Spec: 'Percentages must total 100. Passing an empty allocations array disables automatic rebalancing.' TargetBalanceAllocationInput has percent as an int from 0 to 100, with maxItems 101. RestingMarginReservation enum is [none, max, sum], 'Defaults to `sum` when omitted.' The sharding page says rebalancing runs every 10 seconds and executes an intra-exchange transfer when the balance drifts from the target.

checks.claim: MarketPosition required fields are as listed. position_fp is signed (+YES/-NO), and last_updated_ts is an RFC3339 string.
checks.evidence: Spec MarketPosition required [ticker, exchange_index, total_traded_dollars, position_fp, market_exposure_dollars, realized_pnl_dollars, fees_paid_dollars, last_updated_ts]. position_fp: 'Negative means NO contracts and positive means YES contracts'. last_updated_ts is type string, format date-time.

checks.claim: EventPosition required fields are event_ticker, total_cost_dollars, total_cost_shares_fp, event_exposure_dollars, realized_pnl_dollars and fees_paid_dollars.
checks.evidence: Spec EventPosition required list matches exactly. total_cost_shares_fp: 'total number of shares traded on this event (including both YES and NO contracts)'.

checks.claim: Legacy integer position, exposure, PnL, fee and traded fields are gone (removed Mar 12, 2026). resting_orders_count stopped Nov 13, 2025 and was removed from the schema Jul 9, 2026. Public trades have no integer fields.
checks.evidence: Changelog Mar 8, 2026: legacy integer count fields and integer cents price fields 'will be removed from all REST and WebSocket response payloads on March 12, 2026'. Nov 7, 2025 entry: resting_orders_count removed, 'Expected release: November 13, 2025'. Jul 9, 2026 entry removed MarketPosition.resting_orders_count from the schema. Live /markets/trades keys: count_fp, created_time, is_block_trade, no_price_dollars, taker_book_side, taker_outcome_side, taker_side, ticker, trade_id, yes_price_dollars. Nuances: a Mar 11, 2026 entry temporarily restored some legacy fields (settlement yes_total_cost/no_total_cost and the WS market_positions centi-cent fields) until Apr 2, 2026. Integer-cent fields that have no _dollars twin still exist: GetBalance.balance, portfolio_value, Settlement.revenue/value, Deposit amount_cents.

checks.claim: Params: cursor, limit 1-1000 (default 100), count_filter, settlement_status unsettled|settled|all (default unsettled, added Oct 1, 2026), ticker, single event_ticker, subaccount (default 0) and exchange_index (omit for all). Settled and all queries page by event ticker. An empty cursor means no next page.
checks.evidence: Spec GetPositions params: PositionsCursorQuery, PositionsLimitQuery (1-1000, default 100), CountFilterQuery ('position, total_traded'), PositionSettlementStatusQuery enum [unsettled, settled, all] with default unsettled, TickerQuery, SingleEventTickerQuery, SubaccountQueryDefaultPrimary and ExchangeIndexFilterQuery. Description: 'Settled and all-state positions are paginated by event ticker ... Cursors are specific to the selected settlement status.' GetPositionsResponse.cursor: 'An empty value of this field indicates there is no next page.' Changelog Oct 1, 2026 added settlement_status.

checks.claim: Required Fill fields are as listed. Optional fields are created_time, ts (Unix seconds, legacy), subaccount_number and deprecated side/action.
checks.evidence: Spec Fill required [fill_id, exchange_index, trade_id, order_id, ticker, market_ticker, outcome_side, book_side, count_fp, yes_price_dollars, no_price_dollars, is_taker, fee_cost]. Optional fields: side (deprecated), action (deprecated, enum ['buy','sell']), created_time (date-time), subaccount_number (nullable) and ts (int64). Exception: the REST spec describes ts only as 'Unix timestamp when this fill was executed (legacy field name)' and never states a unit. Only the WS fill ts is documented as seconds.
checks.corrected_fact: REST Fill.ts unit is undocumented. The seconds unit is confirmed only for the WS fill 'ts'. Use created_time (RFC3339) as the REST fill timestamp.

checks.claim: trade_id is a legacy alias of fill_id, and market_ticker is a legacy alias of ticker. Deduplicate on fill_id. The relation to the public trade_id is undocumented.
checks.evidence: Spec: trade_id 'Unique identifier for this fill (legacy field name, same as fill_id)'. market_ticker 'legacy field name, same as ticker'. The asyncapi WS fill.trade_id is described as 'Unique identifier for fills', so the WS trade_id should equal the REST fill_id, though no doc states this explicitly. No doc links a fill id to the public Trade.trade_id.

checks.claim: Integer price/count fields were removed Mar 12, 2026, yes/no_price_fixed were removed Apr 2, 2026, and client_order_id was removed from REST fills Mar 30, 2026. WS fills still carry an optional client_order_id.
checks.evidence: Changelog Mar 30, 2026: 'Removed `client_order_id` from `GET /portfolio/fills` and `GET /portfolio/fills/historical` responses.' Mar 25, 2026, 'Effective April 2, 2026': 'Removed `yes_price_fixed` and `no_price_fixed` ... from GET /portfolio/fills.' asyncapi fill msg has optional client_order_id ('Optional client-provided order ID').

checks.claim: outcome_side and book_side are canonical. Buy yes or sell no maps to yes/bid; buy no or sell yes maps to no/ask. Both parties trade at the same price. Legacy side and action are deprecated (schema says not before May 14, 2026; guide says May 28, 2026).
checks.evidence: The order_direction table matches verbatim. The guide says legacy fields 'will not be removed before May 28, 2026'. Fill and Order schema descriptions say 'This field will not be removed before May 14, 2026.' Both dates have passed (today is 2026-10-05), so the legacy fields can disappear without further notice.

checks.claim: Each fill has is_taker and its own fee_cost (REST since Jan 28, 2026, WS since Jan 29, 2026). There is no maker/taker fee split or rounding/rebate breakdown per fill.
checks.evidence: Spec Fill has is_taker ('If true, this fill was a taker (removed liquidity...)') and fee_cost (FixedPointDollars 'Fee cost in fixed-point dollars'). Changelog Jan 27, 2026: fee_cost on the Fills API 'starting January 28, 2026'. Changelog Jan 29, 2026: fee_cost on WS fill. The per-fill maker_fee_cost/taker_fee_cost fields exist only on FcmFill, which is FCM-only.

checks.claim: Order and WS user_orders carry taker/maker fees_dollars and fill_cost_dollars (6 dp on WS). Create, amend and batch-create responses include average_fill_price and average_fee_paid only when fill_count > 0.
checks.evidence: Spec Order requires taker_fees_dollars, maker_fees_dollars, taker_fill_cost_dollars and maker_fill_cost_dollars. The asyncapi userOrderPayload requires the same fields, described as '(6 decimals)', with example '0.000000'. CreateOrderV2Response.average_fee_paid: 'Volume-weighted average fee paid per contract ... Only present when fill_count > 0.' AmendOrderV2Response: 'Only present when fills occurred.' The BatchCreateOrdersV2Response example has average_fee_paid '0.0012'. These responses come from the V2 endpoints /portfolio/events/orders, /batched and /{id}/amend.

checks.claim: Params: ticker, order_id, min_ts, max_ts, limit 1-1000, cursor, subaccount (omitted means all) and exchange_index. Multi-ticker support (up to 100) is in the spec but carries a changelog date of Oct 8, 2026.
checks.evidence: Spec GetFills: ticker 'Accepts a comma-separated list of up to 100 market tickers', plus OrderIdQuery, MinTsQuery, MaxTsQuery, LimitQuery (1-1000, default 100), CursorQuery, SubaccountQuery ('If omitted, defaults to all subaccounts') and ExchangeIndexFilterQuery. Changelog entry 'Filter fills across multiple markets' is labeled 'October 8, 2026', after today's date of 2026-10-05.

checks.claim: min_ts and max_ts are Unix SECONDS, shared via MinTsQuery/MaxTsQuery across fills, settlements, historical fills and public trades.
checks.evidence: Spec: /portfolio/fills, /portfolio/settlements, /historical/fills, /historical/orders, /portfolio/orders and /markets/trades all reference MinTsQuery/MaxTsQuery (int64 'Unix timestamp'). Independent live test on 2026-10-05: /markets/trades?limit=3&max_ts=1791222792 (17:53:12Z) returned trades created at 2026-10-05T17:53:11.997103Z. The same query with a milliseconds value (1791222792000) returned HTTP 400 Bad Request four times. The research's own conversion (1791219742 = 2026-10-05T17:02:22Z) is correct.

checks.claim: The fill msg contains trade_id, order_id, optional client_order_id, market_ticker, exchange_index, is_taker, side, ts (s), ts_ms, yes_price_dollars only, count_fp, fee_cost, action (buy|sell|sell_partial|sell_to_close|''), post_position_fp, purchased_side, outcome_side, book_side and optional subaccount. The envelope has sending_ts_ms.
checks.evidence: asyncapi.yaml fillPayload.msg required [trade_id, order_id, market_ticker, exchange_index, is_taker, side, yes_price_dollars, count_fp, fee_cost, action, outcome_side, book_side, ts, ts_ms, post_position_fp, purchased_side]. Optional: client_order_id, subaccount. There is no no_price_dollars. ts is 'Deprecated ... (in seconds)'. orderAction enum is ['buy','sell','sell_partial','sell_to_close',''] ('an unknown action is emitted as an empty string'). The example fee_cost is '0.010000'. Missing point: fillPayload required = [type, sid, msg] with NO seq field, so fill gaps cannot be detected on the WS channel.

checks.claim: The msg has user_id, market_ticker, position_fp, position_cost_dollars, realized_pnl_dollars, fees_paid_dollars, position_fee_cost_dollars, volume_fp and optional subaccount. The centi-cent integer fields were removed Apr 2, 2026. Only market_ticker filters are supported.
checks.evidence: asyncapi marketPositionPayload.msg required list matches. The docs page says: 'Filters are by `market_ticker`/`market_tickers` only; `market_id`/`market_ids` are not supported'. Changelog Mar 25, 2026 (effective Apr 2) removed position_cost, realized_pnl, fees_paid and position_fee_cost (integer centi-cents). The payload has no exchange_index and no seq.

checks.claim: Required Settlement fields are as listed. revenue is integer CENTS, settled_time is RFC3339, fee_cost is FixedPointDollars, and value is a nullable integer in cents per YES contract. Use market settlement_value_dollars for sub-cent results.
checks.evidence: Spec Settlement required [ticker, exchange_index, event_ticker, market_result (enum yes|no|scalar), yes_count_fp, yes_total_cost_dollars, no_count_fp, no_total_cost_dollars, revenue, settled_time, fee_cost]. revenue is integer, 'in cents (winning contracts pay out 100 cents each)'. value is a nullable integer, 'Payout of a single yes contract in cents.' fee_cost example is '0.3400'. SDK 3.31.0 has revenue as StrictInt. Market.settlement_value_dollars exists: 'settlement value of the YES/LONG side ... Only filled after determination'.

checks.claim: Settlement.fee_cost is the sum of trade fees over the position, so do not add it on top of the fill fees. yes/no_total_cost integers were removed Apr 2, 2026.
checks.evidence: Changelog Nov 13, 2025: '`GET /portfolio/settlements` now returns the sum of trade fees paid by the user on a settled market position.' The spec describes fee_cost as 'Total fees paid in fixed point dollars.' The Mar 25, 2026 entry (effective Apr 2) removed yes_total_cost/no_total_cost. Unknown: whether a scalar settlement fee is included in this field.

checks.claim: Params: limit 1-1000, cursor, ticker, event_ticker, min_ts, max_ts and subaccount (omitted means all). The endpoint covers only the live data set, and no historical endpoint has the same fields, so persist settlement records locally.
checks.evidence: Spec GetSettlements params: LimitQuery, CursorQuery, TickerQuery, SingleEventTickerQuery, MinTsQuery, MaxTsQuery and SubaccountQuery. There is no exchange_index filter. historical_data page, verbatim: '`GET /portfolio/settlements` reads only settled positions still in the live data set. After archival, `GET /historical/positions` provides position, realized P&L, and fee data, but there is currently no historical endpoint with the same settlement-record fields.'

checks.claim: Settlement fees are zero for yes/no results and apply only to sub-cent scalar results. The FIX example floors a direct user to $0.0001 (fee $0.00006), while the overview says payouts round to whole cents.
checks.evidence: market_settlement page: 'Settlement fees are zero for simple yes/no determinations but may apply for sub-cent scalar settlement. The actual payout (`CollateralAmountChange`) is rounded to whole cents.' The FIX market-settlement example has a direct user with 100.01 YES at 30.60c, gross $30.60306, net 1704=30.6030 and fee 137=0.00006: 'available balance is rounded down to $0.0001 precision'. The two docs conflict as the research noted. Do not assume either; reconcile against balance_dollars.

checks.claim: Direct-member balances are on a $0.0001 grid and non-direct on $0.01. Fees are 6-dp. Each fill has trade fee, rounding fee and rebate components, and net fee is at least $0.
checks.evidence: fee_rounding page, verbatim: 'Direct member balances are aligned to `$0.0001` (`0.01c`)', 'Non-direct member balances are aligned to `$0.01`', 'Fees are six-decimal dollar amounts', table of Trade fee / Rounding fee / Rebate, and '**Net fee** = trade fee + rounding fee - rebate (always >= $0.00)'.

checks.claim: The five documented steps, with a per-order accumulator. Worked example: (0.003639, 0.001361, -0.06) non-direct and (0.003639, 0.000061, -0.0587) direct.
checks.evidence: The doc steps match verbatim, including the per-order accumulator note. I reproduced the research's fill_fee_components in the project's .venv Python 3.12.10 Decimal and independently in PowerShell [decimal]. Non-direct: (0.003639, 0.001361, -0.06), which matches the doc's 'trade fee plus rounding fee is exactly $0.005'. Direct: (0.003639, 0.000061, -0.0587).

checks.claim: A direct member pays ceil_6dp(model fee) plus rounding to the $0.0001 grid, not the old per-trade cent round-up. Per-fill fee_cost can be sub-cent, 'such as "0.010000"'. Whether REST fee_cost is the net fee is undocumented.
checks.evidence: fee_rounding supersedes the older rule. The CFTC-filed Kalshi Fee Schedule (Sept 22, 2022) said 'round up = rounds to the next cent'. No doc states whether REST/WS fee_cost is net of the rounding fee and rebate. The WS describes it as 'Exchange fee paid for this fill'. One wording error: '0.010000' is exactly $0.01, a whole cent, not a sub-cent value. It only shows the 6-dp format.
checks.corrected_fact: fee_cost strings carry up to 6 dp (e.g. '0.010000' = $0.01), so sub-cent values such as '0.000061' are representable. Whether fee_cost is the net fee (trade + rounding - rebate) is still undocumented.

checks.claim: Series.fee_type takes quadratic | quadratic_with_maker_fees | quadratic_with_combo_maker_fees | flat. fee_multiplier is a double. Event overrides and fee_changes endpoints exist, and markets may have fee_waiver_expiration_time.
checks.evidence: Spec FeeType enum [quadratic, quadratic_with_maker_fees, quadratic_with_combo_maker_fees, flat]. The Series.fee_type description is verbatim as quoted. Event.fee_type_override and fee_multiplier_override exist, as do /events/fee_changes and /series/fee_changes (series_fee_change_arr), and Market.fee_waiver_expiration_time. Caveat: live public GET /series/fee_changes?show_historical=true returned 31 rows with fee_type 'margin_market_maker_program_fees' (perps series such as KXBTC-style *PERP). That value is NOT in the REST FeeType enum, although the asyncapi event-fee enum lists it. Strict enum parsing of fee_changes will break.
checks.corrected_fact: Treat fee_type as an open string. Live fee_changes also emits 'margin_market_maker_program_fees', which is outside the REST FeeType enum.

checks.claim: KXUSDJPY15M, KXTEMPMIAH and KXBTC15M are quadratic with multiplier 1 and have empty fee-change history, so maker fills should have zero model fee.
checks.evidence: Live 2026-10-05: /series/{t} returned fee_type 'quadratic' and fee_multiplier 1 for all three. /series/fee_changes?series_ticker={t}&show_historical=true returned {"series_fee_change_arr":[]} for each. /events/fee_changes (85 rows) has none for these series, and current open events carry no fee_type_override. The zero maker fee for plain 'quadratic' is supported by the spec (maker fees exist only in the *_with_maker_fees types) and by the CFTC-filed fee schedule: 'Trading fees are not charged for orders ... left as resting orders'. Confirm on the first real maker fill.

checks.claim: Taker fee = 0.07*C*P*(1-P) and maker fee = 0.0175*C*P*(1-P), times the multiplier. Unconfirmed officially because the PDF returned 429.
checks.evidence: kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf still returns HTTP 429 (retested). An official CFTC-filed copy of the 'Kalshi Fee Schedule' (2nd iteration, Sept 22, 2022) confirms the general fee 'fees = round up(0.07 x C x P x (1-P))', with the cent round-up now superseded by fee_rounding. It also confirms no fees on resting orders at that time. The 0.0175 maker coefficient is not in any official source I could read. It is only consistent with the spec's '0.25 maker multiplier' wording.
checks.corrected_fact: Taker/general coefficient 0.07 is confirmed by an official (2022) filing. The maker coefficient 0.0175 is still unverified.

checks.claim: Public GET /exchange/user_data_timestamp returns {as_of_time: RFC3339}. Combine REST with WS.
checks.evidence: The spec endpoint has no security block. Its description matches the quote and lists 'GetBalance, GetOrder(s), GetFills, GetPositions'. My unauthenticated call returned {"as_of_time":"2026-10-05T18:13:40.924779Z"}.

checks.claim: Timestamp formats are mixed. RFC3339 strings with microseconds: Fill.created_time, Settlement.settled_time, MarketPosition.last_updated_ts, incentive dates. int64 Unix: balance, subaccount, deposit and transfer timestamps. Fill.ts is seconds. ts_ms fields are milliseconds.
checks.evidence: The spec types match: created_time, settled_time and last_updated_ts are date-time; GetBalance.updated_ts, SubaccountBalance.updated_ts, Deposit.created_ts and IntraExchangeInstanceTransfer.created_ts are int64; ts_ms is ms. Corrections from live data: fractional-second digits vary. In incentive_programs and trades I counted 2319 values with 0 digits (e.g. '2026-10-05T18:30:00Z'), 1607 with 6, 68 with 5 ('...10.54676Z') and 9 with 4 ('...30.8027Z'). REST Fill.ts unit is not documented. Order expiration_time in create/amend requests is Unix SECONDS, while WS expiration_ts_ms is ms.
checks.corrected_fact: RFC3339 strings have 0-6 fractional digits, with trailing zeros trimmed, so use a tolerant parser (Python >=3.11 fromisoformat handles these; verified on 3.12.10). The REST Fill.ts unit is undocumented.

checks.claim: amount_cents and fee_cents are int64 cents. status is pending|applied|failed|returned; type is ach|wire|crypto|debit|apm. created_ts and finalized_ts are int64 (finalized_ts nullable). limit max is 500, with cursor pagination. There is no reward type.
checks.evidence: Spec Deposit and Withdrawal schemas match exactly. WithdrawalLimitQuery max is 500. The type enum has no reward or credit value.

checks.claim: Netting is off by default and locks per event at the first order. KXTEMPMIAH events are DIRECNET with 10 markets; KXUSDJPY15M events are '' with 1 market. With netting on, cash deltas will not equal price x quantity.
checks.evidence: The help article is verbatim, including the netting_enabled lock note. Live public /events?series_ticker=...&status=open&with_nested_markets=true returned: KXTEMPMIAH-26OCT0515 collateral_return_type 'DIRECNET' with 10 markets, KXUSDJPY15M-26OCT051415 '' with 1 market, and KXBTC15M-26OCT051415 '' with 1 market. The spec says netting 'also requires netting to be enabled for the trading account'. Missing: GET /portfolio/subaccounts/netting returns netting_configs [{subaccount_number, enabled, exchange_index}], so the bot can read its netting state via the API.

checks.claim: Public GET /incentive_programs. period_reward and max_reward_per_account are int64 CENTI-CENTS. discount_factor_bps is in bps. target_size_fp is a string. paid_out is program-level.
checks.evidence: The spec IncentiveProgram schema matches: period_reward is int64 'Total reward for the period in centi-cents', max_reward_per_account is nullable centi-cents, and discount_factor_bps and target_size_fp are nullable. The endpoint has no security block, and my unauthenticated calls returned 200. SDK 3.31.0: period_reward StrictInt 'centi-cents'. Independent plausibility check: the filed LIP terms cap the Time Period Reward at $1,000 per calendar day per market. Daily FX programs show 250000, which is $25/day in centi-cents but would be $2,500/day if read as cents, breaking the cap. So the centi-cent reading is right.

checks.claim: KXUSDJPY15M 15-minute program = 200000 ($20), target 300.00, 5000 bps. Each of 10 KXTEMPMIAH strikes = 1000000 ($100), target 1000.00. Daily KXUSDJPY/KXEURUSD = 250000 ($25).
checks.evidence: Live /incentive_programs?status=active&type=liquidity&limit=1000 at about 18:16Z: KXUSDJPY15M-26OCT051430-30 period_reward 200000, target_size_fp '300.00', discount_factor_bps 5000, window 18:15-18:30Z. Ten KXTEMPMIAH-26OCT0515-T*.99 strikes each had 1000000 with target '1000.00' and window 18:01:58.38722Z-19:00:00Z (about 58 minutes for this hour, so window length varies with program start). KXUSDJPY-/KXEURUSD-26OCT0610-* had 250000 for a 24h window. None had max_reward_per_account.

checks.claim: Params are status, type, incentive_description, limit (10000) and cursor, with next_cursor in the response. The market_ticker param is ignored. series_ticker is missing. Parsing tickers to infer series is 'the only option'.
checks.evidence: Confirmed parts: spec params status [all, active, upcoming, closed, paid_out], type [all, liquidity, volume, margin_maker_volume, margin_taker_volume], incentive_description, limit (max 10000) and cursor; response next_cursor. Live ?market_ticker=KXUSDJPY15M-26OCT051430-30 returned unrelated KXCOPPER15M, KXPLATINUM15M and KXCRYPTOLEAD15M rows. series_ticker was announced in the changelog ('Expected release: October 13, 2025') but is absent from the v3.32.0 schema and from all 3000 live rows I pulled (active, paid_out and closed). Wrong part: parsing is not the only option. Public GET /markets accepts tickers (comma-separated) and returns event_ticker. GET /events/{event_ticker} returns series_ticker. GET /markets?series_ticker=X lists a series' markets for a join. The glossary says 'do not parse ticker strings to infer relationships.'
checks.corrected_fact: Map incentive market_ticker to series without parsing: GET /markets?tickers=A,B,... gives event_ticker, then GET /events/{event_ticker} gives series_ticker. Or pull GET /markets?series_ticker=KXUSDJPY15M&status=open and join on ticker. Filter incentive rows client-side because market_ticker is ignored server-side.

checks.corrected_fact: openapi.yaml v3.32.0 has 100 paths / 117 operations. None of the three published specs (163 paths total) exposes per-account reward credits.

checks.claim: Rewards are credited in a later batch after the program ends. They show under Rewards (Current month/Lifetime) and Account > Activity > Credits. Estimates are UI-only. Rewards under $1 are not paid and are rounded down to the cent. SSN rule applies.
checks.evidence: Help 16076644 (modified 2026-09-29) is verbatim: 'Rewards are not credited in real time. Final scoring occurs after a program ends, and payment follows in a later processing run. Timing can vary.' and '...a final reward below $1 for an individual program is not paid.' It also covers the Credits path and that the estimate is not final. The SSN sentence is in the LIP article 13823851, not 16076644: 'A verified Social Security Number (SSN) must be on file to receive reward credits above annual IRS reporting thresholds. That threshold covers referral and incentive credits together'.

checks.claim: One snapshot per second at a random moment. The 1/5-Target reference price. Score is size x DF^ticks, normalized per side (max 2.0). A snapshot is excluded unless both sides reach Target. Reward = share x reward x non-excluded ratio, rounded down. Target is >100 and <20,000; periods up to 31 days; program ends Jan 1, 2027. Non-US and IB/FCM users are ineligible.
checks.evidence: Help 13823851 (dateModified 2026-09-25T22:15:52Z) is verbatim on all points. The program end is 'January 1, 2027'. Ineligible: 'Kalshi affiliates and employees; Introducing Brokers, FCMs, and their customers; International, non-U.S. users'. 'Daily rewards: $1-$1,000 per market, per day'. This matches the CFTC-filed July 15, 2026 terms, effective July 30, 2026.

checks.claim: The Feb 11, 2026 filed terms differ (highest-bid reference, ends Sep 1, 2026, $10/day floor, Market Maker Agreement members excluded). The later amendment is posted only at kalshi.com/regulatory/notices, which returned 429.
checks.evidence: The Feb 11, 2026 details are correct; I read the S3 PDF. The rest is wrong: the later amendments are public in the same S3 bucket. An unauthenticated ListObjects on kalshi-public-docs with prefix regulatory/notices/Liquidity returned 'Liquidity Incentive Program - July 15, 2026 Update.pdf' and 'Liquidity Incentive Program - July 30, 2026 Modification to July 15, 2026 Update.pdf'. July 15 filing: 'This amendment will go into effect on July 30, 2026.' The clean terms say 'Eligible Participants are all Kalshi members, except the following: Introducing Brokers, Futures Commission Merchants, and customers thereof'. The affiliate and Market-Maker-Agreement exclusions are struck out. Program end is January 1, 2027. Time Period Reward is 'no less than $1 and no greater than $1,000 per calendar day', and the July 30 modification adds 'applied on a per-market basis'. Reference Yes Price is set where cumulative size >= 1/5 Target. Bids above the reference get N=0. Payout is multiplied by 'ratio of non-excluded snapshots to total snapshots'.
checks.corrected_fact: Current filed LIP terms (effective July 30, 2026, ending Jan 1, 2027): only IBs, FCMs and their customers are excluded. Market-Maker-Agreement members (DLPs) and affiliates are NOT excluded under the filing. The reward is $1-$1,000 per calendar day per market, with the 1/5-Target reference price and payout scaled by the non-excluded-snapshot ratio. The help page still lists affiliates and employees as ineligible.

Running it on a WS NO fill dict produced "KeyError 'no_price_dollars'". The comment says 'no price = 1 - yes price', but the code does not implement it.

checks.claim: cents, centi-cent, fixed-point and _fp conversions, including to_centicents for the intra-transfer amount.
checks.evidence: The unit mappings match the spec (cents: GetBalance.balance/portfolio_value, Settlement.revenue/value, Deposit amount_cents; centi-cents: IncentiveProgram.period_reward, intra-transfer request amount). One safety issue: to_centicents uses Decimal.to_integral_exact without the Inexact trap, so it silently rounds (to_centicents(Decimal('1.00005')) returned 10000 in my run). For a live transfer, assert the value is an exact multiple of 0.0001 instead.
