checks.claim: One generator handles both cursor and next_cursor and stops on a falsy cursor.
checks.evidence: The request param is named 'cursor' for every endpoint, including /incentive_programs (spec param 'cursor'). Only the response field differs (next_cursor). A falsy-cursor stop matches positions ('empty value'), intra-transfers ('Omitted') and the guide ('null'). Suggest a guard against a repeated identical cursor.

missing_critical: Order writes now use V2 paths: POST /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders (CreateOrderV2). Body: {ticker, side: 'bid'|'ask', count: FixedPointCount string e.g. '10.00', price: FixedPointDollars string e.g. '0.5600', time_in_force: 'fill_or_kill'|'good_till_canceled'|'immediate_or_cancel' (required), self_trade_prevention_type: 'taker_at_cross'|'maker' (required), optional client_order_id, post_only, reduce_only (rejected unless IOC), cancel_order_on_pause, expiration_time (Unix SECONDS), subaccount, order_group_id, exchange_index}. The 201 response is {order_id, client_order_id, fill_count, remaining_count, average_fill_price?, average_fee_paid?, ts_ms}. side is BookSide: 'bid' = buy YES and 'ask' = sell YES (= buy NO at 1-price), and price is ALWAYS the YES price. To rest a NO bid at $0.20, send side 'ask' with price '0.8000'. The legacy POST /portfolio/orders 'will be deprecated no earlier than May 6, 2026'. Sources: https://docs.kalshi.com/openapi.yaml and https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/quick_start_create_order

Cancel routing trap: DELETE /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id} routes by shard. 'If omitted, auto-routes when market_ticker is provided; otherwise defaults to 0' and 'An order_id alone cannot identify the exchange shard.' A KXBTC15M order (exchange_index 2) cancelled by order_id alone goes to shard 0 and the order stays live. Always pass market_ticker or exchange_index on cancel, decrease, amend and batch-cancel. The response is {order_id, client_order_id, reduced_by, ts_ms}.

Kill switch: DELETE /portfolio/events/orders (CancelAllOrders) cancels resting orders 'across every exchange shard', but 'Newly placed orders may also be cancelled during the minute after the request.' Do not place orders for at least 60s after using it. Order groups (contracts_limit_fp per rolling 15-second window, is_auto_cancel_enabled) give an exchange-side size cap, but they 'do not function across exchange instances'.

Idempotency and reconciliation: client_order_id dedupes orders, and a duplicate returns '409 Conflict: Order with this client_order_id already exists'. REST fills no longer carry client_order_id, so persist client_order_id->order_id before and after submit. On a timeout, resubmit with the SAME client_order_id or look up GET /portfolio/orders?ticker=...; never resubmit with a new id.

WS user channels (fill, user_orders, market_positions) have NO seq field (required fields are only type, sid, msg), so gaps are undetectable. After any reconnect, reconcile via REST: GET /portfolio/orders?status=resting, GET /portfolio/fills?min_ts=<last_ts_seconds - margin>, and GET /portfolio/positions. Use GET /exchange/user_data_timestamp as_of_time to judge REST freshness.

Auth: headers are KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY, KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP (milliseconds) and KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE = base64(sign(timestamp_ms + METHOD + path)). The path includes /trade-api/v2 and excludes the query string. RSA keys use RSA-PSS SHA-256 with MGF1-SHA256 and salt = digest length. Ed25519 keys sign the raw text. Since Oct 1, 2026 the web app generates Ed25519 keys BY DEFAULT, and the PEM header does not reveal the key type (PKCS#8 RSA keys also start with 'BEGIN PRIVATE KEY'). Detect the type from the parsed key. The WS handshake signs timestamp + 'GET' + '/trade-api/ws/v2'. Sources: https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/api_keys and https://docs.kalshi.com/changelog (Oct 1, 2026)

Hosts: production REST is https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2 (recommended; api.elections.kalshi.com also supported). Demo REST is https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 (or https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2). WS is wss://external-api-ws.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2 (prod) and wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2 (demo). Keys are not shared between environments. The official SDK's default host is PRODUCTION, so set the host explicitly.

Least-privilege key: ApiKeyScope supports child scopes. Give the bot key 'read' + 'write::trade' only (no 'write::transfer', no broad 'write'). Do shard funding with a separate key or in the UI. Keys default to full read+write if scopes are omitted.

Rate limits: the Basic tier has Read 200 and Write 100 tokens/s, and the Basic Write bucket holds only 1 second of budget. Default cost is 10 tokens (about 10 order creates/s); single cancel and GET order cost 2 tokens. A 429 returns body {"error": "too many requests"} with no Retry-After header, so use exponential backoff. Auto-routed single writes bill every shard's Write bucket. GET /account/limits and GET /account/endpoint_costs give live values. Source: https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/rate_limits

Tick grid: snap prices to market.price_ranges, not to the price_level_structure name. Live KXBTC15M markets are tapered_deci_cent ($0.001 ticks below $0.10 and above $0.90, $0.01 in between). KXUSDJPY15M and KXTEMPMIAH are linear_cent ($0.01). Off-grid prices are rejected.

Shard funding: KXBTC15M needs cash on shard 2. Underfunded orders fail with error code 'available_balance_too_low'. Check GET /exchange/status trading_active and intra_exchange_transfers_active per shard. Intra-transfers are async: poll GET /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfers/{transfer_id} until status 'complete'. Same-shard requests are treated as subaccount transfers, and cross-index subaccount transfers are non-atomic.

Second transfer unit trap: POST /portfolio/subaccounts/transfer takes amount_cents (integer CENTS) plus a required client_transfer_id (uuid, for idempotency). The intra-exchange transfer 'amount' is in CENTI-CENTS.

Netting state is readable: GET /portfolio/subaccounts/netting returns netting_configs [{subaccount_number, enabled, exchange_index}]. Read it before trading DIRECNET events such as KXTEMPMIAH so cash deltas can be interpreted, since netting locks per event at the first order.

Amend and order-state semantics: AmendOrderV2 requires ticker, side, price and count, where count = already-filled + desired remaining. 'Increasing size or changing price forfeits queue position'. user_orders last_update_reason enum [Decrease, Amend, MarginCancel, SelfTradeCancel, ExpiryCancel, CloseCancel, HaltCancel, Trade, PostOnlyCrossCancel, ReduceOnlyCancel, SettlementBoundsCancel] explains vanished orders. The WS status enum includes 'unknown'. Use post_only=true to guarantee maker-only fills; a crossing order then cancels with PostOnlyCrossCancel instead of paying taker fees.

LIP competition and economics: under the filed terms effective July 30, 2026, Market-Maker-Agreement members (the DLPs quoting FX 15-min and Hourly Temp) are LIP-eligible. Rewards are scaled by the non-excluded-snapshot ratio and paid only if >= $1 per program. A 25-contract tiny test sits far below Target Size (300 for FX 15-min, 1000 for KXTEMPMIAH) and will likely earn under $1, which pays $0. The test can validate order, fill, fee and cancel plumbing, not the reward leg. Source: https://kalshi-public-docs.s3.amazonaws.com/regulatory/notices/Liquidity%20Incentive%20Program%20-%20July%2015,%202026%20Update.pdf

Parsing tolerance: live fee_changes includes fee_type 'margin_market_maker_program_fees', which is outside the REST FeeType enum. RFC3339 timestamps have 0-6 fractional digits. The WS fill has no no_price_dollars field. The research's fill_row helper raises KeyError on WS NO fills.

research.area: Real-time data (Trade API v2 WebSocket) and exchange rules for small live tests. Sources: docs.kalshi.com pages and specs (openapi.yaml v3.32.0, asyncapi.yaml), the changelog through its Oct 8, 2026 entries, help.kalshi.com, the official Kalshi GitHub starter repo, rulebook v1.29 and contract-terms PDFs, and the July 15, 2026 LIP CFTC filing. Live checks were public, unauthenticated GETs only, made 2026-10-05 around 18:00Z.

facts.fact: Production WebSocket URL (recommended): wss://external-api-ws.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2. The shared host wss://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2 is also supported. Demo: wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2 (wss://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2 also works). Demo and production API keys are separate. The signed path is the same on every host.
facts.quote:
| Production | `wss://external-api-ws.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2` | `wss://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2` |
| Demo | `wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2` | `wss://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2` |

facts.fact: Every WebSocket connection must be authenticated in the HTTP upgrade handshake, even if it only subscribes to public channels such as ticker, trade or lifecycle. Required headers: KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY (key id), KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP (Unix milliseconds as a string) and KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE = base64(sign(timestamp + 'GET' + '/trade-api/ws/v2')). Sign only the path, with no host and no query string. RSA keys sign with RSA-PSS/SHA-256 (MGF1 SHA-256, salt length = digest length); Ed25519 keys (supported on WS since Sep 24, 2026) sign the string directly. There is no unauthenticated WebSocket, so this project cannot test the WS feed until an API key exists.
facts.quote:
Authentication is required to establish the connection; include API key headers during the WebSocket handshake.
Some channels carry only public market data, but the connection itself still requires authentication.

facts.fact: Valid channel names: orderbook_delta, ticker, trade, fill, market_positions, market_lifecycle_v2, multivariate_market_lifecycle, communications, order_group_updates, user_orders, cfbenchmarks_value, cfbenchmarks_value_5hz, pyth_value. Filters by channel: orderbook_delta requires market_ticker (string) or market_tickers (array); market_id(s) is not supported, and omitting a market gives error 14. ticker and trade filters are optional (omit them to get every market); ticker also accepts market_id(s). fill takes optional market_ticker(s). user_orders takes optional market_tickers. market_positions filters by market_ticker(s) only. market_lifecycle_v2 accepts no market filter and delivers all markets. order_group_updates ignores market filters. market_ticker and market_tickers are mutually exclusive. Private, user-scoped channels: fill, user_orders, market_positions, order_group_updates, communications, plus the own-order annotations on orderbook_delta.
facts.quote: enum: ["orderbook_delta", "ticker", "trade", "fill", "market_positions", "market_lifecycle_v2", "multivariate_market_lifecycle", "communications", "order_group_updates", "user_orders", "cfbenchmarks_value", "cfbenchmarks_value_5hz", "pyth_value"]

facts.fact: The Quick Start still lists a public 'multivariate' channel, but that channel was removed on Aug 6, 2026. Subscribing to it returns an unknown-channel error (code 8).
facts.quote: The `multivariate` WebSocket channel (message type `multivariate_lookup`) no longer exists. Subscriptions to it now return an unknown-channel error. For multivariate market state changes, use the `multivariate_market_lifecycle` channel.

facts.fact: Command shape: {id:int, cmd:'subscribe'|'unsubscribe'|'update_subscription'|'list_subscriptions', params:{...}}. The client chooses id and it must be unique within the session; id 0 means no id. Replies by command: (1) subscribe returns {id, type:'subscribed', msg:{channel, sid}}, where sid is the server-assigned subscription id. (2) unsubscribe takes params.sids:[...] and returns type 'unsubscribed' (with sid and seq). (3) update_subscription must target exactly one subscription, via params.sid or a one-element params.sids but not both. Its action is add_markets, delete_markets or get_snapshot (orderbook only). It returns type 'ok' with the full market_tickers list, which skip_ticker_ack:true omits. (4) list_subscriptions returns type 'ok' with msg = [{channel, sid}]. Inference: subscriptions and sids belong to one session, so after a reconnect you must resubscribe and use the new sids.
facts.quote:
Unique ID of the command request. Generated by the client and should be unique within a WS session.
The simplest way to use it would be to start from 1 and then increment the value for every new command sent to the server.
If the id is set to 0, the server treats it the same way as if there was no id.

facts.fact: Errors look like {id, type:'error', msg:{code:int, msg:string}}. Subscription-scoped errors also carry sid, plus seq on sequenced channels. Codes: 1 unable to process; 2 params required; 3 channels required; 4 sids required; 5 unknown command; 7 unknown sid; 8 unknown channel; 9 authentication required; 10 channel error; 11 invalid parameter; 12 exactly one sid required; 13 unsupported action; 14 market ticker required; 15 action required; 18 command timeout; 19-22 communications shard params; 23 match IDs required; 24 index IDs required; 25 subscription buffer overflow; 26 subscription market limit exceeded; 27 too many requests (per-subscription command rate limit); 28 underlying tickers required. Codes 6, 16 and 17 are retired. Codes 10 and 25 are terminal: that subscription is dead and must be created again.
facts.quote:
The following channel errors are terminal and the user must resubscribe.

| Code | Error |
|------|-------|
| 10 | Channel error |
| 25 | Subscription buffer overflow |

facts.fact: Most WebSocket limits are undocumented: Kalshi does not publish the markets-per-subscription cap behind error 26 or the per-subscription command rate behind error 27. The last published connection cap is from Sep 18, 2025: connections per user are limited by API tier, starting at 200 by default. Maximum message size is 64 MiB. RFC 7692 permessage-deflate compression is optional; you get it only if the client offers it in the handshake. Error 25 (buffer overflow) means the subscription was too broad or the client read too slowly.
facts.quote: WebSocket connections per user are limited by usage tier. The default limit begins at 200 and increases based on API usage tier.

facts.fact: An orderbook_snapshot is sent first for each subscribed market, and again in reply to get_snapshot. Envelope: {type:'orderbook_snapshot', sid, seq, id (only when replying to get_snapshot), sending_ts_ms, msg}. msg holds market_ticker, market_id (UUID), yes_dollars_fp and no_dollars_fp. Each is an array of [price_in_dollars, contract_count_fp] string pairs; for example ['0.0800','300.00'] means 300.00 contracts bid at $0.08. A side's key is missing entirely when that side is empty. Prices are dollar strings with 4 decimals and sizes are contract strings with 2 decimals. The docs do not say how WS levels are ordered; REST returns them ascending.
facts.quote:
Price levels represented as [price_in_dollars, contract_count_fp].
Format: [price_in_dollars, contract_count_fp]

facts.fact: orderbook_delta fields: msg.price_dollars (dollar string, e.g. '0.9600'), msg.delta_fp (signed contract change with 2 decimals; '-54.00' means 54 contracts left that level), msg.side ('yes'|'no'), msg.ts_ms (Unix ms; the RFC3339 ts is deprecated), and market_ticker/market_id. msg.client_order_id and msg.subaccount appear ONLY when your own order caused the change, which lets the bot see its own book impact.
facts.quote:
Optional - Present only when you caused this orderbook change.
Contains the client_order_id of your order that triggered this delta.

facts.fact: By default (use_yes_price false), NO-side snapshot and delta levels use NO-leg prices: a no-side level at 0.30 is a bid for NO at 30c, which equals a YES ask at 70c. Subscribing with params.use_yes_price:true reports NO-side levels at YES-leg prices instead (0.30 becomes 0.70). Kalshi plans to make true the default and later remove the flag; no dates have been announced, so set the flag explicitly. The REST book (GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook) also lists bids only, and best YES ask = 1 - best NO bid.
facts.quote:
Orderbook channel only. When true, no-side `orderbook_delta` and `orderbook_snapshot` updates
are reported in yes-leg pricing instead of no-leg pricing

facts.fact: GET /trade-api/v2/markets/{ticker}/orderbook needs no auth. It returns orderbook_fp.yes_dollars and orderbook_fp.no_dollars as [price_dollars, count_fp] string pairs sorted ascending, best bid last. Observed live on KXBTC15M-26OCT051430-30: depth=3 returned the best 3 levels, still ascending (yes [['0.5600','1658.88'],['0.5700','2173.00'],['0.5800','2685.09']]). The full book had 148 YES and 131 NO levels, reaching down to $0.0010 with sub-cent edge ticks. A /markets top-of-book read (yes_bid 0.56) differed from the orderbook read seconds later (best yes bid 0.58), so treat the /markets bid/ask fields as indicative only.
facts.quote:
Arrays are sorted by price in **ascending order**
* The **highest** bid (best bid) is the **last** element in each array

facts.fact: seq is an integer >= 1. The schemas put it on orderbook_snapshot/orderbook_delta, trade, market_lifecycle_v2 (including metadata_updated), multivariate_market_lifecycle, event_lifecycle, event_fee_update, order_group_updates, RFQ/quote messages and cfbenchmarks/pyth messages. It also appears on 'unsubscribed' replies, optionally on 'ok' replies, and on subscription-scoped errors. ticker, fill, user_order and market_position messages have NO seq; their required envelope is only type, sid and msg. Inference: gaps in your private order and fill streams cannot be detected by seq and must be reconciled over REST.
facts.quote: Sequential number that should be checked if you want to guarantee you received all the messages. Used for snapshot/delta consistency

facts.fact: Kalshi publishes no gap-recovery procedure. Three tools are available. (a) update_subscription with action get_snapshot (added Apr 20, 2026) returns a fresh orderbook_snapshot for the listed market_tickers without changing the subscription or its delta stream; it accepts only market_tickers, not market_ticker or market_id. (b) Unsubscribe and subscribe again. (c) Terminal errors 10 and 25 always require resubscribing. Inference from the examples (snapshot seq 2 then delta seq 3 on sid 2; ok reply sid 456 seq 222; unsubscribed sid 2 seq 7): there seems to be one counter per sid that also advances on ok/unsubscribed frames, so track seq on every frame that carries the sid. On a gap in a multi-market sid you cannot tell which market missed an update, so resnapshot every market on that sid.
facts.quote: Sends an `orderbook_snapshot` response for the requested markets without adding them to the subscription or affecting the existing delta stream.

facts.fact: Since Sep 17, 2026, a subscription's 'subscribed' acknowledgement always arrives before its data. Before that fix, the first event right after the ack could be lost.
facts.quote: Fixed a race that could skip events arriving immediately after a `subscribed` response, including on the `cfbenchmarks_value_5hz` channel. The acknowledgement continues to precede subscription data.

facts.fact: Kalshi sends a Ping control frame (opcode 0x9) with body 'heartbeat' every 10 seconds, and the client should answer with a Pong (0xA). Clients may also send their own Pings. The Python websockets library answers Pings automatically. The docs give no Pong timeout or idle-disconnect rule. They recommend automatic reconnection with exponential backoff and warn to expect disconnects during the Thursday 3:00-5:00 AM ET maintenance window.
facts.quote:
Kalshi sends Ping frames (`0x9`) every 10 seconds with body `heartbeat` to maintain the connection.
Clients should respond with Pong frames (`0xA`). Clients may also send Ping frames to which Kalshi will respond with Pong.

facts.fact: Since Oct 1, 2026, every WS message carries a top-level sending_ts_ms: an int64 Unix-ms time when Kalshi queued the message at the network layer, useful for measuring latency. Event times are in msg.ts_ms (Unix ms). The seconds-based ts and RFC3339 ts/time fields are deprecated.
facts.quote: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when Kalshi queued this message at the network layer.

facts.fact: ticker msg fields and units: market_ticker, market_id; price_dollars (last trade, dollar string such as '0.4800'); yes_bid_dollars and yes_ask_dollars (dollar strings); yes_bid_size_fp, yes_ask_size_fp and last_trade_size_fp (contract strings, 2 decimals, e.g. '300.00'); volume_fp and open_interest_fp (contract strings); dollar_volume and dollar_open_interest are signed INTEGER whole dollars (e.g. 16948); ts_ms. ticker has no seq. An update is sent whenever any ticker field changes, including size-only changes (since Feb 12, 2026). Setting send_initial_snapshot:true makes the subscription start with a current ticker message for each requested market.
facts.quote:
dollar_volume:
  type: integer
  description: Signed whole-dollar cumulative traded notional

facts.fact: trade msg fields (sequenced): trade_id (UUID), market_ticker, yes_price_dollars and no_price_dollars (dollar strings, e.g. '0.3600' and '0.6400'), count_fp (contracts traded, 2 decimals), taker_outcome_side (yes|no), taker_book_side (bid|ask, where bid means yes), is_block_trade (bool) and ts_ms; taker_side is deprecated. Live REST /markets/trades on 2026-10-05 showed fractional prints such as count_fp '138.98', '228.36' and '4151.23', and sub-cent prices such as yes_price_dollars '0.9990' on KXGOLD15M-26OCT051400-00.
facts.quote:
count_fp:
  type: string
  description: Fixed-point contracts traded (2 decimals)

facts.fact: fill msg (private, no seq), sent immediately when one of your orders fills: trade_id (UUID, unique per fill), order_id, client_order_id (optional), market_ticker, exchange_index (shard), is_taker (bool), yes_price_dollars (dollar string, e.g. '0.7500'), count_fp (contracts filled, e.g. '278.00'), fee_cost (the exchange fee for this fill as a dollar string; the example has 6 decimals, '0.010000'), post_position_fp (your position after the fill, 2 decimals), outcome_side (yes|no), book_side (bid|ask), ts_ms, subaccount (optional). The side, action and purchased_side fields are deprecated.
facts.quote:
fee_cost:
  type: string
  description: Exchange fee paid for this fill in fixed-point dollars

facts.fact: user_order msg (private, no seq) is sent when your orders are created, filled, canceled or otherwise updated. Fields: order_id, ticker, exchange_index, status (resting | canceled | executed | unknown), outcome_side, book_side, yes_price_dollars (4 decimals), fill_count_fp, remaining_count_fp and initial_count_fp (2 decimals), taker_fill_cost_dollars, maker_fill_cost_dollars, taker_fees_dollars and maker_fees_dollars (6-decimal dollar strings), client_order_id, order_group_id, self_trade_prevention_type (taker_at_cross | maker), created_ts_ms, last_updated_ts_ms, expiration_ts_ms, last_update_reason (Decrease, Amend, MarginCancel, SelfTradeCancel, ExpiryCancel, CloseCancel, HaltCancel, Trade, PostOnlyCrossCancel, ReduceOnlyCancel, SettlementBoundsCancel), subaccount_number (0 = primary, 1-63).
facts.quote:
status:
  type: string
  description: Current order status
  enum: ["resting", "canceled", "executed", "unknown"]

facts.fact: market_position msg (private, no seq), sent when your position changes because of trades, settlements and so on: user_id, market_ticker, position_fp (net position, 2 decimals), position_cost_dollars, realized_pnl_dollars, fees_paid_dollars and position_fee_cost_dollars (dollar strings such as '50.0000'), volume_fp, subaccount. In REST, a negative position_fp means NO contracts and a positive one YES; the WS docs only say 'net position'.
facts.quote: All monetary values are returned as fixed-point dollar strings (`_dollars` suffix).

facts.fact: market_lifecycle_v2 accepts no market filter and covers every non-MVE market. event_type values: created, activated, deactivated, close_date_updated, determined, settled, price_level_structure_updated; separate metadata_updated messages also arrive on this channel, as do event_lifecycle (new events) and event_fee_update. Optional fields appear only on the matching event: open_ts, close_ts, determination_ts and settled_ts are Unix SECONDS; result; settlement_value (dollar string, e.g. '0.5000'); is_deactivated (trading paused on an open market); exchange_index (on created); price_level_structure plus price_ranges [{start, end, step} dollar strings].
facts.quote: enum: ["created", "deactivated", "activated", "close_date_updated", "determined", "settled", "price_level_structure_updated"]

facts.fact: Lifecycle rules that affect order handling. initialized becomes active silently when open_time passes, with no 'activated' event. Reactivating a paused (inactive) market cancels ALL of its resting orders. After close_time, every order operation, cancels included, is rejected with MARKET_INACTIVE, and resting orders are cancelled shortly after close. GET /markets/{ticker} may return 404 just after a 'created' event; retry with backoff.
facts.quote: Once `close_time` passes, all order operations, including cancellations, are rejected with `MARKET_INACTIVE`. Resting orders are cancelled shortly after close, and cancellation updates are published on the usual user channels.

facts.fact: order_group_updates (private, sequenced) fields: event_type (created | triggered | reset | deleted | limit_updated), order_group_id, contracts_limit_fp (2 decimals; only on created and limit_updated), ts_ms. An order group cancels all of its resting orders once filled contracts in a rolling 15-second window exceed its limit (1-1,000,000 whole contracts). New orders in the group are then rejected until it is reset. Order groups do not work across exchange shards. They make a useful kill switch for a test bot.
facts.quote: Order groups provide automatic order cancellation when a contracts limit is reached within a rolling 15-second window. When an order group is triggered, all resting orders in that group are canceled and no new orders can be placed until the group is reset.

facts.fact: cfbenchmarks_value (auth required; params.index_ids such as ['BRTI']) streams CF Benchmarks index values about once per second. Each message includes avg_60s_data. Only during the final minute before :00, :15, :30 and :45 it also includes last_60s_windowed_average_15min, the 60-second average the 15-minute crypto markets settle on. Values are strings with 8 decimals and timestamps are Unix ms. cfbenchmarks_value_5hz sends up to 5 ticks per second for BRTI, ETHUSD_RTI, SOLUSD_RTI, XRPUSD_RTI and DOGEUSD_RTI. pyth_value is a PAID feed: $1,000/month after a 7-day free trial. Its documented ticker table lists only metals and commodities, while the KXUSDJPY15M series lists Pyth as its settlement source.
facts.quote: The Pyth data feed costs **$1,000/month**, with the **first seven days free**.

facts.fact: GET /trade-api/v2/exchange/status is public (no auth). It returns exchange_active, trading_active, intra_exchange_transfers_active, exchange_estimated_resume_time (date-time, present only during maintenance), and exchange_index_statuses[] with exchange_index, description, exchange_active, trading_active and intra_exchange_transfers_active for each shard; the top-level fields describe shard 0. Live on 2026-10-05 every flag was true; the shards were 0 'Default', 1 'Combos', 2 'Crypto & Commodities' and 3 'Tennis, Baseball, Basketball'. Before sending an order, check trading_active for the market's own shard.
facts.quote: True if we are currently permitting trading on the exchange. This is true during trading hours and false outside exchange hours. Kalshi reserves the right to pause at any time in case issues are detected.

facts.fact: GET /trade-api/v2/exchange/schedule is public. It returns schedule.standard_hours[] (weekly sessions as 'HH:MM' in ET) and maintenance_windows[]. Live on 2026-10-05 the exchange was open 24 hours every day except Thursday, which had sessions 00:00-03:00 and 05:00-00:00. Every Thursday 3:00-5:00 AM ET is a trading pause: you cannot place or amend orders, but you can cancel, and resting orders stay unless they were placed with cancel_order_on_pause:true. A rarer exchange pause also blocks cancels. Rule 5.16: trading is available at all times outside maintenance windows.
facts.quote: Every **Thursday from 3:00 AM to 5:00 AM ET**, Kalshi runs scheduled maintenance. During this window, a **trading pause** is in effect. In rare cases, a more intensive maintenance may require a full **exchange pause** instead.

facts.fact: Cash is held separately on each exchange shard, and orders placed through the API do not pull funds across shards automatically. The docs say programmatic traders must pre-fund the target shard, either with the Intra Account Transfer API or at kalshi.com/account/exchange-indexes; only App and Web orders transfer cash automatically. Live /series data: KXBTC15M is on exchange_index 2 ('Crypto & Commodities'), while KXTEMPMIAH and KXUSDJPY15M are on 0. Auto-routing requires the market ticker. An auto-routed single REST write is billed to every shard's Write bucket; an explicit exchange_index >= 1 is billed only to that shard's bucket.
facts.quote: Kalshi's collateralization checks run within the matching engine. Programmatic traders must preallocate collateral on a given exchange shard before order placement.

facts.fact: Members can place fractional orders. count is a fixed-point string: requests accept 0-2 decimals ('1', '1.5', '0.25'), responses always show 2 decimals, and the minimum granularity is 0.01 contracts. Since Apr 17, 2026 every market supports fractional trading; the always-true fractional_trading_enabled field was removed on Jul 9, 2026. FIX OrderQty also accepts fractional quantities. The docs give no minimum order count or notional beyond the 0.01-contract granularity. Kalshi's own first-order example buys count '1' at price '0.0100'. Exceptions: order-group contracts_limit and margin exit-trigger counts must be whole contracts.
facts.quote: Fractional contract values (e.g., "2.50") are supported; the minimum granularity is 0.01 contracts.

facts.fact: Units. Prices are *_dollars fixed-point dollar strings: market data usually has 4 decimals ('0.5600'), requests accept 2-4, and responses can have up to 6, as in cost and fee fields like '0.010000'. Counts are *_fp strings with 2 decimals. Integer-cent and integer-count fields were removed from REST and WS payloads on Mar 12, 2026. Integer fields that remain: GetBalance balance and portfolio_value are integer CENTS (balance_dollars is the dollar string); settlement revenue is integer cents; subaccount transfers use amount_cents; incentive period_reward and max_reward_per_account are CENTI-CENTS ($0.0001 units); ticker dollar_volume and dollar_open_interest are whole dollars. FIX Price defaults to whole cents (1-99) unless the session sets UseDollars=Y.
facts.quote: Legacy integer count fields (with `_fp` equivalents) and integer cents price fields (with `_dollars` equivalents) will be **removed** from all REST and WebSocket response payloads on **March 12, 2026**

facts.fact: Each market's price_ranges array [{start, end, step}] defines its valid order prices; off-grid prices are rejected, and whole-cent prices are valid in every structure. Live KXBTC15M on 2026-10-05: price_level_structure 'tapered_deci_cent' with price_ranges [{start '0.0000', end '0.1000', step '0.0010'}, {start '0.1000', end '0.9000', step '0.0100'}, {start '0.9000', end '1.0000', step '0.0010'}], i.e. 0.1-cent ticks below 10c and above 90c. Contract terms give a Minimum Tick of $0.001 for CRYPTO and $0.01 for MIAWINDEX (KXTEMPMIAH) and FXUSDJPY. The Quick Start's 'price must be 1-99 cents' hint is out of date for sub-cent markets.
facts.quote: This is the source of truth for valid prices: any price on the grid is valid, and any off-grid price is rejected. Consume it dynamically per market and snap order and quote prices to the relevant band's `step`.

facts.fact: The three contract terms checked set no hard position limit. Each has the same Position Accountability Level: $25,000 per strike per Member (CRYPTO, MIAWINDEX, FXUSDJPY). Under Rule 5.18, if you exceed it you must give Compliance the information it asks for, and stop increasing or reduce the position if instructed. Rule 5.19 allows hard Position Limits only where a contract's terms specify one.
facts.quote: Position Accountability Level: The Position Accountability Level for the Contract shall be $25,000 per strike, per Member.

facts.fact: The REST and WS docs publish no maximum order size. FIX reject texts show that exchange-side limit checks exist: EXCEEDED_PER_MARKET_RISK_LIMIT, EXCEEDED_SELL_POSITION_FLOOR and INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE all map to 'Order exceeds limit'. Their thresholds are not documented. Orders must be fully funded (Rulebook 5.17(a)).
facts.quote: EXCEEDED_PER_MARKET_RISK_LIMIT - maps to OrdRejReason "Order exceeds limit"

facts.fact: Self-trade prevention is mandatory on REST V2 orders: self_trade_prevention_type is a required field. 'taker_at_cross' cancels your incoming order when it would hit your own resting order; any fills already matched stand. 'maker' cancels your resting order and keeps matching. FIX defaults to Taker At Cross. A self-trade cancel appears as last_update_reason SelfTradeCancel on user_orders, or as FIX text TAKER_/MAKER_CANCEL_FOR_SELF_TRADE_PREVENTION. Separately, Rulebook 5.17 forbids trades with no change of beneficial ownership (5.17(c)), wash trades (5.17(bb)) and spoofing (5.17(aa)).
facts.quote: `taker_at_cross` cancels the taker order when it would trade against another order from the same user; execution stops and any partial fills already matched are executed. `maker` cancels the resting maker order and continues matching.

facts.fact: REST and FIX share token buckets; WebSocket commands are limited separately. Basic tier: Read 200 tokens/s, Write 100 tokens/s. Costs: 10 tokens by default (order create, amend, and each order in a batch); 2 for a single cancel; 2 for cancel-all; 30 for the Advanced-upgrade call. The Basic Write bucket holds only 1 second of budget (100 tokens). Derived: Basic allows about 10 creates/s or 50 cancels/s sustained, and at most 10 orders per batch, because a whole batch must fit in the bucket at once. Advanced (300/300) is granted by POST /account/api_usage_level/upgrade once at least 1 of your last 100 orders was placed via API. A 429 has no Retry-After header and carries no penalty or cooldown.
facts.quote: Predictions Read buckets above Advanced, Perps Read buckets, and Basic-tier Write buckets hold one second of budget.

facts.fact: The rate-limit docs contradict each other in two places. (1) The rate-limits page says Write buckets above Basic hold three seconds of budget, while the GET /account/limits schema says 'two seconds'. Read bucket_capacity from GET /account/limits at runtime. (2) The docs give the 429 body as {"error": "too many requests"}, but an unauthenticated public GET on 2026-10-05 returned {"error":{"code":"too_many_requests","message":"too many requests"}} with no rate-limit headers. Handle both shapes.
facts.quote: 429 responses do not currently include `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-*` headers. There is no penalty or cooldown.

facts.fact: Kalshi publishes no order-to-trade ratio or cancel-rate rule beyond the token buckets. Rulebook 5.4 says an order rate limiter caps orders per second per member, and that members must keep adequate controls against excessive messaging. Rule 5.17(aa) bans spoofing. The Aug 22, 2026 changelog says post-only quoters who cross the book several times in short succession may be temporarily rate limited. Kalshi can also revoke LIP participation for abusive behavior.
facts.quote: Order rate limiter functionality will cap the maximum number of orders that may be submitted to the Exchange per second (or per a specific time period expressed in seconds) per Self-Clearing Member in order to prevent a risk of harm to the Company.

facts.fact: Erroneous-trade rule (Rulebook 5.11): a review request must arrive within 15 minutes of the trade and before expiration. Trades within 20 cents of Kalshi's fair value stand. If Kalshi cancels or adjusts a trade, the trader whose order caused it pays $3,000, refunded only if a platform malfunction was wholly to blame. A runaway bot cannot rely on its bad trades being reversed.
facts.quote: If Kalshi cancels or adjusts a Trade, the Trader whose order resulted in the cancellation or adjustment shall pay $3,000 to compensate Kalshi for administrative costs and any subsequent actions under this Rule

facts.fact: Orders match by price, then time (Rule 5.9). GET /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/queue_position returns queue_position_fp, the number of contracts queued ahead of your order (0-indexed, so first in line returns '0.00'). This is useful for measuring fill probability.
facts.quote: Kalshi's trading algorithms execute all trades by matching orders according first by price and then time priority.

facts.fact: LIP rewards need no opt-in: resting orders in an eligible market during an active reward period are scored automatically. Under the July 15, 2026 amendment (effective July 30, 2026), every Kalshi member is eligible except IBs, FCMs and customers trading through them; the earlier exclusions for Kalshi affiliates and members with a Market Maker Agreement were struck. The help article (updated 2026-09-25) still lists affiliates and employees as excluded and says non-U.S. users are ineligible. Nothing in the terms treats API orders differently from app orders, but this is implied rather than stated. The program runs until Jan 1, 2027 unless amended, and Kalshi can end it at any time.
facts.quote: “Eligible Participants” are all Kalshi members, except the following: Introducing Brokers, Futures Commission Merchants, and customers thereof when transacting via the IB or FCM.

facts.fact: LIP scoring under the terms effective July 30, 2026. (1) Kalshi takes one book snapshot per second at a random time. (2) For each side, it walks down from the best bid adding resting size until it reaches the Target Size (more than 100 and fewer than 20,000 contracts); YES asks count as NO bids. The Reference Price is the first level where cumulative size reaches 1/5 of the Target Size. (3) Each qualifying order scores Discount Factor^N x size, where N is the number of ticks below the Reference Price (0 if at or better). (4) Scores are normalized per side, and your snapshot score is your YES share plus your NO share. (5) A snapshot is excluded if the market is not open or either side falls short of the Target Size. (6) Payout = your share of all snapshot scores x Time Period Reward x (non-excluded snapshots / total snapshots). It is paid only if it reaches $1.00 for that Time Period, and is rounded down to the cent.
facts.quote: Each Time Period Liquidity Provider Score is multiplied by the Time Period Reward and the ratio of non-excluded snapshots to total snapshots, and if the result is greater than or equal to $1.00, the result is paid out to the corresponding user, rounded down to the nearest cent.

facts.fact: GET /trade-api/v2/incentive_programs is public. Filters: status (all|active|upcoming|closed|paid_out), type (all|liquidity|volume|margin_maker_volume|margin_taker_volume), limit (up to 10000), cursor. Units: period_reward is int64 CENTI-CENTS (1 = $0.0001); max_reward_per_account is also centi-cents; discount_factor_bps is basis points; target_size_fp is a contract string. Live on 2026-10-05: KXPALLADIUM15M-26OCT051400-00 had a program from 17:45 to 18:00Z with period_reward 200000 ($20.00 for 15 minutes), discount_factor_bps 5000 (0.50 per tick), target_size_fp '300.00' and incentive_description 'series_lip'. A KXCRYPTOLEAD15M program had target_size_fp '1000.00'.
facts.quote:
period_reward:
  type: integer
  format: int64
  description: Total reward for the period in centi-cents

facts.fact: Inference from the $1.00 floor: a very small test order will probably earn $0 in LIP rewards. On a 15-minute program paying $20 you need at least 5% of all qualifying snapshot score in that period to be paid anything; on a $5 program you need at least 20%. Your orders also count only when both sides of the book reach the Target Size. A tiny live test can prove order placement, cancels, fills and reconciliation, but it cannot prove LIP income.
facts.quote: if the result is greater than or equal to $1.00, the result is paid out to the corresponding user, rounded down to the nearest cent.

facts.fact: Each account has a location attestation date for API key use, returned as api_key_region_expiration_ts by GET /api_keys. After it expires, API keys cannot trade Sports, Elections or Entertainment markets. Weather, crypto and FX are not on that list.
facts.quote: Once this date has passed, API keys are not valid for trading Sports, Elections, and Entertainment markets.

facts.fact: You can hard-cap the money at risk by funding a numbered subaccount (1-63) and using an API key restricted to it. A restricted key can trade only that subaccount and cannot transfer funds or create subaccounts. Creating subaccounts requires Advanced API access (since May 12, 2026). Subaccount balances belong to one exchange shard.
facts.quote: A restricted key can only read and trade on that subaccount

facts.fact: Safety-related fields on CreateOrderV2 (POST /portfolio/events/orders): time_in_force is required (fill_or_kill | good_till_canceled | immediate_or_cancel); expiration_time is Unix SECONDS and only valid with good_till_canceled; with post_only, an order that would cross is cancelled (PostOnlyCrossCancel / POST_ONLY_CROSS) instead of trading; reduce_only is rejected unless time_in_force is immediate_or_cancel; cancel_order_on_pause cancels the order if trading pauses; order_group_id attaches the order to an order group. Cancel-all is DELETE /portfolio/events/orders, which covers all shards. Resubmitting a client_order_id that already exists returns 409, so retries with the same client_order_id are idempotent.
facts.quote: Newly placed orders may also be cancelled during the minute after the request.

facts.fact: REST portfolio endpoints (balance, orders, fills, positions) trail the matching engine slightly. Kalshi recommends combining the responses to your order requests with WebSocket data. GET /exchange/user_data_timestamp reports roughly when that REST data was last validated.
facts.quote: There is typically a short delay before exchange events are reflected in the API endpoints. Whenever possible, combine API responses to PUT/POST/DELETE requests with WebSocket data to obtain the most accurate view of the exchange state.

facts.fact: GET /trade-api/v2/live_data/weather/{city} is public and returns the minute-by-minute temperature index used to settle hourly temperature markets (Miami is first). Live on 2026-10-05: {city:'miami', config_version:'miami-temperature-v1.0-cal-20261005', units:'fahrenheit', timeseries:[{t:1791223200000, v:88.88, contributors:5, status:'normal'}, ... status 'degraded' when 4 contributors]}. t is Unix ms and v is degrees F rounded to 0.01; minutes where too few stations reported are omitted. The KXTEMPMIAH series note says 'The data shown is 5 minutes delayed.'
facts.quote: Values are Fahrenheit rounded to 0.01. Minutes where the index quorum failed carry no value and are never returned as points, so gaps in the series are real gaps.

facts.fact: A demo environment with mock funds exists: REST https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2, WS wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2. It needs its own demo API keys, and Kalshi warns demo prices and behavior may not match production. It is the only zero-risk place to test the WS, sequence and order flow.
facts.quote: The price and behavior of markets in the demo environment may not be reflective of those in real markets.

facts.fact: Kalshi's official starter repo (github.com/Kalshi/kalshi-starter-code-python, last commit 2025-03-07) has a WebSocket client that only subscribes to ticker and prints messages, with no seq or gap handling. The docs recommend generating your own client from openapi.yaml and asyncapi.yaml. The official SDKs are kalshi_python_sync and kalshi_python_async; Ed25519 keys need version 3.31.0 or later.
facts.quote: SDKs are updated periodically and may lag the API. Active traders should treat the REST [OpenAPI specification](https://docs.kalshi.com/openapi.yaml) and WebSocket [AsyncAPI specification](https://docs.kalshi.com/asyncapi.yaml) as the source of truth.

code_examples.purpose: Authenticated WebSocket connection and orderbook subscription. Verbatim excerpt from Kalshi's Quick Start; the trailing '...' marks where the message loop was cut. WS_URL here is demo. The signed path is always /trade-api/ws/v2, and the headers must be regenerated with a fresh timestamp on every reconnect.
code_examples.code:
import asyncio
import base64
import json
import time
import websockets
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization, hashes
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import padding
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

# Configuration
KEY_ID = "your_api_key_id"
PRIVATE_KEY_PATH = "path/to/private_key.pem"
MARKET_TICKER = "KXHARRIS24-LSV"  # Replace with any open market
WS_URL = "wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2"

def sign_text(private_key, text: str) -> str:
    """Sign message with the key's algorithm: Ed25519, or RSA-PSS for RSA keys"""
    message = text.encode('utf-8')
    if isinstance(private_key, Ed25519PrivateKey):
        signature = private_key.sign(message)
    else:
        signature = private_key.sign(
            message,
            padding.PSS(
                mgf=padding.MGF1(hashes.SHA256()),
                salt_length=padding.PSS.DIGEST_LENGTH
            ),
            hashes.SHA256()
        )
    return base64.b64encode(signature).decode('utf-8')

def create_headers(private_key, method: str, path: str) -> dict:
    """Create authentication headers"""
    timestamp = str(int(time.time() * 1000))
    msg_string = timestamp + method + path.split('?')[0]
    signature = sign_text(private_key, msg_string)

    return {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY": KEY_ID,
        "KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE": signature,
        "KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP": timestamp,
    }

async def orderbook_websocket():
    """Connect to WebSocket and subscribe to orderbook"""
    # Load private key
    with open(PRIVATE_KEY_PATH, 'rb') as f:
        private_key = serialization.load_pem_private_key(
            f.read(),
            password=None
        )

    # Create WebSocket headers
    ws_headers = create_headers(private_key, "GET", "/trade-api/ws/v2")

    async with websockets.connect(WS_URL, additional_headers=ws_headers) as websocket:
        print(f"Connected! Subscribing to orderbook for {MARKET_TICKER}")

        # Subscribe to orderbook
        subscribe_msg = {
            "id": 1,
            "cmd": "subscribe",
            "params": {
                "channels": ["orderbook_delta"],
                "market_ticker": MARKET_TICKER
            }
        }
        await websocket.send(json.dumps(subscribe_msg))
        ...
