code_examples.purpose: Live public REST responses captured 2026-10-05 around 18:00Z on unauthenticated GETs, quoted verbatim or as field excerpts. Raw copies are in the scratchpad folder kdocs_rt/live.

Illustrative helper, not Kalshi code. It encodes the documented rules: which frames carry seq, the get_snapshot resync (market_tickers only), terminal error codes 10 and 25, and snapping prices to price_ranges. It also relies on one unconfirmed assumption: a single seq counter per sid that also advances on ok, unsubscribed and error frames for that sid. Confirm that in demo before relying on it.

open_questions: How far does the WebSocket seq counter reach? Kalshi never says whether seq is one counter per sid (across all markets on that subscription) or one per market, or whether ok, unsubscribed and error frames advance the same counter. The schema examples point to one counter per sid that includes ok and unsubscribed frames. Verify against demo traffic before trusting a gap detector.

Which WebSocket limits apply, and at what values? Kalshi does not publish: markets per subscription (error 26), per-subscription command rate (error 27), the current connections-per-user cap (last stated in Sep 2025 as starting at 200), subscriptions per connection, a Pong timeout or idle-disconnect rule, or a freshness window for the signed handshake timestamp.
Are WebSocket orderbook_snapshot levels sorted ascending like REST? REST was confirmed live: ascending, best bid last, and depth=N returns the best N levels.

What is the maximum order size, and what thresholds sit behind the FIX rejects EXCEEDED_PER_MARKET_RISK_LIMIT and EXCEEDED_SELL_POSITION_FLOOR? Neither is published. Is there a minimum order notional beyond the 0.01-contract granularity, for example will count '0.01' at $0.01 (a $0.0001 order) be accepted? Test in demo.

Is an API order on shard 2 (KXBTC15M) rejected with INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE when funds sit only on shard 0? Docs say only App and Web orders transfer funds automatically, but this is untested. Would opting into target_balance_allocation auto-rebalancing (every 10 s) be a good enough workaround?

Several LIP details are unclear. On tapered sub-cent markets, does the discount factor's 'number of ticks' count $0.001 steps, which would make the penalty much steeper near 0 and 1? Are API orders treated exactly like app orders (implied, not stated)? Is there a minimum resting time? The terms say the $1.00 floor applies per Time Period; is a Time Period here the same as one program on one market? The help article still links to the Feb 11, 2026 terms, while the July 15, 2026 amendment (effective July 30) is the newest CFTC filing found.

Is there any order-to-trade or cancel-ratio policy beyond the token buckets, Rulebook 5.4's 'adequate controls' wording and the post-only crossing throttle? None is published, and the threshold for 'cross several times in short succession' is not given.

Two rate-limit doc conflicts are unresolved. Write buckets above Basic hold 3 s of budget per the rate-limits page but 'two seconds' per the GET /account/limits schema. The 429 body is documented as {error:'too many requests'}, but a public GET returned {error:{code:'too_many_requests',message:'too many requests'}}. The authenticated 429 shape was not observed.

Is USD/JPY available on the paid pyth_value channel? KXUSDJPY15M settles on Pyth, but the documented ticker table lists only metals and commodities. The feed costs $1,000/month, so under the project rules it needs the user's explicit approval.

Rulebook v1.29 (public S3, last modified 2026-08-17) is the newest version found. A later version could exist on kalshi.com/regulatory, which was not checked because kalshi.com rate-limits (HTTP 429).

verification.area: realtime_rules: adversarial check of the Kalshi Trade API v2 WebSocket and exchange-rules research. I re-fetched every source myself on 2026-10-05: docs.kalshi.com asyncapi.yaml, openapi.yaml v3.32.0, changelog.md through the Oct 8, 2026 entries, llms-full.txt, and the getting_started, websockets, api-reference and fix pages; rulebook v1.29, the CRYPTO, MIAWINDEX and FXUSDJPY contract-terms PDFs, and the CFTC LIP filing of July 15, 2026; the Kalshi help-center LIP article; GitHub Kalshi/kalshi-starter-code-python; and PyPI kalshi_python_sync/async. Live checks were public, unauthenticated GETs on api.elections.kalshi.com around 18:25Z. I sent no authenticated, order, portfolio or WebSocket requests.

checks.claim: Production WS is wss://external-api-ws.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2, and the shared host wss://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2 also works. Demo is wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2, and wss://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2 also works. Demo and production keys are separate, and the signed path is the same on every host.
checks.evidence: The separate page /getting_started/api_environments shows the same table and says: 'Credentials are not shared between environments, so demo API keys only work against demo endpoints and production API keys only work against production endpoints.' It also says: 'The host does not change the signature payload.' In asyncapi.yaml, servers.production has host external-api-ws.kalshi.com and pathname /trade-api/ws/v2. /websockets says: 'WebSocket connections use the same API key authentication and signing path as before. Only the hostname changes for the dedicated Trade API path.'

checks.claim: The handshake must include KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY, KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP (Unix ms) and KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE = base64(sign(timestamp+'GET'+'/trade-api/ws/v2')). Sign the path only, with no host or query. RSA keys use PSS/SHA-256 with MGF1-SHA256 and salt length equal to the digest length; Ed25519 keys work on WS since Sep 24, 2026. There is no unauthenticated WebSocket.
checks.evidence: The WS Quick Start shows 'KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP: unix_timestamp_in_milliseconds' and the string to sign as timestamp + "GET" + "/trade-api/ws/v2". /getting_started/api_keys says: 'Ed25519 keys sign the string directly; RSA keys use RSA-PSS with SHA-256 (MGF1 with SHA-256, salt length equal to the digest length).' It also says to sign the path 'without query parameters'. The asyncapi root channel says: 'Some channels carry only public market data, but the connection itself still requires authentication.' The Sep 24, 2026 changelog says Ed25519 uses 'the same KALSHI-ACCESS-* headers and pre-sign text as RSA, with an Ed25519 signature in place of RSA-PSS, on REST, WebSocket and FIX'. Not in the research: the Oct 1, 2026 changelog says the web app 'now generates an Ed25519 key pair by default', and api_keys warns 'The PEM header does not identify the key type'.

checks.claim: The 13 valid channels are orderbook_delta, ticker, trade, fill, market_positions, market_lifecycle_v2, multivariate_market_lifecycle, communications, order_group_updates, user_orders, cfbenchmarks_value, cfbenchmarks_value_5hz and pyth_value.
checks.evidence: In asyncapi.yaml, subscribeCommandPayload.params.channels.items.enum lists exactly these 13 values. 'multivariate' is not among them.

checks.claim: orderbook_delta needs market_ticker or market_tickers; market_id is not supported, and omitting a market gives error 14. ticker and trade filters are optional, and ticker also accepts market_id(s). fill takes market_ticker(s), user_orders takes market_tickers, market_positions takes market_ticker(s) only. market_lifecycle_v2 takes no filter, and order_group_updates ignores filters. market_ticker and market_tickers are mutually exclusive. The private channels are fill, user_orders, market_positions, order_group_updates and communications, plus the own-order annotations on orderbook_delta.
checks.evidence: Each filter rule matches the asyncapi channel text: orderbook_delta '`market_id`/`market_ids` are not supported for this channel'; ticker 'Supports `market_ticker`/`market_tickers` and `market_id`/`market_ids`'; fill 'Market specification optional via `market_ticker`/`market_tickers`'; user_orders 'Market specification optional via `market_tickers`'; market_positions 'Filters are by `market_ticker`/`market_tickers` only'; market_lifecycle_v2 '(`market_ticker` filters are not supported)'; order_group_updates 'Market specification ignored'. The market_ticker param is '(mutually exclusive with market_tickers)'. The Quick Start describes error 14 as 'The command requires a market filter such as `market_ticker` or `market_tickers`.' Nuance: the Quick Start lists orderbook_delta itself as private ('Private channels (user-specific data): `orderbook_delta`, `fill`, `market_positions`, `communications`, `order_group_updates`'), and asyncapi marks orderbook_delta 'Authentication required'. The Jul 23, 2026 changelog says communications 'still broadcasts every RFQ'.

checks.claim: The Quick Start still lists the public 'multivariate' channel, which was removed on Aug 6, 2026; subscribing to it returns an unknown-channel error (code 8).
checks.evidence: The WS Quick Start still lists 'Public market-data channels (no additional channel-level auth): `ticker`, `trade`, `market_lifecycle_v2`, `multivariate_market_lifecycle`, `multivariate`'. The Aug 6, 2026 changelog says: 'The `multivariate` WebSocket channel (message type `multivariate_lookup`) no longer exists. Subscriptions to it now return an unknown-channel error.' Code 8 is 'Unknown channel name'.

checks.claim: Commands are {id, cmd, params}; the client picks id, and 0 means no id. subscribe returns 'subscribed' with {channel, sid}. unsubscribe takes sids and returns 'unsubscribed' with sid and seq. update_subscription targets exactly one sid, via sid or a one-element sids; its actions are add_markets, delete_markets and get_snapshot, and it returns 'ok' with the full market_tickers list (omitted when skip_ticker_ack is set). list_subscriptions returns 'ok' with [{channel, sid}]. sids belong to one session.
checks.evidence: Every part matches the asyncapi schemas. commandId says: 'If the id is set to 0, the server treats it the same way as if there was no id.' unsubscribedResponsePayload requires ['sid','seq','type']. updateSubscription sids is 'Array containing exactly one subscription ID (alternative to sid). Either sid or sids must be provided, not both.' (maxItems 1), and its action enum is [add_markets, delete_markets, get_snapshot]. In the ok reply, msg.market_tickers is 'Full list of market tickers after update'. skip_ticker_ack: 'If true, OK responses omit the market_tickers/market_ids lists'. listSubscriptionsResponsePayload has type const 'ok'. The session scope is backed by the Quick Start text for code 7: 'The command references a subscription ID that is not active in the session.' The cfbenchmarks and pyth channels also have their own actions: subscribe_indices, unsubscribe_indices, indexlist, subscribe_underlyings, unsubscribe_underlyings and underlying_list.

checks.claim: The error codes are 1-5, 7-15 and 18-28, with 6, 16 and 17 retired. Codes 10 and 25 are terminal. Subscription-scoped errors carry sid, plus seq on sequenced channels.
checks.evidence: errorResponse.code lists 23 'Match IDs required', 24 'Index IDs required', 25 'Subscription buffer overflow', 26 'Subscription market limit exceeded', 27 'Too many requests - The subscription exceeded its command rate limit' and 28 'Underlying tickers required'. It says: 'Codes 6, 16, and 17 are retired.' Per the schema, sid is 'Present when the error is scoped to a subscription.' and seq is 'Present on subscription-scoped errors on sequenced channels.' The Terminal Errors table says: 'The following channel errors are terminal and the user must resubscribe.' It lists 10 and 25.

checks.claim: Most WS limits are undocumented: Kalshi does not publish the markets-per-subscription cap behind error 26 or the per-subscription command rate behind error 27. The last published connection cap is from Sep 18, 2025: 200 per user by default.
checks.corrected_fact: Kalshi published WS limits after Sep 2025. The June 18, 2026 changelog (tags WebSocket, Predictions) says: 'Sanity limits enforced on orderbook subscriptions: Max 500k market subscriptions per session. Max 10k/s commands per second enforced.' The Sep 18, 2025 entry (default 200 connections per user, rising with tier) is still the only statement on connection count. Exact thresholds for the per-subscription codes 26 and 27 are not stated separately. None of these limits matter for a tiny bot.
checks.evidence: changelog.md, entry dated June 18, 2026 and titled 'Sanity limits enforced on orderbook subscriptions'. The same text appears in llms-full.txt.

checks.claim: Messages are capped at 64 MiB. permessage-deflate is optional and only used if the client offers it. Connections per user start at 200 and rise with tier. Error 25 means the subscription was too broad or the client read too slowly.
checks.evidence: The Sep 24, 2026 changelog says: 'Public WebSocket connections support RFC 7692 `permessage-deflate` compression when the client offers it during the opening handshake. Clients can choose to remain uncompressed by omitting `permessage-deflate`... Message formats and the 64 MiB message limit are unchanged.' The May 12, 2026 changelog says code 25 is returned 'when a subscription's event buffer overflows during a message burst... subscribe to a smaller subset of data, or ensure that your connection read throughput is optimized.' Note: the Python websockets client offers permessage-deflate by default.

checks.claim: The snapshot is sent first, and again in reply to get_snapshot (carrying id). msg holds market_ticker, market_id, yes_dollars_fp and no_dollars_fp as [price_dollars, count_fp] string pairs. A side's key is missing when that side is empty. WS level ordering is not documented.
checks.evidence: orderbookSnapshotPayload requires ['type','sid','seq','msg']. Its id field is 'Present when replying to a get_snapshot command with an ID'. yes_dollars_fp is described as 'Optional - This key will not exist if there are no Yes offers in the orderbook. Price levels represented as [price_in_dollars, contract_count_fp].' The example is yes_dollars_fp [["0.0800","300.00"],["0.2200","333.00"]]. The channel text says 'Sends `orderbook_snapshot` first, then incremental `orderbook_delta` updates'. I found no WS ordering statement in asyncapi or llms-full.txt. Watch the key names: WS uses yes_dollars_fp and no_dollars_fp, while REST uses orderbook_fp.yes_dollars and no_dollars.

checks.claim: Delta fields are price_dollars, delta_fp (signed, 2 decimals), side, ts_ms (with ts deprecated) and market_ticker/market_id. client_order_id and subaccount appear only when your own order caused the change.
checks.evidence: The delta msg requires market_ticker, market_id, price_dollars ('Price level in dollars'), delta_fp ('Fixed-point contract delta (2 decimals)') and side. client_order_id is described as 'Optional - Present only when you caused this orderbook change.' subaccount is 'Present only when you caused this orderbook change and are using subaccounts.' ts is 'Deprecated ... Use ts_ms instead.' ts_ms is 'Optional - Unix timestamp ... (in milliseconds)'. The example has price_dollars "0.9600" and delta_fp "-54.00".

checks.claim: By default, NO-side WS levels use NO-leg prices. use_yes_price:true reports them at YES-leg prices instead (0.30 becomes 0.70). The default will flip later, with no dates announced. The REST book lists bids only, and best YES ask = 1 - best NO bid.
checks.evidence: order_direction: 'a no-side delta at `price_dollars=0.30` corresponds to a market offer of "no at 30c", which would match against "yes at 70c"'. With the flag set, the level 'is instead reported as `0.70` (yes-leg)'. It also says: 'The default for `use_yes_price` will be flipped to `true` in a future release... We will announce concrete dates for both steps before they happen'. orderbook_responses: 'Kalshi's orderbook only returns bids, not asks', and the best YES ask is '$1.00 - (Highest price in the `no_dollars` array)'.

checks.claim: GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook needs no auth. It returns orderbook_fp.yes_dollars and orderbook_fp.no_dollars sorted ascending with the best bid last. depth=N returns the best N levels, and sub-cent edge levels go down to 0.0010.
checks.evidence: orderbook_responses: 'No authentication is required for this endpoint.', 'Arrays are sorted by price in **ascending order**', 'The **highest** bid (best bid) is the **last** element in each array'. I repeated the live check at 18:25Z on the same ticker, KXBTC15M-26OCT051430-30. depth=3 returned {"orderbook_fp":{"no_dollars":[["0.0510","6572.00"],["0.0520","1898.06"],["0.0530","1422.93"]],"yes_dollars":[["0.9440","188.00"],["0.9450","10.00"],["0.9460","723.81"]]}}. The full book had 210 YES and 53 NO levels, both strictly ascending and both starting at 0.0010.

checks.claim: A /markets top-of-book read differed from an orderbook read seconds later, so treat /markets bid/ask as indicative only.
checks.evidence: I saw the same kind of gap: /markets yes_bid_dollars was 0.9390, and the orderbook's best YES bid was 0.9460 seconds later. But this was the final minutes of a fast-moving 15-minute BTC market, so a stale field and real price movement look the same. No doc says /markets top-of-book is delayed. Treating it as indicative is prudent but undocumented.

checks.claim: seq is an integer >= 1. It appears on snapshot/delta, trade, lifecycle (including metadata_updated), MVE lifecycle, event_lifecycle, event_fee_update, order_group_updates, RFQ/quote and cfbenchmarks/pyth messages, on unsubscribed replies, optionally on ok replies, and on subscription-scoped errors. ticker, fill, user_order and market_position have no seq.
checks.evidence: sequenceNumber is described as 'Sequential number that should be checked if you want to guarantee you received all the messages. Used for snapshot/delta consistency', with minimum 1. seq is required on every payload listed. tickerPayload, fillPayload, userOrderPayload and marketPositionPayload each require only ['type','sid','msg'] and have no seq property.

checks.claim: Kalshi publishes no gap-recovery procedure. get_snapshot (added Apr 20, 2026) returns a fresh snapshot without changing the subscription and accepts only market_tickers. Errors 10 and 25 require resubscribing.
checks.evidence: The Apr 20, 2026 changelog says: 'Sends an `orderbook_snapshot` response for the requested markets without adding them to the subscription or affecting the existing delta stream.' and 'Only `market_tickers` is supported (not `market_ticker`, `market_id`, or `market_ids`).' A search of llms-full.txt found no WS gap-recovery guidance; the only resend rules are for FIX.

checks.claim: Inference: there is one seq counter per sid that also advances on ok and unsubscribed frames.
checks.evidence: The AsyncAPI examples (snapshot sid 2 seq 2, delta seq 3, ok sid 456 seq 222, unsubscribed sid 2 seq 7) are separate illustrative payloads, not one stream. The schema does show that get_snapshot replies, ok replies and unsubscribed replies carry sid and seq, which fits the hypothesis without stating it. Nothing says whether seq counts per sid or per market. This has to be measured in demo.

checks.claim: Since Sep 17, 2026 the 'subscribed' ack always arrives before data. Before that fix, the first event right after the ack could be lost.
checks.corrected_fact: Wording correction: the ack already came before data ('The acknowledgement continues to precede subscription data'). The Sep 17, 2026 fix only stopped events that arrived right after the ack from being skipped.
checks.evidence: The Sep 17, 2026 changelog says: 'Fixed a race that could skip events arriving immediately after a `subscribed` response, including on the `cfbenchmarks_value_5hz` channel. The acknowledgement continues to precede subscription data.'

checks.claim: Kalshi sends a Ping with body 'heartbeat' every 10 s and the client answers with a Pong; Python websockets does this automatically. No Pong timeout is documented. Reconnect with backoff, and expect disconnects during Thursday 3-5 AM ET maintenance.
checks.evidence: The keep-alive page has the quoted text, and in asyncapi the outgoingPing payload is const 'heartbeat'. The Quick Start says: 'The Python `websockets` library automatically handles WebSocket ping/pong frames to keep connections alive.' and 'Implement automatic reconnection with exponential backoff'. The maintenance page says: 'Clients should be prepared for session disconnections during this window and reconnect after 5:00 AM ET.' I found no Pong-timeout or idle rule in llms-full.txt.

checks.claim: Since Oct 1, 2026, every WS message carries a top-level sending_ts_ms (int64 Unix ms). Event times are in msg.ts_ms. The seconds-based and RFC3339 ts/time fields are deprecated.
checks.evidence: The Oct 1, 2026 changelog says: 'WebSocket messages now include `sending_ts_ms`.' sendingTimestampMs is 'type: integer, format: int64 ... Unix timestamp in milliseconds when Kalshi queued this message at the network layer.' ts and time are marked deprecated with 'Use ts_ms instead.'

checks.claim: ticker fields and units: price_dollars, yes_bid_dollars and yes_ask_dollars (dollar strings); yes_bid_size_fp, yes_ask_size_fp, last_trade_size_fp, volume_fp and open_interest_fp (2-decimal contract strings); dollar_volume and dollar_open_interest (signed integer whole dollars); ts_ms. There is no seq. Size-only changes trigger updates since Feb 12, 2026. send_initial_snapshot gives a current ticker message per market at subscribe.
checks.evidence: The tickerPayload field descriptions match each unit listed. dollar_volume: 'Signed whole-dollar cumulative traded notional'. The Feb 12, 2026 changelog says: 'Size changes (even without price changes) now trigger ticker updates.' send_initial_snapshot: 'If true, receive an initial snapshot for requested market tickers on the ticker channel'.

checks.claim: trade fields: trade_id, market_ticker, yes_price_dollars and no_price_dollars, count_fp (2 decimals), taker_outcome_side, taker_book_side, is_block_trade and ts_ms, with taker_side deprecated. Fractional prints and sub-cent prices occur live.
checks.evidence: The tradePayload required fields match, and count_fp is 'Fixed-point contracts traded (2 decimals)'. taker_side is deprecated. My live /markets/trades check at 18:25:18Z on KXBTC15M-26OCT051430-30 returned count_fp values "0.10", "2.51" and "0.01" with yes_price_dollars "0.9460", and taker_book_side 'bid' paired with taker_outcome_side 'yes'.

checks.claim: fill (private, no seq) has trade_id, order_id, client_order_id, market_ticker, exchange_index, is_taker, yes_price_dollars, count_fp, fee_cost (dollar string, 6 decimals in the example), post_position_fp, outcome_side, book_side, ts_ms and subaccount. side, action and purchased_side are deprecated.
checks.evidence: fillPayload requires ['type','sid','msg']. fee_cost is 'Exchange fee paid for this fill in fixed-point dollars', and the example is "0.010000". trade_id: 'Unique identifier for fills. This is what you use to differentiate fills'. REST GET /portfolio/fills describes trade_id as 'legacy field name, same as fill_id', so the same ID works as a dedupe key across WS and REST.

checks.claim: user_order (private, no seq) carries status (resting|canceled|executed|unknown) and the listed fields and units. last_update_reason takes 11 values, and subaccount_number is 0 for primary or 1-63.
checks.evidence: userOrderPayload requires ['type','sid','msg']. status enum: ["resting","canceled","executed","unknown"]. yes_price_dollars is '(4 decimals)', the counts are '(2 decimals)', and the cost and fee fields are '(6 decimals)'. The lastUpdateReason enum has the 11 values listed. subaccount_number: '(0 for primary, 1-63 for subaccounts)'. Note that this message uses 'ticker', not 'market_ticker'.

checks.claim: market_position (private, no seq) has user_id, market_ticker, position_fp, the *_dollars money fields and volume_fp. In REST, a negative position means NO contracts.
checks.evidence: marketPositionPayload requires ['type','sid','msg']. The channel says: 'All monetary values are returned as fixed-point dollar strings (`_dollars` suffix).' position_fp is 'Fixed-point net position (2 decimals)'. REST GET /portfolio/positions describes position_fp: 'Negative means NO contracts and positive means YES contracts'.

checks.claim: market_lifecycle_v2 takes no filter and covers non-MVE markets. Its event_types are created, activated, deactivated, close_date_updated, determined, settled and price_level_structure_updated; metadata_updated, event_lifecycle and event_fee_update messages also arrive on it. The *_ts fields are Unix seconds, and settlement_value is a dollar string.
checks.evidence: event_type enum: ["created","deactivated","activated","close_date_updated","determined","settled","price_level_structure_updated"]. marketMetadataUpdatedPayload event_type is const 'metadata_updated'. eventFeeUpdate is 'Delivered on the `market_lifecycle_v2` channel only.' open_ts is '(in seconds)'. settlement_value is 'fixed-point dollars (e.g. "0.5000")'. The market_lifecycle page says the channel covers 'All markets except MVE (`KXMVE*`)'.

checks.claim: initialized becomes active silently, with no 'activated' event. Reactivating a paused market cancels all its resting orders. After close_time all order operations, cancels included, get MARKET_INACTIVE. GET /markets/{ticker} can 404 right after a 'created' event.
checks.evidence: /getting_started/market_lifecycle says: 'There is no `activated` WebSocket event for this transition.'; 'All resting orders are cancelled on this reactivation.'; 'Once `close_time` passes, all order operations, including cancellations, are rejected with `MARKET_INACTIVE`.'; FAQ: 'The market may not be queryable immediately after a `created` event. Retry with backoff.'

checks.claim: order_group_updates is private and sequenced; its event_types are created, triggered, reset, deleted and limit_updated. An order group cancels its resting orders when 15-second rolling fills exceed the limit (1-1,000,000 whole contracts), and blocks new orders until reset. Groups do not work across shards. Useful as a kill switch.
checks.corrected_fact: Two additions. (1) POST /portfolio/order_groups/create has an exchange_index that 'Defaults to 0', so a group for a shard-2 market (KXBTC15M, KXGOLD15M) must be created with exchange_index 2. (2) contracts_limit is 'Whole contracts only' with a minimum of 1, and the group triggers only when the rolling total 'exceeds the limit'. It therefore cannot stop a sub-1-contract test of about $0.25.
checks.evidence: orderGroupUpdatesPayload requires seq, and its event_type enum has those five values. /getting_started/order_groups says: 'Create a group with a contracts limit (1–1,000,000)' and 'If the rolling total exceeds the limit, the group is triggered'. In openapi.yaml, CreateOrderGroupRequest.exchange_index is 'Defaults to 0.' The sharding FAQ says: 'Order groups do not function across exchange instances.'

checks.claim: cfbenchmarks_value needs auth and ticks about once per second. avg_60s_data is always present; last_60s_windowed_average_15min appears only in the final minute before each quarter hour. Values have 8 decimals and timestamps are Unix ms. The 5 Hz channel covers BRTI, ETHUSD_RTI, SOLUSD_RTI, XRPUSD_RTI and DOGEUSD_RTI. pyth_value costs $1,000/month after 7 free days, and its documented table lists only metals and commodities. KXUSDJPY15M settles on Pyth.
checks.evidence: asyncapi: 'Ticks are emitted roughly once per second'; '`last_60s_windowed_average_15min` (present only in the final minute before quarter-hour close: `:00`, `:15`, `:30`, `:45`)'; values are 'formatted to 8 decimal places'. 5Hz: 'It carries BTC (`BRTI`), ETH (`ETHUSD_RTI`), SOL (`SOLUSD_RTI`), XRP (`XRPUSD_RTI`), and DOGE (`DOGEUSD_RTI`)'. Pyth: 'The Pyth data feed costs **$1,000/month**, with the **first seven days free**.' Live /series/KXUSDJPY15M has settlement_sources [{"name":"Pyth"}].

checks.claim: last_60s_windowed_average_15min is 'the 60-second average the 15-minute crypto markets settle on'.
checks.evidence: asyncapi describes the averaging window as (close-60s, close] with up to 60 ticks but never says the field equals the official settlement value. KXBTC15M rules say 'the simple average of the sixty seconds of CF Benchmarks' BRTI before 2:30 PM EDT' and 'The official and final value is the average of these prices, rounded to the nearest 2 decimal places', while the feed value has 8 decimals. Treat the field as an estimate.

checks.claim: GET /exchange/status is public. It returns exchange_active, trading_active, intra_exchange_transfers_active, exchange_estimated_resume_time and per-shard exchange_index_statuses; the top-level fields describe shard 0. The live shards are 0 Default, 1 Combos, 2 Crypto & Commodities and 3 Tennis, Baseball, Basketball.
checks.evidence: Schema: 'The top-level fields above reflect the default exchange index (0). Absent when the per-index breakdown is unavailable.' exchange_estimated_resume_time is nullable. My unauthenticated GET at 18:25Z returned exactly the research's JSON: 4 shards, all flags true. Not in the research: exchange_index_statuses can be absent, in which case the shard-2 state is unknown.

checks.claim: /exchange/schedule is public, with times in ET. The exchange is open 24/7 except Thursday 3:00-5:00 AM ET. During the trading pause you can cancel but not place or amend orders, and resting orders stay unless cancel_order_on_pause is set. An exchange pause also blocks cancels. Rule 5.16 says trading is available at all times outside maintenance windows.
checks.evidence: My live GET returned the same schedule (thursday [{00:00-03:00},{05:00-00:00}], maintenance_windows []). The schedule docs say 'Opening time in ET (Eastern Time) format HH:MM.' The maintenance page table says Trading Pause 'Cancel orders | Yes', Exchange Pause 'No', and 'Remain on the book (unless CancelOrderOnPause is set)'. Rule 5.16(a): 'trading shall be available at all times outside of any maintenance windows'.

checks.claim: Cash is held per shard, and API orders do not pull funds across shards (only App and Web orders do). KXBTC15M is on shard 2, while KXTEMPMIAH and KXUSDJPY15M are on shard 0. Auto-routing needs the ticker. An auto-routed write is billed to every shard's Write bucket; an explicit exchange_index >= 1 only to that shard.
checks.evidence: The sharding page says: 'Programmatic traders must preallocate collateral on a given exchange shard before order placement.' It also says: 'orders placed through the Kalshi App and Web automatically transfer capital between exchange shards' (repeated in the Oct 8, 2026 changelog), and 'Auto-routing requires the market ticker... An order ID alone cannot identify the exchange shard.' The rate-limits page says: 'Auto-routed traffic (exchange_index: -1, or omitted when market_ticker is provided) is billed to every shard's Write bucket.' Live /series confirms KXBTC15M on 2 and KXTEMPMIAH and KXUSDJPY15M on 0. KXGOLD15M and KXPALLADIUM15M are also on 2.

checks.claim: count is a fixed-point string: requests take 0-2 decimals, responses show 2, and the minimum is 0.01. All markets are fractional since Apr 17, 2026, and fractional_trading_enabled was removed Jul 9, 2026. FIX OrderQty is fractional. No minimum order size or notional is documented. Kalshi's own first-order example is count '1' at '0.0100'. Order-group limits are whole contracts.
checks.evidence: FixedPointCount: 'Requests accept 0-2 decimal places... responses always emit 2 decimals... the minimum granularity is 0.01 contracts.' Apr 17, 2026: 'the field is always `true`'. The Jul 9, 2026 entry removed `Market.fractional_trading_enabled`. FIX OrderQty: 'Fractional quantities supported.' The create-order Quick Start uses "count": "1", "price": "0.0100". A search of llms-full.txt and openapi.yaml found no minimum or maximum order size; FIX error handling only mentions 'Position or order size limit'.

checks.claim: Prices are *_dollars strings: 4 decimals in market data, 2-4 accepted in requests, up to 6 in responses. Counts are 2-decimal *_fp strings. Integer cent and count fields were removed Mar 12, 2026. Integer fields that remain: balance and portfolio_value (cents), settlement revenue (cents), subaccount transfer amount_cents, incentive period_reward and max_reward_per_account (centi-cents), ticker dollar_volume (whole dollars). FIX prices are whole cents unless UseDollars=Y.
checks.corrected_fact: Two corrections. (1) A few legacy fields were temporarily restored on Mar 11, 2026 and only removed effective Apr 2, 2026: market_positions WS position_cost, realized_pnl, fees_paid and position_fee_cost (integer centi-cents), and settlements yes_total_cost and no_total_cost. (2) The list of integer fields is missing one that matters: POST /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfer takes 'amount' as an integer in CENTI-CENTS ('The amount to transfer in centicents', so $1.00 = 10000), while transfer records return 'amount' as a dollar string. Deposits and withdrawals use amount_cents and fee_cents.
checks.evidence: FixedPointDollars: 'Most request fields accept 2-4 decimal places... responses emit up to 6.' GetBalance balance is 'Member's available balance in cents'. Settlement revenue is 'in cents'. ApplySubaccountTransferRequest has amount_cents. IncentiveProgram period_reward is 'in centi-cents'. FIX Price: 'Whole cents (1–99) by default'. See the changelog entries for Mar 11 and Mar 25, 2026 ('Effective April 2, 2026'), and openapi.yaml IntraExchangeInstanceTransferRequest.

checks.claim: price_ranges is the source of truth for valid prices, and whole-cent prices are valid everywhere. KXBTC15M is tapered_deci_cent (0.001 ticks below 0.10 and above 0.90). The terms give CRYPTO a $0.001 tick and MIAWINDEX and FXUSDJPY $0.01. The Quick Start's '1-99 cents' hint is stale.
checks.evidence: fixed_point_migration: 'any price on the grid is valid, and any off-grid price is rejected' and 'Whole-cent prices are valid in every structure.' Live /markets/KXBTC15M-26OCT051430-30 price_ranges is [0.0000-0.1000@0.0010, 0.1000-0.9000@0.0100, 0.9000-1.0000@0.0010]. Live KXTEMPMIAH and KXUSDJPY15M markets are linear_cent, 0-1 in 0.01 steps. CRYPTO.pdf: 'The Minimum Tick size for the Contract shall be $0.001.' MIAWINDEX.pdf and FXUSDJPY.pdf: '$0.01.' The Quick Start still says '(price must be 1-99 cents)'.

checks.claim: None of the three contract terms sets a hard position limit. Each sets a Position Accountability Level of $25,000 per strike per Member. Rules 5.18 and 5.19 apply.
checks.evidence: All three PDFs say 'Position Accountability Level ... $25,000 per strike, per Member' and contain no Position Limit clause. Rule 5.18(c): 'must refrain from increasing the size of their position or reduce the size of their position in a timely fashion if instructed to do so by Kalshi.' Rule 5.19(a): Position Limits 'will be specified in each contract's Terms and Conditions'.

checks.claim: No maximum order size is published. FIX texts show undocumented exchange-side limits (EXCEEDED_PER_MARKET_RISK_LIMIT, EXCEEDED_SELL_POSITION_FLOOR, INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE all map to 'Order exceeds limit'). Orders must be fully funded (Rule 5.17(a)).
checks.evidence: FIX order-entry lists all three as mapping to OrdRejReason "Order exceeds limit". FIX error handling: '3 | Order exceeds limit | Position or order size limit, insufficient balance'. Rule 5.17(a): Members may not enter orders 'if there are insufficient funds or Contracts in the Member's Account to satisfy such Orders if they are executed'.

checks.claim: self_trade_prevention_type is required on V2 orders. taker_at_cross cancels the incoming order and keeps partial fills; maker cancels the resting order. FIX defaults to Taker At Cross. Cancels show as SelfTradeCancel or TAKER_/MAKER_CANCEL_FOR_SELF_TRADE_PREVENTION. Rule 5.17 bans trades with no change of beneficial ownership, wash trades and spoofing.
checks.evidence: CreateOrderV2Request required: [ticker, side, count, price, time_in_force, self_trade_prevention_type]. The SelfTradePreventionType text matches the research's quote. FIX tag 2964: '`1`=Taker At Cross (default), `2`=Maker'. The FIX Text list includes TAKER_CANCEL_FOR_SELF_TRADE_PREVENTION. Rule 5.17(c)a: 'Does not result in a change in beneficial ownership'; 5.17(aa) covers spoofing and 5.17(bb) wash trades.

checks.claim: Basic tier is Read 200 and Write 100 tokens/s, and its Write bucket holds 1 s of budget. Create, amend and each batch item cost 10 tokens; a cancel or a cancel-all costs 2; the Advanced upgrade costs 30. That allows about 10 creates/s, 50 cancels/s and at most 10 orders per batch. Advanced (300/300) needs at least 1 API order among your last 100. A 429 has no Retry-After header and no penalty. REST and FIX share buckets.
checks.evidence: The rate-limits page tiers table shows Basic 200/100 and Advanced 300/300. It says 'Most requests cost the default of **10 tokens**', 'Basic-tier Write buckets hold one second of budget', 'The whole batch must fit in the bucket at once', 'REST and FIX requests drain the same buckets' and '429 responses do not currently include `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-*` headers. There is no penalty or cooldown.' Cancel V2: '2 tokens per request'. Cancel All: '2 tokens per request, the same cost as cancelling one event-market order'. Upgrade: 'This endpoint costs 30 tokens' and 'at least 1 of the user's last 100 Predictions orders was created via API'. The derived numbers are plain arithmetic.

checks.claim: The rate-limits page says Write buckets above Basic hold 3 s of budget, but the GET /account/limits schema says 2 s. The documented 429 body is {"error": "too many requests"}, but the observed body was nested.
checks.evidence: The rate-limits page says Write buckets above Basic 'hold up to **three seconds of budget**', while the BucketLimit.bucket_capacity schema says '(e.g. write buckets at non-Basic tiers hold two seconds of budget)'. I reproduced the 429 independently at 18:25:21Z on an unauthenticated GET /markets: body {"error":{"code":"too_many_requests","message":"too many requests"}}, with no Retry-After or X-RateLimit headers and 'X-Cache: Error from cloudfront'. The OpenAPI RateLimitError schema is ErrorResponse {code, message, details}, which matches the nested shape. My 429 happened while this machine's background download jobs were also calling the API, which may be why I hit it.

checks.claim: No order-to-trade or cancel-ratio rule is published beyond the token buckets. Rule 5.4 covers an order rate limiter and 'adequate controls'; Rule 5.17(aa) bans spoofing. The Aug 22, 2026 changelog may rate-limit post-only quoters who cross repeatedly. LIP participation can be revoked for abuse.
checks.evidence: Rule 5.4(a)a and (d) say what the research quotes, including that members 'must ensure adequate controls are in place to prevent excessive messaging'. The CFTC LIP terms keep the right to 'revoke participant status' for abusive participation. Nuance: the Aug 22, 2026 entry is about the RFQ 'post-only on quotes' flag ('quoters with post-only set to true may be temporarily rate limited if they cross several times in short succession'). It is not about ordinary post_only limit orders on the book.

checks.claim: Under Rule 5.11, a review request must arrive within 15 minutes and before expiration. Trades within 20 cents of fair value stand. If Kalshi cancels or adjusts a trade, the trader who caused it pays $3,000.
checks.evidence: Rule 5.11(c): 'no later than fifteen (15) minutes after the trade has been executed on the Platform and before Expiration of the Contract'. 5.11(c)(ii): 'a twenty (20) cent range will be added above and below such fair market value'. 5.11(c)(v): 'shall pay $3,000'. Nuance: 5.11(d) gives a narrow, discretionary exception for advanced-API-tier members whose automated system malfunctioned despite 'reasonable safeguards'.

checks.claim: Orders match on price, then time. GET /portfolio/orders/{order_id}/queue_position returns queue_position_fp, the contracts ahead of you ('0.00' when first in line).
checks.evidence: Rule 5.9: 'matching orders according first by price and then time priority'. The schema describes queue_position_fp as 'The number of preceding shares before the order in the queue.' The changelog adds 'quantity of shares preceeeding the given order'.

checks.claim: No opt-in is needed. Under the July 15, 2026 amendment (effective July 30), every member except IBs, FCMs and their customers is eligible, with the affiliate and MM-agreement exclusions struck. The program runs until Jan 1, 2027 unless amended. The help article still excludes affiliates, employees and non-U.S. users. API and app orders are not distinguished.
checks.evidence: CFTC filing, clean terms: '“Eligible Participants” are all Kalshi members, except the following: Introducing Brokers, Futures Commission Merchants, and customers thereof when transacting via the IB or FCM.' The tracked version strikes '(i) affiliates of Kalshi; (ii) members who have executed a Market Maker Agreement'. It says 'This amendment will go into effect on July 30, 2026' and the program runs 'until the earlier of January 1, 2027, or the date that Kalshi amends or terminates the Program.' The help article lists 'Kalshi affiliates and employees' and 'International, non-U.S. users (ineligible for rewards)', links the Feb 11, 2026 terms, and adds 'A verified Social Security Number (SSN) must be on file to receive reward credits above annual IRS reporting thresholds.' Its date shows only as 'Updated over a week ago'. Neither source treats API and app orders differently.

checks.claim: The scoring algorithm in steps (1)-(6): one random snapshot per second; Target Size above 100 and below 20,000; Reference Price at 1/5 of target; DF^N x size per order; normalised per side; excluded snapshots; a $1.00 payment floor with rounding down.
checks.evidence: The CFTC terms contain each step: 'taken once for each second, with the exact time of the snapshot drawn from a random uniform distribution'; '“Target Size” will be greater than 100 contracts and less than 20,000 contracts'; 'greater than or equal to one fifth of the target size, then the Reference Yes Price is set'; 'a yes ask is counted as a bid for no'; 'N is the number of ticks between the Reference Yes Price and the price of the Qualifying Yes Bid... N is set to zero'; 'Snapshots will be excluded if a market is not open for trading or if there is not two-sided liquidity'; the payout clause. Two notes: the formula image writes the exponent as Max(Reference Price - Price(bid), 0), a price difference rather than a tick count, so the sub-cent tick question is still open; and the minimum Time Period Reward was cut from $10 to $1 per day.

checks.claim: GET /incentive_programs is public, with status, type, limit (up to 10000) and cursor filters. period_reward and max_reward_per_account are centi-cents, discount_factor_bps is basis points, and target_size_fp is a contract string.
checks.evidence: Spec: status enum [all, active, upcoming, closed, paid_out]; type enum [all, liquidity, volume, margin_maker_volume, margin_taker_volume]; 'Maximum value is 10000'; period_reward 'Total reward for the period in centi-cents'; max_reward_per_account 'in centi-cents'. There is also an incentive_description filter the research didn't list. My unauthenticated GET at 18:25Z returned the same field shapes, for example period_reward 1000000 ($100.00), discount_factor_bps 5000, target_size_fp "1000.00", incentive_description "series_lip".

checks.claim: KXPALLADIUM15M-26OCT051400-00 had a program from 17:45 to 18:00Z: period_reward 200000, discount_factor_bps 5000, target_size_fp '300.00'.
checks.evidence: That program ended at 18:00Z, before my check, so I could not see it. The unit arithmetic is right: 200000 centi-cents = $20.00, and 5000 bps = 0.50.

checks.claim: Because of the $1.00 floor, a tiny test will probably earn $0: you need at least 5% of a $20 period or 20% of a $5 period. Snapshots count only when both sides reach Target Size.
checks.evidence: Arithmetic on the CFTC payout formula: payout = share x reward x (non-excluded/total), paid only if it is >= $1.00. So share must be >= $1/(reward x ratio), which is at least 5% for $20 and 20% for $5. The exclusion rule covers the both-sides condition. This is an inference, but it follows directly from the terms.

checks.claim: GET /api_keys returns api_key_region_expiration_ts. After it passes, API keys cannot trade Sports, Elections or Entertainment, which does not include weather, crypto or FX.
checks.evidence: The Aug 16, 2026 changelog says it is 'the unix timestamp (seconds) when your location attestation for API key requests expires. Once this date has passed, API keys are not valid for trading Sports, Elections, and Entertainment markets. The field is absent when the account has never attested.' The research's 'each account has a date' overstates this, because the field is absent when the account has never attested.

checks.claim: You can cap money at risk with a funded numbered subaccount (1-63) and a key restricted to it, which cannot transfer funds or create subaccounts. Creating subaccounts needs Advanced tier (since May 12, 2026). Subaccount balances belong to one shard.
checks.evidence: The subaccounts page says: 'A restricted key can only read and trade on that subaccount' and 'A restricted key cannot transfer funds, manage subaccounts or API keys'. Create Subaccount: 'available to all users on the Advanced API tier and above'. The May 12, 2026 changelog has the matching entry. Sharding FAQ: 'Subaccount balances are local to a specific exchange instance.' Not in the research: 'Subaccounts are currently an **API-only** feature'; CreateSubaccountRequest exchange_index 'Defaults to 0 if unspecified'; and since Jul 23, 2026 restricted keys can open WS sessions, with private channels scoped to their subaccount.

checks.claim: Order flags on POST /portfolio/events/orders: time_in_force is required (fill_or_kill, good_till_canceled or immediate_or_cancel); expiration_time is in Unix seconds and only valid with GTC; post_only cancels on cross; reduce_only requires IOC; cancel_order_on_pause and order_group_id are available. Cancel-all is DELETE /portfolio/events/orders across all shards. A duplicate client_order_id gets 409, so retries are idempotent.
checks.evidence: The CreateOrderV2Request enum and descriptions match. expiration_time is 'Optional Unix timestamp in seconds'. reduce_only: 'Orders with reduce_only set to true will be rejected unless time_in_force is immediate_or_cancel.' Cancel-all is 'across every exchange shard'. The Quick Start says: '`409 Conflict`: Order with this `client_order_id` already exists'. Nuances: the docs only forbid IOC with expiration ('The `immediate_or_cancel` time-in-force value cannot be combined with `expiration_time`'). A crossing post-only order may come back as an HTTP error rather than a 201; the Oct 24, 2025 changelog shows error 'invalid order' / 'post only cross'.

checks.claim: REST portfolio data lags the matching engine. Kalshi recommends combining REST write responses with WS data. GET /exchange/user_data_timestamp shows roughly when REST data was last validated.
checks.evidence: openapi /exchange/user_data_timestamp: 'Whenever possible, combine API responses to PUT/POST/DELETE requests with WebSocket data... This endpoint provides an approximate indication of when the data from the following endpoints was last validated: GetBalance, GetOrder(s), GetFills, GetPositions'.

checks.claim: GET /live_data/weather/{city} is public. t is Unix ms, v is °F to 0.01, status is normal or degraded, and minutes that fail quorum are omitted. The KXTEMPMIAH note says the data is 5 minutes delayed.
checks.evidence: The docs match every field. My unauthenticated GET /live_data/weather/miami?last_sec=1800 at 18:25Z returned config_version 'miami-temperature-v1.0-cal-20261005', units 'fahrenheit', and points such as {"contributors":5,"status":"normal","t":1791223200000,"v":88.88} and {"contributors":4,"status":"degraded",...}. Live /series/KXTEMPMIAH says: 'The data shown is 5 minutes delayed.' The docs define 'degraded' as 'a member was absent, fallback-fed, or substituted by quality control', which can happen even when 5 stations contribute.

checks.claim: A demo environment with mock funds exists (REST external-api.demo.kalshi.co, WS external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co). It needs separate keys, and demo behaviour may differ from production.
checks.evidence: demo_env: 'Kalshi offers a *demo* environment with mock funds', with the endpoint table and the warning 'The price and behavior of markets in the demo environment may not be reflective of those in real markets.' api_environments covers the separate credentials.

checks.claim: The starter repo was last committed 2025-03-07; its WS client subscribes only to ticker and prints messages, with no seq handling. The docs recommend generating your own client from the specs. The SDKs are kalshi_python_sync and kalshi_python_async, and Ed25519 needs version 3.31.0 or later.
checks.evidence: The GitHub API shows pushed_at 2025-03-07T18:17:48Z, last commit 08fd693c. clients.py subscribes only to ["ticker"], on_message only prints, and it signs RSA-PSS only (sign_pss_text), so it cannot use an Ed25519 key. The SDK page says: 'we recommend generating your own client from those specs' and 'Ed25519 keys need SDK 3.31.0 or later'. PyPI kalshi_python_sync and async 3.31.0 were uploaded 2026-09-29, one version behind openapi 3.32.0.

checks.claim: Example 1 is verbatim from the Quick Start. Examples 2-4 are AsyncAPI examples converted to JSON. Example 5 captures live public responses.
checks.evidence: Example 1 matches /getting_started/quick_start_websockets up to the cut. Examples 2-4 match the asyncapi.yaml message examples field for field; the use_yes_price line is correctly labelled as constructed. My own GETs at 18:25Z returned identical /exchange/status and /exchange/schedule bodies, the same KXBTC15M market structure (exchange_index 2, notional_value_dollars 1.0000, settlement_timer_seconds 1, tapered_deci_cent) and the same 429 body.

checks.claim: The helper encodes the documented rules (which frames carry seq, get_snapshot takes market_tickers only, terminal codes 10 and 25, snapping prices to price_ranges) plus one unconfirmed seq-counter assumption.
checks.evidence: The documented parts match the spec (see the checks above). Three caveats. (1) The per-sid counter assumption cannot be verified. (2) snap() can return 0.0000 (bid floor in the first band) or 1.0000 (ask ceiling in the last band); these are edges of the grid, not sensible order prices, so clamp strictly inside (0,1). (3) SidSeq keeps entries for dead sids after a reconnect; reset it whenever a session or subscription is recreated.

missing_critical: Cancels on non-zero shards. DELETE /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id} routes by exchange_index: 'If omitted, auto-routes when market_ticker is provided; otherwise defaults to 0', and 'An `order_id` alone cannot identify the exchange shard'. Its subaccount parameter also defaults to 0. KXBTC15M, KXGOLD15M and KXPALLADIUM15M are on exchange_index 2 (live /series). Send market_ticker, or exchange_index=2, on every cancel, amend, decrease and batch-cancel item. Otherwise the cancel goes to shard 0 (likely a 404) and the order keeps resting. Source: https://docs.kalshi.com/api-reference/orders/cancel-order-v2

Order-group kill switch. POST /portfolio/order_groups/create takes exchange_index, which 'Defaults to 0', and 'Order groups do not function across exchange instances', so create the group on the market's own shard. contracts_limit is 'Whole contracts only' (minimum 1) and triggers only when the rolling 15-second total exceeds it, so it can never stop a $0.25 test of under 1 contract. The real hard cap is the cash on the target shard or subaccount, because Rule 5.17(a) requires full funding. Keep target_balance_allocation auto-rebalancing (opt-in, runs every 10 s) off so that cash is not topped up.

V2 order direction. CreateOrderV2 side is BookSide: 'For event markets, this refers to the YES leg only: `bid` means buy YES, `ask` means sell YES', and price is the YES price. To buy NO at p, send side=ask with price=1-p. Required fields: ticker, side, count (fp string), price (dollar string, 2-4 dp), time_in_force, self_trade_prevention_type. The 201 response returns fill_count and remaining_count as fixed-point strings without the _fp suffix.

Shard funding units. POST /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfer takes amount as an integer in CENTI-CENTS ('The amount to transfer in centicents', so $1.00 = 10000). source and destination are exchange instances (event_contract or margined); the shard numbers go in source_exchange_shard and destination_exchange_shard, which default to 0. The transfer 'is processed asynchronously' (status pending or complete), and transfer records report amount as a dollar string. Poll GET /portfolio/intra_exchange_instance_transfers/{transfer_id} until it is complete, and check intra_exchange_transfers_active first.

Cancel-all side effect. DELETE /portfolio/events/orders cancels on every shard, and 'Newly placed orders may also be cancelled during the minute after the request'. Wait 60 s after a cancel-all before placing new orders, or expect them to be cancelled.

Cancel and amend response bodies are not reliable. The May 21, 2026 changelog says: 'In certain uncommon cases, responses from `DELETE /trade-api/v2/portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}` and `POST .../amend` do not describe the order that was cancelled or amended'. I found no later entry saying this was fixed, through Oct 8, 2026. Confirm each cancel through user_orders (status canceled) or GET /portfolio/orders/{order_id}.

Ambiguous creates. POST /portfolio/events/orders documents 500 and 503 responses, and after a timeout or 5xx the order may still exist. GET /portfolio/orders has no client_order_id filter, so filter by ticker and min_ts and match on client_order_id (a required Order field). Alternatively resubmit with the same client_order_id; a 409 means the order already exists. FIX documents the same pattern: EXCHANGE_UNAVAILABLE 'could not confirm whether the order was applied... Reconcile the order's state, or retry with the same ClOrdID'.

Empty-side placeholders on REST /markets. An empty side still shows a price, with size zero. Live example: KXTEMPMIAH-26OCT0515-T91.99 had yes_bid_dollars "0.0000" with yes_bid_size_fp "0.00"; the research's own KXBTC15M excerpt had yes_ask_dollars "1.0000" with yes_ask_size_fp "0.00". Never quote or compute edge from these values.

Key type. Since Oct 1, 2026 the web app 'generates an Ed25519 key pair by default'. The official starter repo signs RSA-PSS only, and SDKs before 3.31.0 cannot sign with Ed25519. 'The PEM header does not identify the key type', so detect it from the parsed key object.

Crossing post-only orders. The Oct 24, 2025 changelog says a crossing post-only order returns error code 'invalid order' with details 'post only cross', 'consistent with single order creation'. The June 4, 2026 entry says order records show last_update_reason PostOnlyCrossCancel. Handle both an HTTP error and a canceled order record.

Field-name traps for reconciliation. WS fill.trade_id equals the REST fill's trade_id ('legacy field name, same as fill_id'); use it as the fill dedupe key. user_order uses 'ticker', while fill and market_position use 'market_ticker'. The REST book is orderbook_fp.yes_dollars and no_dollars; the WS snapshot uses yes_dollars_fp and no_dollars_fp. Private WS streams carry no seq, so reconcile over REST after every reconnect.

Fees on tiny fractional fills. Per /getting_started/fee_rounding, the trade fee is rounded up to $0.000001, and then a rounding fee re-aligns a direct member's balance to $0.0001 (with rebates via a per-order accumulator). The series show fee_type 'quadratic' and fee_multiplier 1 for KXBTC15M, KXTEMPMIAH and KXUSDJPY15M. The fee formula itself is not covered by this research and must be applied before sizing a $0.25 test.

Subaccount ordering. Create Subaccount needs the Advanced tier, and Advanced needs 'at least 1 of the user's last 100 Predictions orders was created via API'. So the first live order must come from a full-access key on the primary account. Subaccounts are API-only. CreateSubaccountRequest exchange_index 'Defaults to 0 if unspecified', so for KXBTC15M first move cash to shard 2, then create the subaccount there. Subaccount transfers use amount_cents, and retrying with the same client_transfer_id returns 409.

Reconciliation horizon. Canceled or executed orders from before the historical cutoff appear only in GET /historical/orders, and orders_updated_ts 'sits two weeks before the present' (Sep 24, 2026). GET /portfolio/positions returns unsettled positions by default; use settlement_status=settled or all (added Oct 1, 2026), then /historical/positions.

Shard status and clock. exchange_index_statuses is 'Absent when the per-index breakdown is unavailable', and the top-level flags 'reflect the default exchange index (0)', so treat a missing shard-2 status as not tradable. The allowed clock skew on the REST and WS signed timestamp is undocumented (FIX rejects SendingTime more than 30 s off), so keep the clock NTP-synced and stop trading on 401s.
